Unfortunately while I wanted to give this game a chance, for the $15.00 price tag it genuinely wasn't worth it to me. I've played plenty of other games around the same price and received significantly more content, that is much more polished. Perhaps it's unethical to compare other games with this, but I feel like it's reasonable to do that;
Here's WHY I don't recommend you buy this game.
I know I said the tutorial above was simple, which it was, I have a complaint. While the tutorial was explaining what to do, the monsters in the game continued to move, this really annoyed me because I ended up losing that round because I was trying to read and understand what I was doing, I don't know why but it really rubbed me the wrong way. The other thing that really bothered me was the dialogue popups for the tutorial. They literally come up right in the middle of the screen and they overlap buttons, creatures, everything. I feel like the placement is really invasive, and even after I thought I completed the tutorial, the game was still 'barking orders' and holding my hand through a couple missions. It really bothered me, I just wanted to play at that point but I had to deal with random popups
While the talents that were available were kinda cool, there was like 8 of them per character. I was really concerned with this because I knew that once I max out those talents there's not really much more progression beyond that aside from augmenting and improving my weapons, which might be enough for some people, but I really look for more of that end game content early on because for me it's something to set goals for, and I didn't feel like I could keep myself hooked on talents and weapon upgrades alone
To be honest, the initial maps while being very visually appealing, are extremely short in length, I'm sure they get longer as you progress through the game; however because of the short length, the poor balancing became extremely noticeable. Even after completing the tutorial the next 1 or 2 missions right after that were relatively difficult (Was forced to use 'freeze' powerups) and I almost lost some lives because of some enemies being too powerful. I understand how the game works with some heroes being stronger to certain enemy types, and I assure you with the utmost confidence that I do/did understand how the mechanics worked and that it wasn't a personal struggle causing me to have difficulty killing creatures. The poor balancing was obvious
This was what did it for me, I really wanted to give this game a chance, I thought maybe, you know for $15.00 I could live with minimal talents, having some weapons upgrades, etc. everything else wasn't a huge concern. But upon entering into the game in the top right corner I noticed the little Gem icon, and a little 'uh oh' went off in my head.
Upon entering the weapons shop, I discovered, to my dismay, that they allowed people to purchase what appeared to be 'legendary' (Orange) weapons augments for 500 Gems/Diamonds, and also in order to upgrade your weapon with diamonds. Being that this game offers Co-Op, PVP, and Ranked matches, I figure this will give players an unreasonably fair advantage over other players that do not intend to purchase Gems/Diamonds.
; everything but the microtransactions wasn't too awful, and I could see why some people may like this game. However I do feel that the game was poorly balanced to give players more incentive to purchase diamonds to augment and enhance their character.
Personally, I cannot support a developer that charges $15.00 for a game that allows you to purchase and upgrade/enhance your equipment with gems. I totally wouldn't care or even make a big deal about it if it were cosmetics, but we are talking about the potential for giving one player an advantage over another. If I spent $100.00 in gems, it wouldn't be fair to Billy Joe Bob from Arkansas who didn't buy any gems at all. I've come to expect gear enhancing microtransactions from free games, or even cosmetic microtransactions from purchased games; however when a game that you purchased supports gear enhancing microtransactions. I cannot, and will not stand behind it or it's developers.
I'm not some guy who doesn't support developers at all, I understand there are costs for server maintenance, etc. But there are BETTER types of microtransactions to add to your game to generate revenue, but to allow players to gain an advantage over one another based upon who has the bigger pocketbook, in my eyes, extremely unethical; to be honest I'm a tad shocked that nobody else who has reviewed the product has taken issue with this.
_______________________________

Whether or not you get it it is up to you, but as stated initially in this review, I personally wouldn't recommend this game to ANYONE for the reasons listed above.

To be honest, I was not quite sure whether to pick this game up a while back. Ive allready played through multiple open world games set in todays era (you know which ones I mean), but something told me that this one would be different. And yes, I gladly confess that it is :) Its more compact, meaning a smaller world, but that does not equate to less things to do. On the contrary, I found the side content quite entertaining and much less repetitive than in other titles of this sort.
- Story: focused, intense, believable, basically enthralling from start to finish. Two thumbs up!
- Graphics: Pretty damn sweet, I especially appreciated the 3D depth option (I want more of this !) and always present antialising. Character models and rain-in-game are very nicely done, again two thumbs up!
- Sound: very good as well, I loved the cantonese inclusion, plus the local music. Hiphop beats while riding full speed on a highway in rain? Hell yeah!!
- Controls: Not bad, vehicle control was very smooth, in comparison to other titles of this genre. On foot..meh..At times I wanted to punch the air, and that was while playing WITH a controller. But not anywhere catastrophic, mind you.
Overall, you cant really miss with this game. Provided that you do NOT own the original version, this is basically a no - brainer. The setting is great, fresh, voice acting and overall story as well, tons of things to do...For me, personally, the game felt like a Romeo Must Die spin on top of old Hong Kong police flicks from the 80s and 90s..And for that, I applaud the creators. You deserve it !
If you wanna experience Hong Kong without going to Hong Kong. This is the game for you... Nostalgic AF

Tomb Raider has always been one of my favourite game series'. I first joined the series when I was five or so and AoD had just been released. Despite that game being considered a low point in the series I loved it. To me there was something about Lara, something about her adventures and the history mixed with mythology that made them unique.
Tomb Raider II was, and still is I might add, considered a high point for the series. Not only due to the commercial success it experienced almost twenty years ago but because of everything about it. The game was in 3d which at the time was not really a thing, save for Mario 64, and not only that but it feautured an awesome protagonist, an awesome story and very good graphics for the time. Sure it may not hold up today but it is definitely a game worth revisiting for long time fans of the series or a game worth discovering for people who were drawn in due to the 2013 reboot of the series.
The plot follows Lara one year after the first game as she seacrhes for an ancient Chinese dagger said to possess the powers of a dragon to whomever plunges it into their chest. This search takes her all over the world, from China to Venice and beyond. Along the way you will experience fun, and sometimes challenging, platforming, fight all sorts of enemies from feeble spiders to mythalogical monsters. If you don't want to follow the main story right away or you maybe want a refresher course in the controls you can always visit Laras home: Croft Manor. It features an assault course, a hedge maze, various rooms and you can lock her butler Winston in the fridge so, you know, the usual for the classic tomb raider games.
Whether you are new to the series or are revisiting it, this is definitely a game worth buying and really what do you have to lose? It's very cheap on steam and virtually everywhere else. However, I must say that it does take a while to get back into the controls which are a little clucky by modern standards but once you do it fits like an old glove.

This game is my CHILDHOOD!! This game is definitely one of the best games on the Playstation, alongside the first game. Since it has been a long time since I've ever played it (on PC), I had to get used to the controls and they got a little hard to get used to, but if you use a controller, then it's a BLAST! I do have some cons, but it's on the list below,
~~~PROS~~~
-Great level design
-An outstanding soundtrack that fits Lara Croft
-Interesting Puzzles
-Great improvement from having cheap weapons (in the 1st) to having multiple weapons that are usable for most occasions, (Like using the Harpoon Gun underwater, which is a pretty impressive Improvement if you ask me.)
-Flares (First Tomb Raider to have Flares)
-The compass is replaced with a Status thing? (Really, That compass from the 1st game was absolutely useless.)
-More cutscenes (Instead of having a cutscene at the end of the last level in the specific area.)
-Most classic ending scene. (Everyone knows what I mean.)
~~~CONS~~~
-A kinda cliche story (The bad guy scares you then doesn't really appear until the end.)
-This game has the least amount of bosses! (A total of 6! It's 4 if you don't count the T-Rex's that contain the Gold Dragon in the first level. And I did count the Double Pistol goonies in Opera House and Home Sweet Home.)
-You can't change Screen Resolution (In the PC port.)
-The only hard boss was the final boss, ("Whoever" the Dragon.)
-The classic 'I STEAL YOUR WEAPONS ♥♥♥♥♥!!' level. (Luckily, you keep your ammo, flares, and Health packs for some reason...)
-Water Levels (Use that Harpoon Gun to your advantage, PLEASE!!)
-Nude Code's existence (I love Core & Eidos adding that hilarious code, Every fan knows what I'm talking about.)
-Hair Logic (Lara's hair flies all over the place e.e)
-Stone Warriors Spear ones. (I hate these damn enemies so much... they are the killer of my nightmares.)
This is the end of my review, I would definitely start the Series with this game if you're new to it. Rating would be... 8.5/10.

Why?
- Amazing and awesome levels,
- VARIOUS levels,
- amazing story,
- first animated hair and first mobile source of light (flares),
- many cool ideas packed into those levels,
- very nice FMVs (movie clips with hi-poly models),
- many cut-scenes,
- amazing music, some those memorable notes which defined TR music,
- a big training map (house & garden) available anytime,
- an old servant thanks to who Lara was never thirsty (unless frozen :>),
- first usable vehicles (boat & snowmobile),
- various enemies (human, animals, fantasy creatures) with various weapons,
- those moments when the music changed and you discovered new part of the map and you said "WOW!",
- those some moments when you was going to s##t your pants (remember those loud howls&roars chasing you in the winter level?),
- some nice FANTASY included (the dragon story, the Floating Islands map)...
I simply love that part!
Level sizes are JUST RIGHT in that part and they found a golden mean between the fight and the exploration!
And an important thing many kids forget about. Expensive computers in that era were only capable to play (NOT encode) two MP3 320kbit/s files in realtime and do nothing more. And TR2 creators did such a great 3D game with audio for those computers and overcame those limitations...
I believe it was still the moment when great ideas were involved to make the game even more fun!
I bought mine game with the TR Collection and I am satisfied.
There is a level editor (TRLE) for TR2, available for free! There are many fan-made custom levels for TR2! Those levels are often provided as a full games ready-to-run, but when installing those maps into the Steam game you will get the TR2 music.
For Geeks: You can also use the fly-patch as it is compatible with the Steam version and is NOT compatible with the version provided with many custom levels. The fly-patch does NOT mess multiplayer experience as there are no multiplayer in TR2, but this is an unnoficial cheating hack and use it only at your own risk. It may break the gameplay experience and I do not recommend it unless you already did the whole game. You can also find 16:9, 16:10 and 5:4 widescreen support patch. Use only trusted sources and scan patcher files for malware before launching them!

Papers, Please!
Papers, Please is a fantastic game where you, the player, assume the role of an immigrations officer where as you decide who may or may not enter Arstotzka. Arstotzka is a fictional country bearing a resemblance to the former soviet union before its collapse on December 26th of 1991. As the game starts it's very simple and straightforward, and as you would expect as the game progresses it become more challenging. However there's a catch, you're not just stamping passports without a goal, mind you! Every person you process correctly gains you an income, this income is then put towards maintaining your family's well being and as well as upgrading your workstation to improve efficiency. Papers, Please also has a compelling story that's choice based and is definitely worth replays to experience each choices effects.
Overall this game is designed to challenge you. You need to know how to maintain a level head when faced with a stressful work environment, however that being said it's not rage inducing at all. The one thing to consider is that each day in the game will timed, but fair. The other major reason I love this game is that it makes you pay attention to detail and if you have a keen eye it can be quite satisfying to spot forged documentation.
While I never like to give a game a score I must say that it’s looking like a 9/10 for me, and the reason I never like giving scores is because the game is only as good as what you put into the game.

As someone who has actually sunken 737hrs into this game in total since the Beta (before it moved onto steam) I can say that I had a solid addiction to this game to the point that when I needed to stay up for my dissertation I used this for breaks to keep me awake.
Positives
- Third Person - You feel so much more in the action in third person. Knowing if you're not looking the right way you could be ganked at any point makes you so much more wary of your surroundings and I'll be the first to admit stalking someone in the jungle or being made jump when someone leaps over a wall.
- Plenty of variety. I joined when there were 40 gods and even then I never felt starved for choice. Each character has a variety of unique moves not to mention your build can have a huge effect.
- Mythology - Sad as it is I've always loved mythology so to me this was so unique.
- Updates and Events - There are so many events and updates that whenever I felt comfortable with all the gods a new one would be on the way.
- Esports - I love the smite championships so much and the commentary is amazing so if thats your thing its a great watch. I did have a game where I ended up against one of the runners up to the championship and its fair to say we were absolutely brutalised but it was such a good match all the same.
- You don't have to pay for anything unless you want to. The game is completely free to play to the point that if you desperately want a gem based skin you can save up on event weekends, get free chests in events or even save up points Raptr and exchange them. It's 100% possible to unlock all the gods just through time and effort. Plus the rotating gods let you have a chance to try before you buy.
Negatives
- Toxic Community - Don't get me wrong I've met some really good friends on smite but there are probably 50 bad interactions to every good one. There are so many people that will rage at people and spam abuse, blaming their entire team for their stupidity or sulking and staying afking when they can't get the god they want and it has ruined so many games that would have been amazing.
- Some iffy updates - This is a minimal problem but occassionally in the past I will have an update that will completely cripple my game BUT I will give 100% credit that usually it will take a maximum of 2 weeks for a patch to be out that completely solves the issue.
- The navigation after the Xbox release - The menu is a bit counterintuitive for PC but this all happened when they announced the Xbox release so it makes sense that they made it more accessible to Xbox but it can be so frustrating on PC (chance are I'm just frustrated as I know how much better it was before)
I haven't played in some time (I had to cut myself for a while) but I will always think incredibly fondly of Smite and some of the amazing games I've played. It's always a game I keep thinking about coming back to so if you're into Mythology or just want a MMOBA that you can play in third person its definately worth trying.

Community is non-friendly (for me at least)if you are a newbie, experienced player will most likely blame you for their losing. Been to 3 games, not an expert in this game yet, and we lose, then you can smell the saltiness from far, coming out from an expert.

Been playing Smite since it's open beta release. Since then tons of free content has been added; graphical overhauls, new gods (playable characters), gamemodes and more. It allows for both casual and competitive play for players of many different skill levels. But as with any MOBA, you will run into the occasional toxic player that will blame you for everything and be nothing but a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥
It's third person view makes it a very fun game to play for people who feel more comfortable with a more character centered view, compared to other MOBAs which utilize and overhead perspective. And it's heavy reliance on reaction time and skillshots makes it a very fun game to play, especially when you make a crazy enemy prediction and land that huge damage ultimate! This also means there's a huge skill gap between new players and veterans.
Seconded only to Dota 2, this game in my honest opinion has the most fair FTP model. As with many others, a few characters are available to play forever from the beginning, with rotations every week. You can then unlock gods you like using in-game currency unlocked through play. However, you can also for a one time fee unlock every single god available now and in the future, instead of only being able to purchase one or two at a time.
The game is full of small micro-transactions; skins, voice packs and other cosmetics. Nothing purchased with real money will give you an advantage over another player (maybe except for one god being favored over another in some 1v1 matchups), which is a huge plus! Recently a lot of the minor cosmetics (voice packs, announcers, some skins and more) have become unlock-able through random chests you earn for every victory (4 free chests every week). Meaning now you unlock tons of more free stuff without paying a dime!

What's even better is when you die, you lose one of your weapon abilities - and should you have had combined an attack using more than one ability - then they are gone too. and is still one of the most audio-engaging games i've ever played to date, maybe only rivaled by Audio surf.
Words can't even describe how utterly beautiful and magnificient this game is. This game is artistically a treat to your eyes. Seriously, sometimes just take a moment to "take it all in' This is a game meant to be a visual spectacle, and it clearly wants you to take a moment to look at it.  If we really judged games by aesthetics alone, then it easily earns a solid 10/10 for it's unique "Interactable Painting"-Esque world that just oozes style and personality like it's distance cousin: Bastion.
However, in a world where we judge a game by multiple factors, I will give it a fair review.
This easily earns a solid 10/10 for it's art style.
Gameplay can be jagged sometimes, as there's ever only three real stages of the combat:
1. Plotting your Turn()
2. Fleeing from enemies during Turn() Recovery.
3. Psuedo-Combat in realtime, in which most enemies outright dodge your attacks unless you carefully plan.
However, it's still engaging. The sheer amount of customizations done with your functions, and all the nifty and unique combinations that can be made from them is absoloutely stellar, and provides a deep "Play how you want to play" feeling to the game.
The difficulty can be artificially tweaked by enabling "Limiters" which power up the enemies in exchange for more EXP. It's worth it, for the most part. However by late game some of the Limiter's are fairly hard to keep up with, so be careful.
So as as such, the combat earns a 8.5/10, with a bit of room for improvement, mostly on some of the odd-looking animations that accompany Red's moves, and a lack of real in-between for the Turn() Planning period.
The Story of the game is told through the functions you find, whether they be extracted from the data of people, or enemies you defeat, reading is essential. There is a post about the story of Transistor, and it is a decent story filled with some intrigue and computer-geek jokes that some people might not catch unless they're pretty saavy in the computer sciences.
Lastly, and probably the second most important part of this game I feel, is the BGM.
Oh lordy, probably my favorite part of this game, the OST is hands down one of the most ear-pleasing experiences known to man.
It's hard to argue that this game doesn't just compell you to listen to the BGM, you grow an utter appreciation for the atmosphere it creates. The best part of the game is when you learn to simply "Hum" with Red by holding Tab. Try it out! Once you learn how to Flourish, you also learn how to Hum.
I'd say I spent many a 20 minutes or so simply listening to red "Hum" songs at various points. Absoloutely amazing. Earns an easy 9.5/10, only deducting .5 because you aren't given the ability to "Hum' at the very start of the game.
With that said, I'd say the game comes out to be a pretty solid
with a definite "Recommend This Game" from me.

To be honest, I was not quite sure whether to pick this game up a while back. Ive allready played through multiple open world games set in todays era (you know which ones I mean), but something told me that this one would be different. And yes, I gladly confess that it is :) Its more compact, meaning a smaller world, but that does not equate to less things to do. On the contrary, I found the side content quite entertaining and much less repetitive than in other titles of this sort.
- Story: focused, intense, believable, basically enthralling from start to finish. Two thumbs up!
- Graphics: Pretty damn sweet, I especially appreciated the 3D depth option (I want more of this !) and always present antialising. Character models and rain-in-game are very nicely done, again two thumbs up!
- Sound: very good as well, I loved the cantonese inclusion, plus the local music. Hiphop beats while riding full speed on a highway in rain? Hell yeah!!
- Controls: Not bad, vehicle control was very smooth, in comparison to other titles of this genre. On foot..meh..At times I wanted to punch the air, and that was while playing WITH a controller. But not anywhere catastrophic, mind you.
Overall, you cant really miss with this game. Provided that you do NOT own the original version, this is basically a no - brainer. The setting is great, fresh, voice acting and overall story as well, tons of things to do...For me, personally, the game felt like a Romeo Must Die spin on top of old Hong Kong police flicks from the 80s and 90s..And for that, I applaud the creators. You deserve it !

To do so, you must morph and migrate the disease to fit within the different climates on Earth. If your disease becomes popular enough, the local governments try to cure it. While the premise the promising, the fact is the huge difficulty complete eliminates all chance of repeatability. You could go lethal too soon, not infecting enough population and lose. You can become too lethal too soon, the governments will find out about your disease and will cure your disease before you had a chance to either infect or eradicate the world's population. Overall, I would suggest you do not even spend your money on this simulator. In it's beta stages, it needs some fine ironing to do, and requires significant balancing before it goes out of beta. Right now, I cannot recommend this game.

Enjoyed the game overall but I would probably only recommend it on sale because of lack of replayability.  There were  also some nuisances regarding:
-how precisely the mouse sometimes needed to be manipulated (which I understand probably isn't a problem for most people, but was sometimes rather irritating)
-a puzzle piece being triggered prematurely in either Chapter 3 or 4 which required an item that I didn't have, so I knew I could'nt have possibly triggered it by accident (which might not have
the stage per se, but definitely confused me enough regarding my next step that I reset the chapter. Hints would have probably sorted me out quickly, but I wasn't using them, trying to prolong a  game that most reviewers spent a short time on and which I didn't expect to have much replay value. I haven't investigated the bug yet, or whether the chapter can be completed after triggering it--so maybe there's some replayability there after all?).
The most challenging parts felt like they were caused by my having to exactly position the POV to see points of interaction, which was a bit of a pain since it didn't feel like part of a logic puzzle and more like a set of mouse-manipulation exercises. The puzzles themselves were satisfying to solve while perhaps being a bit on the easy side--the challenge is in finding pieces/puzzles rather than the actual solving, since everything you need to know is in the chapter.

This is everything a puzzle game should be - the 3D interface is smooth and responsive, the puzzles make logical sense and are challenging without being too abstract or obtuse (plus there's an effective built-in hint system if you need it), and the supernatural plot framing everything is compelling and interesting, and adds a sense of mystery and intrique to what you're doing. It plays like a room escape game but in reverse - this time you're trying to break into something rather than out of it. It's short but perfectly made, and I am definitely awaiting the continuation of the series on PC.

Papers, Please!
Papers, Please is a fantastic game where you, the player, assume the role of an immigrations officer where as you decide who may or may not enter Arstotzka. Arstotzka is a fictional country bearing a resemblance to the former soviet union before its collapse on December 26th of 1991. As the game starts it's very simple and straightforward, and as you would expect as the game progresses it become more challenging. However there's a catch, you're not just stamping passports without a goal, mind you! Every person you process correctly gains you an income, this income is then put towards maintaining your family's well being and as well as upgrading your workstation to improve efficiency. Papers, Please also has a compelling story that's choice based and is definitely worth replays to experience each choices effects.
Overall this game is designed to challenge you. You need to know how to maintain a level head when faced with a stressful work environment, however that being said it's not rage inducing at all. The one thing to consider is that each day in the game will timed, but fair. The other major reason I love this game is that it makes you pay attention to detail and if you have a keen eye it can be quite satisfying to spot forged documentation.
While I never like to give a game a score I must say that it’s looking like a 9/10 for me, and the reason I never like giving scores is because the game is only as good as what you put into the game.

Seconded only to Dota 2, this game in my honest opinion has the most fair FTP model. As with many others, a few characters are available to play forever from the beginning, with rotations every week. You can then unlock gods you like using in-game currency unlocked through play. However, you can also for a one time fee unlock every single god available now and in the future, instead of only being able to purchase one or two at a time.
The game is full of small micro-transactions; skins, voice packs and other cosmetics. Nothing purchased with real money will give you an advantage over another player (maybe except for one god being favored over another in some 1v1 matchups), which is a huge plus! Recently a lot of the minor cosmetics (voice packs, announcers, some skins and more) have become unlock-able through random chests you earn for every victory (4 free chests every week). Meaning now you unlock tons of more free stuff without paying a dime!

Hero Defense - Haunted Island is a tower defense with a different twist on it: you don't use actual towers, you control them in the form of heroes, while far from being the first in the genre, it is the first time I've played a game where you can have control up to five different characters at the same time and are free to move them as you like.
If you're here looking for an opinion on the co-op or PvP mode then move along. You won't find it here since I still didn't have the chance to play them (and I'm not keen on the idea of playing PvP anyway).
Call it whatever you want, but having control over your towers/heroes is nice and refreshing, I know people that never got into tower defense genre as - in their own words - "you just click and watch" (although personally that is one of the reasons I like it).
Hero Defense has only five heroes, but they are unique on their own way and each one has defining traits and weak points which you'll have to work with in order to win.
The controls are simple enough: 1 to 5 selects the hero, left-click moves them and Space will level them up if you have enough orbs. The game keeps it clean and simple as it should be.
Of course if these controls are not to your liking you can reassign them.
Everything starts simple enough: pay gold (gems for one building) and get a permanent bonus.
But as you may already be thinking: Grinding? Yes. Read below.
This is what could be the ugly part for me. Grinding is a VERY delicate balance that either makes a game good and tolerable or downright insufferable. And I personally can be very much fickle about this as well.
Hero Defense does it… Mildly right. While the beginning will certainly be bumpy and hard, the game has a nice, and may I add cathartic, surprise later on that will tell the difficulty of grinding to go suck a big one. But it's there merely to help you as town and weapon upgrades will get ridiculously expensive.
Every hero has its skill tree which will define their own style. Most of them are clear cut on what the hero does: focus on a single target, deals with crowds and so on.
For those who played games which give you tons of skills and makes you pull your hair just thinking what to do, what skills to leave behind, Hero Defense allows you to have all skills at once.
However you'll have to grind and level up your heroes accordingly. Some will love this, others will not. This left a mixed taste in my mouth; as in initially sweet but sour aftertaste. Why? While I do love having everything, it takes away some potential unique builds that would give characters even more distinction.
There's the usual tower defense: you get resources to start, put a hero, kill enemies, get money, level up your heroes, put another hero... Nothing out of the usual.
What makes it unique then?
Runes does.
Runes are how you make each hero unique on their own even with their skill tress. You can give runes to turn a mild damaging hero into something powerful, or give an attack speed rune to that slow attacking hero and watch them fill the screen with attacks.
Runes are scaled as this: Common - Uncommon - Rare - Epic. As you can imagine Epic runes will take the longest to get as they are fairly expensive, but at least you are granted to get one, but you'll still need to luck out to get the one you want (power up, speed up, extra projectile chance…).
The game has a simple craft system defined as "Merge" which allows you swap lower rarity runes into better quality ones. Use all of the same type and it'll ensure you a better rarity rune of that type. If you don't, you'll need luck as the result will be random.
Hero Defense may not receive a ton of awards, but it sure does try hard and the efforts of the team behind it clearly show. But the game, like 100% of everything out there, has its share of problems.
1) The loading time to use the Town is unacceptable. It is far too long and wears down on the player really fast.
2) Hero AI can be random or downright stupid at times. They tend to focus on enemies in the middle instead of the last in the group. While manual targeting DOES help, options of automatic targeting (most health, etc.) would be greatly appreciated.
3) Shrines costs gem. No problem. Shrines are permanent until you build something on them. No problem. Shrine cost increases with each one you build. No problem. The game doesn't keep track where you built shrines.
4) This is a very little something but bugs me to no end: whenever you finish a map with a victory there's no Restart button. Sounds like nitpicking, but this is a game about farming to a certain degree and having to go back to the World Map to choose the map you want again gets tiresome.
5.1) The game has only five types of enemies and while they try to be distinct from each other they always feel "samey" when you reach higher levels. Since every enemy can have about every ability (with some exceptions), the only thing you'll end worrying about in most cases is which hero should fight which enemy.
5.2) Enemy abilities feel uninspired as they only affect themselves, enemies will never actively hamper your heroes' progress. Enemies could have other things like swapping heroes' position, swapping one hero for another, blocking one hero, reducing their range or attack speed, punishing players for clustering heroes too much or leaving them too far from each other…
6.1) Another complaint is the lack of runes that can give unique effects like Poisoning enemies, slowing them and similar effects to somewhat emulate other characters.
6.2) Lack of variety in weapons. While rune slot upgrades are good it'd give much more character definition having equipable weapons that increases their attack rate, attack strength or range.
7) And this feels more like nitpicking from me, but the game gets
you get everything; town upgrades, powerful Epic runes, and weapons maxed. While it does feel immensely good crush Insane difficulty levels that were getting under your skin, that also loses its charm fast. And no, Endless is not a solution for this, Survival Mode in tower defenses never felt accomplishing or anything since, you know, they don't have end. Maybe a fifth difficulty could solve this.
8) Camera control. You don't have free control of your camera and more often than not you can end up having an obstacle obstructing your view which may cause anything from an annoyance to costing you the entire map.
Hero Defense - Haunted Island is a hidden gem that is still being polished by Happy Tuesday even after taking off its Early Access status, but it's far from being bad, broken or unplayable. As I've just noted, this game has its issues, feels like it still has a lot of potential, but it's very well worth playing.
In the end its lack of diversity of enemies, runes and weapons can make the game feel repetitive for some people, but Hero Defense - Haunted Island was charming enough to keep me captive for good 55 hours (as of this writing). And that's not counting the co-op mode which I haven't tested yet.
Knowing Happy Tuesday is still working and releasing patches on *drums rolls* Tuesdays to address known issues and seeing that they at least care enough to ask and answer people in their Community Hub is another good thing I want to point. If you have the chance, give Hero Defense a try.

On the game:
Great addition to the True Crime series. For those of you guys who don't know, this game was/is [originally] True Crime: Hong Kong. Due to the inadquate sales of True Crime: New York City, Activision didn't wanna follow through publishing this game after it had been in development for 3 years. It was then picked back up by Square Enix, thankfully. And as of december 2014 of last year, Activision apparrently left the True Crime trademark abandoned. So if there's a Sleeping Dogs 2, it might just be True Crime [whatever] if Square Enix feels like registering it. Unless everyone's happy with "Sleeping Dogs". lol.
Gameplay:
The game has great emphasis on combat. This is what the first game was known for. That, and the alternate mission pathways and varied directions in story the player had access to. This game is more linear, story/gameplay-wise, but everything else in it is what you'd find in a True Crime game. The slow-mo, the combat(which has been expanded upon with environmental interactions and takedowns, like putting an enemie's head between a car's inside and it's door and slaming the door shut on it 'till he passes out or bleeds/dies), the ability upgrade system, and the detail in the worldspace. With a little more. Can't say much for firearms yet, because I haven't gotten far enough in the game to have access to all of them yet. Just a pistol, smg, and a shotgun. And a cover system to be used with them, along with it's own forms of interaction. Movement is great, like when chasing down a thug and free-running. Driving works well.
Graphics:
They're beautiful. They're not as good as Watch Dogs, but they're great on their own. Hong Kong is colorful, lighting is great, and textures and models are revised for the definitive edition. Many(kinda) graphics settings are available to tweak. Don't like that the ambient occlusion and anti-aliasing(if no other method of standard/advanced AA is being used, FXAA) are hardcoded, but you can just turn them down to their lowest qualities for more FPS. Animations are also great. Weather effects, like when it rains, look great. Water isn't Watch Dogs', but it's good. Still some low-res textures that Watch Dogs doesn't have, though. I'm a graphics wh_re. :)
Hmm. But no FOV slider, though. Supposedly a higher fov angle than the standard edition's, but it's still tight for me. 'cause I get motion sickness.
Soundtrack and audio:
Some stuff is good. The voice acting performances are good. Obviously the main characters' are best. Music is great, as it should be for this kind of game.
Performance:
I've seen many people complaining about the performance of this Definitive Edition, as they say the regular version played fine. IDK, but I'm not getting their issues.
These are my specs..
GPU - HD 6950 1GB - latest drivers in use
CPU - i5 2500K, @ 3.30GHZ
RAM - 8GB, 1600MHZ
Running with all graphics settings at max, except I turned AA and AO down to their lowest qualities.
No stuttering, no bad frame dropping, no nothing. For me, this is like the 2nd-best optimized open-world game like it since Saints Row 3. It just seems that stable. Load fasts, menu's are very responsive, graphics settings enable quickly. No alt-tab issues. Nada. Controls are responsive for everything, overall. Better than Watch Dogs, :P

... What can be said about Rock of Ages?
If I could describe this game in one word, it would be "silly". In the next few lines, you'll understand why.
The plot/concept of this game is a unique take on the famous Greek myth of Sisyphus, a man condemned to Tartarus and punished to roll a boulder up a hill that keeps rolling back down for all eternity. In this game, Sisyphus has had enough, and uses his accursed boulder to escape and flatten all of time itself. From then on, it becomes a cross between a Ski-Ball game and a Tower Defense, in which you are sent to different courses modeled after different historical figures and are challenged to squish them. Gameplay is divided between two turns: Construction and Rolling. During the Construction phase, you can put up obstacles with earned points to slow down and impede your opponent's boulder, by either blocking the way or knocking them off course. Rolling Phase has you roll your boulder down the opponent's course (which has also been furnished with defenses), and break down the doors to squish your opponent.
Like I said. Silly.
Sure, this game can get repetitive at times, but it's still a fun little bit of weirdness to lighten up your day. Plus, every level begins and ends with 'Dies Irae' and 'Ode to Joy'. It's quirky good fun, and a fun challenge to boot. I give this game a 7/10 recommendation, just for some jolly good fun. Besides: where else can you crush Leonardo Da Vinci with a smiling boulder?

Life isn't fair, and neither is Eryi's Action. This game is a pretty, stylistic, precision-controlled, fiendishly difficult platformer. At first glance it looks and plays like an anime Mario Bros, but a few minutes' gameplay will dispel that idea. Eryi's Action throws a variety of clever and/or cheap traps at you, For instance, in many places, the ground will just drop out from underneth you, sending you to your death. In other places an enemy might drop out randomly from the sky at an inoppotune time, or spikes might shoot up out of a pit while you're jumping across. Anything easy is likely to be a trap, and, after a while, you'll start anticipating some of the traps.
There's a true beauty to the gameplay here, Eryi's Action establishes early on that the game is not fair, nor does it intend to be. If you can tolerate and embrace this mindset, and if you don't mind dying literally hundreds of times, then you'll enjoy the game. Eryi's Action is beautifully made, the platforming is precise, the graphics are lovely, and the game features not just platforming, but some flying/shooting sections, swimming, a clever RPG-style boss fight, and some very clever physics puzzles. All of it is brutally difficult, it's a match of wits between the programmer and yourself, a battle against unfair odds. It's a true gem, if only for the most hardcore of gamers.

Lara Croft is searching for an artifact called the Dagger of Xian but discovers that a mysterious organization is also tracking it. If she wants to be the first to reach it and prevent a catastrophic fate for the world, she will need to find the keys that will open the way... elsewhere than in China.
I must say that Tomb Raider II isn't perhaps my favorite game in the series, as I'm heavily influenced by the first opus and Anniversary. But the story is well written too. I mean, who doesn't want to follow her under the water or in Italy or in Tibet?
The gameplay is pretty much the same as the first game: you jump, you search levers, you move stuff and you shoot anything coming in your way. And Tomb Raider II has a major shift here: instead of the animals or the legendary creatures, your enemies are now humans. Many humans. Many crazy humans. And you're confronted to them more than the animals (true, you have sharks, dogs, even Yetis or spiders). I suppose that maybe, this shift may have contributed to the fact that I'm still clinging more to the first game.
But this game is also introducting vehicles for Lara: boat (well in Venice) and the snow bike which I had the most fun with. This is great to take ramps, to jump over pits or to race against the clock. That's also one of the main changes. Another new thing is the fact that you have allies in the game in the form of Tibetan monks. Don't hurt them and they'll let you in peace.
Tomb Raider II is also an improvement for Lara herself: she has more weapons (like an harpoon for example) if she needs to defend herself (and trust me, she will need them nearly all the time). But the best improvement is probably aethestic: she's looking more curvy than angular, though she's still wearing her regular outfit.
However, during the game, now, Lara changes also clothes. While the change is perhaps minimal, it's more realistic for the levels. It's just a little disappointing that she must find her way on a platform in the middle of the sea, where it's very very industrial. But generally, the landscapes are still sticking to the "Tomb Raider", aka, historical places like the Great Wall of China or Venice but also more mysterious levels like a wreck of a cruiser or a Tibetan monastery. It's very nice done and guess what? The T-Rex makes also a cameo.
Anyway, I liked a lot the soundtrack, mainly the one used with the snow bike for the first time.
Tomb Raider II is a nice way to keep going with the series. Too bad, it doesn't come with the add-on The Golden Mask (more snowbiking!) but anyway, if you're nostalgic of putting the butler in the fridge, given the price and the regular promotion of -75%/-80%, you shouldn't hesitate.

"Transistor: a semiconductor device with three connections, capable of amplification in addition to rectification."
The 2nd title from indie developer Supergiant Games, Transistor is a story driven sci-fi action-RPG. Like Supergiant's previous title Bastion, the game is controlled from a 3rd person isometric standpoint.
Transistor takes place in the city of Cloudbank, where every decision is voted on by the people, from the colour of the sky, to building a bridge. Transistor throws the player right into its world, indeed, it begins before you can even open the options menu. The game opens with the protagonist Red, the most famous singer in all of Cloudbank, kneeling beside the body of an unnamed man with the titular Transistor a great big glowing greatsword, buried in his chest. The Transistor has absorbed Red's voice and the mans consciousness, allowing him to speak to the now voiceless Red. Taking the Transistor, Red seeks to to find those who attempted to kill her, a mysterious group known as the Camerata. The Camerata control an army of robot-like creatures, known as the Processes throughout the game, in an attempt to stop Red and regain the Transistor for an yet-unknown purpose. The story is quite mature, requiring the player to pay close attention to the dialogue throughout the game.
Red is an interesting protagonist. Whereas historically the "silent protagonist" has been used as an avatar for players to project themselves on, Red is very much her own character. The player makes choices throughout the game, but Red has her own personality, indeed, she feels like a deconstruction of the silent protagonist trope. The scene where she realises how to communicate with the voice inside the Transistor is a powerful moment. Its the small details that bring Red's character to life. There's even a dedicated hum button, where Red hums along to the music playing in the game.
The narrator in the Transistor, like Rucks in Bastion, serves to drive the narrative forward. For a dead guy, the narrator has a pretty lively personality. He comments on the world, providing insight to the events transpiring, commenting Red's performance during combat. Logan Cunningham once again delivers a fantastic performances, and while it may not be quite as good as his performance in Bastion, the narrator's well written dialogue and exposition brings much life to the game.
Transistor is very much the spiritual successor to Bastion, where many gameplay features present in Bastion have been refined and tweaked in Transistor. Once again, combat is done through the 3rd person isometric point of view. Transistor combat greatly differs from Bastion's with the use of the Transistor. Using a function in the Transistor known as Turn(), combat can be fought through a somewhat turn-based fighting system. Functions, people who have been killed by the Process whose consciousness is absorbed by the Transistor, can be used by the Transistor as either offensive functions, upgrades to functions or passive defence boosts. The combat mechanics is Transistor are surprisingly deep, and it will take a while to get used to. The game encourages and rewards experimenting with different builds, using Functions in different Transistor slots unlock the bio for the character the Function once was. It is a unique way to deliver the lore of the game, and while it may be annoying for some, it is refreshing to see a game using its mechanics to expand the story and world building, rather than through exposition or books found in-game.
Supergiant once again outdo themselves in the art design of Transistor, make a visually stunning world. Just like Bastion and the world of Caelondia, Transistor's city of Cloudbank is one of the most visually stunning games I have ever played. The sci-fi inspired art design is one of the games most impressive features, every scene is masterfully hand drawn and put together, the landscapes are visually breathtaking. Transistor is an absolute delight to look at and play, showing that visual art design can make a game look better than graphically intense games.
Music remains on point, with Darren Korb once again composing the soundtrack. Described as "old-world electronic post-rock," the music is absolutely fantastic. With my personal favourite songs being "Old Friends," "The Spine," "Coasting," "In Circles," "Sandbox," "We All Become," "Impossible," and "We All Become," I can safely say that Transistor's official soundtrack is well worth the purchase.
It is very find to any flaws with Transistor, as the game is so well put together. Game length is fairly short, with a single playthrough only lasting around 6-8 hours, however it does offer New Game+, with the ability to use many new Function's, expanding even further on its combat system. The story at times can be a bit hard to follow, requiring the player to pay close attention to dialogue, information terminals and character bios to learn about the world.
Supergiant Games' Transistor is an absolute masterpiece. Fans of previous work Bastion should absolutely buy Transistor. With a mature narrative, a deep combat system, gorgeous aesthetic and art design, excellent music, and tons of replayability, Transistor is a must buy. One of my favourite games of all time.

Transistor,
Transistor is an enjoyable game with interesting game mechanics, a fantastic soundtrack that fits perfectly to the theme and environment at hand, and also has quite the story (which is quite sad).
I enjoyed playing the game, and I also enjoyed the Combat system with its perks, mixing and matching different abilities, beautiful cyber theme and its difficulty that makes you think twice on your moves you make.
The only part I found annoying was that Royce your lover (The Transistor Sword you wield), is constantly talking and literaly can never shut up for more than 10 seconds, I found him to be a nuisance throughout the game. I would enjoy 30 seconds without him talking to me, although I know Red is a mute, (Story Explains Why), and he basically gives you advice and comfort, but the frequent rate of listening to his voice can get irritating.
The other thing is this game can be quite difficult if you don't have the right mixed and matched perks and abilities, especially for the last boss, so you will find yourself annoyed and frustrated attempting to figure out the right choices for abilities.
The Ending?, well that part I will leave to you, but for me personally it was sad, but at the same time you understand why Red chose this decision, It was beautifully put together, a fantastic tale of Love and Romance.
At the end of the day is it worth its retail value of $22?, absolutely Not. Only buy it on sale (I bought it for $5), You can beat the game in a matter of 5-6 hours, its still an enjoyable and interesting piece of art but definetely not worth its set price, but It's still a notable work of art to add to your collection.

Eryi's Action is the platformer that will appeal to many masochistic or challenge gamers.
This game is effecitvely a puzzle platformer. It's all about memorizing traps and knowing what the traps are, where those traps are, and when they happen.
But in spite of the gameplay is simple and the incredibly bland story which can be summarized in the following three sentences...
"Eryi is a cute fairy who wants to eat a melon. Farta the troll has stolen her melon. Help Eryi get it back!"
The game is amusing and the puzzles are fun to conquer. Eryi's Action certainly isn't lacking in the humor department. It's got a few references to other games and some traps will often leave you laughing as opposed to screaming in frustration.
This game is NOT for simply killing time. You have to push your memory, reactions, and ability to adapt if you want to succeed in this game.
$4.99 is a small price to pay to help little Eryi get her melon back. The game will hurt you. But it hurts so good.
You can tell they spent a lot of time making the traps. More of an anti-game, and definitely not for everyone, but definitely worth picking up during a sale.

Eryi's Action Review
It's no secret that Eryi's Action is a torture platformer, the kind of game that everywhere you step a set of spikes or bombs or enemies or thorny vines and whatnot will pop out and kill you.  Despite the happy and colorful look of this game, it is ruthless and quickly lets you know that it doesn't want you to win.  And while I hate the idea of that and honestly I'm not very good at platformers, I still found Eryi's Action to be fun, and I was able to beat it.
Make no mistake, there were plenty of ragequit moments.  I should point out that there were a few points I had to look up video walkthroughs, such as the RPG part and a few platforming sections.  But eventually if you are just patient enough, you will get through the end of the game.  If you like the evil platformer genre, things like Super Meat Boy and N+, don't hesitate to play Eryi's Action.

Shakes and Fidget is a very fun and compelling game as long as you know what you're getting into. Namely, it's an idle starical free to play RPG. You can go on quests, collect loot, do PVP, and eventually enter dungeons and build a fortress. The game is very light hearted in its writing and humor. It is very much a parody of a lot of modern RPGs, especially World of Warcraft. I like the art style in particular. It's very ... German if that makes any sense.
When you go on a quest, there is a timer that counts down until the quest is completed. And this is where the idle aspect of the game fits in. This is a small game designed to run in the background while you do other things. I usually had my character going on quests in the background while I played WoW and FF14. I honestly have had a lot of fun leveling and gearing my character and pitting her against other people's characters in the arena. And the dungeons are actually tough which is something I kind of miss in modern MMOs! There is a premium currency in the form of mushrooms, but I never felt forced to spend money on any as the game is pretty forgiving in giving you mushrooms as you play, allowing you to go on extra quests or do an extra arena if you so desire. And when you decided you've had enough for the day, you can even assign your character to guard duty so you can continue to earn gold even when you've turned the game off.
Overall, I have had a lot of fun with this game and I highly recommend everyone at least give it a try.

If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

Sleeping Dogs is a crime genre sandbox game, or a "Grand Theft Auto clone" if you prefer. It's different enough in tone and mechanics that I don't feel that label is entirely fair, though.
For a start, Sleeping Dogs is more grounded and 'realistic' than any of the GTA games. It's set in an accurately recreated Hong Kong instead of a fictional city, and rather than the story functioning as a vehicle for satire it's a well crafted tribute to gritty Hong Kong cop movies like Police Story and Hard Boiled.
The melee combat in this game is excellent. It's a lot like Batman Arkham Asylum or Assassin's Creed, but with more varied and fluid moves. Fighting feels fast-paced and brutal - protagonist Wei Shen can break arms and legs and use the environment to kill enemies (nothing like impaling some poor sucker on a fishhook or slamming their head in a car door). Despite the noted rarity of guns in Hong Kong, you'll get into quite a few gunfights as well. The shooting mechanics are solid enough and Max Payne style bullet time when you vault over cover and disarm enemies is very cool. The driving mechanics are the weakest link; lower-level cars have stiff handling and higher-level cars are seriously twitchy. Driving boats is a tremendous chore.
So should you get this game? If you enjoy GTA-like games for the crazy amounts of destruction you can wreak on the streets, then bear in mind Sleeping Dogs is much more subdued - no planes or helicopters, no freely available rocket launchers to use on the police, no jetpacks. But it does have a much stronger and better-paced story than any other crime sandbox game I've played, with a well developed cast of characters and a world that feels real and full of life. Unlike newer GTAs, there are also collectables that give you bonuses, giving you a reason to explore every rooftop and alleyway.
And you can shove a taxi driver in the trunk of his own car, drive toward the ocean and bail. Or dress up like Bruce Lee and beat up huge crowds of triads. Or deliberately screw up karaoke as hard as possible in order to irritate people at a club. So if your taste in video game sociopathy is more subtle, Sleeping Dogs has you covered.

I played this like once like a year ago maybe idk. Either way heres a good recipe for a good Venison Stew.
2 tablespoons canola oil
2 pounds venison stew meat
3 large onions, coarsely chopped
2 garlic cloves, crushed
1 tablespoon Worcestershire sauce
1 bay leaf
1 teaspoon dried oregano
1 tablespoon salt
1 teaspoon pepper
3 cups water
7 potatoes, peeled and quartered
1 pound carrots, cut into 1-inch pieces
1/4 cup all-purpose flour
1/4 cup cold water
Bottled browning sauce, optional
1.  Heat oil in a Dutch oven. Brown meat. Add onions, garlic, Worcestershire sauce, bay leaf, oregano, salt, pepper and water. Simmer, covered, 1-1/2 to 2 hours or until meat is tender.
2.  Add potatoes and carrots. Continue to cook until vegetables are tender, about 30-45 minutes.
3.  Mix flour and cold water; stir into stew. Cook and stir until thickened and bubbly. Add browning sauce if desired. Remove bay leaf. Yield: 8-10 servings

After playing 1000 hours of Reign of Kings, I thought I should say a few things in a review.
There are some aspects to RoK that keep me coming back. For one, I really enjoy the persistence of it, how you can keep working and making progress day after day. Another is the freedom to make your base however you want, with many different building materials and furniture to choose from. You can spend so many hours working on getting your base just the way you want it, one of the things I enjoy most. I don't mind the time consuming farming either, I usually put on some music or an audio book on while I'm out swinging the pickaxe. It feels pretty good once your base is built up to the point that any attacker would have a very hard time making much progress inside. If you happen to be in-game while being sieged, it's an intense experience being on the defensive fighting back, doing things like using your ballista or trebuchet to take out attackers and their siege gear. Unfortunately, you will most likely be offline while being raided.
There are plenty of toxic people that play, but also some great people who you will become close allies with. Playing with friends is a much better experince than going solo.
There are some huge problems with Reign of Kings that are bad enough to ruin the game for most people. Almost everyone will agree the worst problem is the duping/exploits/cheating, whatever you want to call it. After people realized that Codehatch won't be fixing problems or adding content, most of the player-base left the game for good.
EDIT: The duping cheat seems to be wiped out by October's patch.

Plague inc evolved comes from a genre of games dedicated to real time strategy but on an information bases dealing strictly with graphs and interactive maps.
It stems from two free flash games that came out in the early 2000's called Pandemic and Pandemic 2. Plague inc is essentially the same game except presented much better and with far more in depth features that lacked in the flash game.
Plague Inc evolved is simple and easy to navigate. This however does not mean the game is at all easy to beat, it is very challenging and unrelenting in handing you defeats for poor strategy choices. This is a good thing. This isn't a menu game you would find on facebook that rewards you endlessly and gives no consequences for neglectful choices and behaviour. A victory in this game is something that is relished and feels authentic as a seal of approval, proving your strategy works. Its also very realistic (in the default state of the disease only) I find it very enjoyable reading the news headlines and seeing how each nation reacted as new studies and new symptoms of the disease surfaced, The visual cues below showing how much chaos you have wrought on a nation is also very satisfying
My experience in Plague Inc Evolved is a very positive one, I myself have bought this game for a few of my steam friends and they all agree this is a very well made game pointing out the same good qualities that i had mentioned previously. The choices among different plague scenarios and types as well as the ability to tinker the starting genetic make up of your plague can radically change how the game plays out forcing you to adopt a new strategy that was counter productive in a previous version of that same disease.
Visuals are good, the music is great and sets the mood of your nafarious goal quite splendidly. It however relies heavily on imagination playing off the description of symptoms and side effects of combined symptoms. Those that aren't great at visualizing things in their mind probably won't enjoy the game. Those who want live action probably won't enjoy the game. For those who do like using their imagination. You will be pleased when you read that your disease has begun making people defecate themselves in public due to diarrhea and insanity spreading the disease much more quickly. The Types of diseases are quite staggering and they continuously add more all the time so its always going to be fun. The only complaint I have on the level of realism is simply the homogeneous properties of a nation, All of the nation is subject to to certain environmental and cultural effects that simply make no sense to me. Sure China does have the biggest cities out there, but that doesn't mean that the whole country resides in urban areas. If they wanted to improve this, they would change the game from nation initial infection to something that illustrated city to city infection as well as how pervasive the desease spreads through water ways, the wildlife and rural communities more realistically. This would make the game eerily more realistic as well as the amount of information at your disposal require true thought processing and strategic planning. Instead of losing simply because Greenland closed its seaport, You would lose because your pathogen had difficulty traversing cold rural areas due to lack of mutation to infect local wildlife. Untill they implement that, I wouldn't call this game perfect

I bought this on sale and it was easily worth it.  I'd go so far as to say it's worth it at full price (only $1 a chapter, really).  The Room can be beaten in 4-5 hours, but I urge you to take your time and enjoy the atmosphere.
Pros:
- Excellent atmosphere in terms of both visuals and sounds.  The ideal environment for playing is a dimly lit room with headphones.
- The simple game mechanics of being centred on an object and able to interact with selected portions is used to good effect without becoming repetitive.
- The variety of puzzles.
Cons:
- The sequel hook.  While I still enjoyed The Room in and of itself, I would have preferred more closure. Admittedly I look forward to playing the rest of the series.
- The player.  There were two or three puzzles which hand me banging my head against a wall, but the fault was mine.  The Room gives you everything necessary to solve the situation; sometimes all you need is to come at it from a different angle.
*Update 11/25/16: Nominated this game for the The “Game Within A Game” Award.  Considering this game is nothing but puzzles within puzzles within puzzles within puzzles within puzzles, it was an easy choice.

Sleeping Dogs is a crime genre sandbox game, or a "Grand Theft Auto clone" if you prefer. It's different enough in tone and mechanics that I don't feel that label is entirely fair, though.
For a start, Sleeping Dogs is more grounded and 'realistic' than any of the GTA games. It's set in an accurately recreated Hong Kong instead of a fictional city, and rather than the story functioning as a vehicle for satire it's a well crafted tribute to gritty Hong Kong cop movies like Police Story and Hard Boiled.
The melee combat in this game is excellent. It's a lot like Batman Arkham Asylum or Assassin's Creed, but with more varied and fluid moves. Fighting feels fast-paced and brutal - protagonist Wei Shen can break arms and legs and use the environment to kill enemies (nothing like impaling some poor sucker on a fishhook or slamming their head in a car door). Despite the noted rarity of guns in Hong Kong, you'll get into quite a few gunfights as well. The shooting mechanics are solid enough and Max Payne style bullet time when you vault over cover and disarm enemies is very cool. The driving mechanics are the weakest link; lower-level cars have stiff handling and higher-level cars are seriously twitchy. Driving boats is a tremendous chore.
So should you get this game? If you enjoy GTA-like games for the crazy amounts of destruction you can wreak on the streets, then bear in mind Sleeping Dogs is much more subdued - no planes or helicopters, no freely available rocket launchers to use on the police, no jetpacks. But it does have a much stronger and better-paced story than any other crime sandbox game I've played, with a well developed cast of characters and a world that feels real and full of life. Unlike newer GTAs, there are also collectables that give you bonuses, giving you a reason to explore every rooftop and alleyway.
And you can shove a taxi driver in the trunk of his own car, drive toward the ocean and bail. Or dress up like Bruce Lee and beat up huge crowds of triads. Or deliberately screw up karaoke as hard as possible in order to irritate people at a club. So if your taste in video game sociopathy is more subtle, Sleeping Dogs has you covered.

Cerebral Atmospheric Horror
This game is great. Fingerbones tells a story using abstract and broad strokes. One of the greatest elements to a compelling story is not actually showing the audience what has happened, but making the audience paint the details with their imagination. This game does just that. The story, as well as the mood the author wants to evoke in the player is told through notes littered through the game. I can't help but compare this game to Silent Hill - the story is great. Another facet to great cerebral horror is making the player feel uncomfortable - and a really great story is making the player feel and think this after completing the story. Accompanying the game is a great ambient soundtrack.
Pros - Short, simple mechanics. You walk, you left click. Let's not mention the fact that such a great story is FREE (so honestly, all complaints should be rendered nil)
Cons - The solution to certain puzzles may not be too easily deciphered. Nothing a quick trip to the Community Hub can't solve.
Afterword - The story is a bit mature, especially depending on how you perceive it. Again, the narrative lets your mind fill in many of the blanks. Just note that while not necessarily obscene, the subject matter is quite disturbing.
Bottom Line: Play it. Free. Cerebral Atmosperic Horror

1. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F. Spray a 9x9-inch pan with nonstick spray, then line with a strip of parchment paper so that it covers the bottom and comes up two sides of the pan. Spray the parchment with nonstick spray too.
2. In a microwave safe bowl (or in the top of a double boiler or pan set on top of a pan of simmering water), microwave in 30 second bursts to melt butter and chocolate chips together until all is melted and smooth. Whisk in the sugars, then whisk in the eggs, vanilla and salt. Sift flour into the bowl and stir that in too. Scrape the brownie batter into the prepared pan. Bake for 25 to 30 minutes, or until the brownie layer is cooked through (toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean). Place the pan of brownies in the refrigerator to speed up the cooling process (or cool at room temperature and add the cookie dough layer later).
Prepare the cookie dough layer:
3. In a large bowl, use an electric mixer to combine the butter, sugars and salt until soft and creamy (1 to 2 minutes). Mix in the milk and vanilla. Sprinkle in the flour and mix in until combined. Stir in the 1 cup of chocolate chips. Scoop the cookie dough onto the top of the brownies and spread onto the brownie layer. I find that it's easiest to do this if the brownie layer is chilled and firm. Wet your hands or spray them with nonstick spray and pat the cookie dough on top in a even layer. Sprinkle additional chocolate chips on top to create a nicer, visual appearance. For easy, clean cutting, chill the brownies (wrap the brownies with plastic wrap and chill until firm- 1 to 2 hours or up to 2 days).
4. Cut the brownies: Run a knife along the sides of the brownie pan and then use the parchment paper to lift the brownies from the pan and onto a cutting board. Slice the brownies with a sharp knife, wiping the knife with a paper towel between cuts. If you'd like all of your slices of brownies to look clean-cut without edges, use the knife to cut the sides of the brownies off before cutting pieces. Keep brownies slices covered and chilled until ready to serve.

If you are not familiar with the
series of games, then get ready for the best kind of loot, crazy and nearly unlimited gunplay, and a rich detailed trash laden setting with one of the best villains in any game out there.
builds upon the success and lore of its predecessor in major ways.
The main characters in this game are not the star. In fact, much like the first game they are fairly hollow and have no dynamic to the story. Their skills, however, are what makes the game great.  Aside from the massive amount of guns possible, each character has three skills trees that can be leveled up, making each characters experience exponentially different both during the main game, and all subsequent play throughs.
Unlike the first game, there is some real substance to
. It takes the mythology established from the first game and pushes it a little further, with a one of the best villains in any game to date. Handsome Jack has taken control of Pandora via the Hyperion corporation and rules it with an iron fist. He is as charismatic as he is deadly, and he proves to have bite behind his bark. Although the main playable characters in this game are inconsequential to the story, the original four vault hunters and other favorites such as Tannis and Clap Trap from the first game have become fully fleshed out dynamic characters who are integral with the story.
Additionally there are four story-oriented DLCs which add a good amount of story (for the most part) to the base game. The best is definitely
which has some of the best writing in the series, while the others send you to interesting new areas of Pandora in search of glory, loot, and big game.
Probably one of the biggest things in this game is the loot, and more specifically, the weapons. All weapons (as well as shields and grenades) are comprised of different parts from different manufacturers to make up an incalcuable amount of possible combinations. Each manufacturer gives the item different characteristics, making each pickup fairly unique. Additionally, each item has a rarity assigned with matching characteristics including unique weapons with special abilities to make your time on Pandora even more fun.
If you are familiar with the first game, then this one will feel like the most natural of progressions. There are plenty of updates to the original game engine, including a far superior UI that is easy to navigate and include a minimap with easy to locate markers, even more possible gun combinations, an amped up story with DLC campaigns rivaling the base game,  proper play-mode for multiple run-throughs, and character skill trees that make the game even more fun. Overall, there is nothing in
that was not vastly improved in
.
Although there is little to nitpick about this game, one thing that can cause some annoyance is the gun leveling once you get to Ultimate Vault Hunter Mode (UVHM, the third playthrough on a single character). Similar to the original, each weapon has a level, and attributes that match the level. Although the progression through the first two playthroughs is fairly balanced, once you get to UVHM, you will find the need to constantly upgrade your weapons every level or so to take on the UVHM enemies. They are always matching your level (+/- 2 of your level) and usually drop items lower than their level. As such, you will find yourself constantly getting new weapons and even farming certain areas or enemies for special weapons to make the fight easier. Some may even find the item farming fun, as nothing beats killing an enemy and seeing that Orange glow appear over a special weapon.
Something else that might be a problem for some is the sheer amount of "stuff" going on at any one time. With all of the weapons, enemies, particles, backgrounds, and projectiles going on, the screen can become a jumbled mess of color. It can be overwhelming for a new player who might not know what is going on. Once you get through the first couple of crazy fights, it becomes second nature and you start looking forward to those crazy moments where you get back up from a second wind even though you cannot clearly see the enemy.
Overall, this game is for anyone who is looking for a fun and unique bullet-sponge type game, where you will find yourself scouring the land for new loot to have fun with. With a cohesive and engaging story, new and old players of the
series will quickly find themselves right at home with very little to not like.

People told me this game was fun. And it was.
"Rock of Ages" is a half-strategy, half-reflex and speed reliant destruction game, where you build defenses to protect your gate, while also trying to hit your opponent's gate with as much force with your boulder as you can. And it's really fun! The controls are smooth, the level layout accomodates the different strategy and action playstyles, and the enemy AI can be pretty relentless during some levels. It's a nice blend of challenge and fun.
However, there are some problems. While I enjoyed the cutscenes, some of the jokes presented fell flat or got old very fast. Like the girly shrieks your enemy would cry before you'd flatten them. Or the pop-culture jokes that were shoved in here and there. The animation and style are great, but I didn't like the humor that much.
On top of that, while the graphics look fantastic in this game... the color pallette isn't the most spectacular. There's some good crimsons and golds and crimsons and greens for certain levels, but there are some that are really dirty, unpleasant pallettes like blue and gold that just aren't that colorful. But, again, that's my own taste.
And finally, the game can be a little TOO easy sometimes. Some levels I got through in one try, because their structure didn't stump me, but f***ed the living daylights out of the enemy's AI. And the bosses, while creative, are all very simplistic and really REALLY easy. You literally cannot die when fighting a boss, and the structure is find the weak spot then hit it three times.
Despite its flaws, I really enjoyed playing Rock of Ages, and earning what achievements I did. It's addicting fun you can get hooked on for a good weekend or so. And I'm giving Rock of Ages a 7/10.
