CuteFish Review: Longish review, pro/con list, closing thoughts. Just skip ahead if you don't like reading! :3
FFXIV: A Realm Reborn is a game that aimed to polish and refine the 'WoW-era' MMO instead of hamfisting in a slightly different spin of the genre. A story based leveling system (at first) that leads into a content rich MMO that has appeal to, quite literraly, any form of player who likes the genre. Very challenging group-based endgame PvE, good PvP, and an abundance of 'things to do' that makes for a very gratifying time sink.
Aesthetically, the game has a clean look similar to the other current-gen Final Fantasy games. It runs rather well on my machine and pretty decently on lower end machines, but it's definitely an art style that loses quite a lot of its charm when you start setting graphical settings to 'low'.
The combat system is the standard tab-targetting most of us are likely accustumed to but actually at a slower pace. The game has a 2.5 second global cooldown between abilities. Early on, this feels incredibly slow (because it is) but later on it feels much more meticulous since each ability use is quite a time commitment. I feel much more weight to use the 'right' ability than any other MMO I've ever played, and a big part of using the 'right' ability lies in understanding the fight. This makes the game far less 'go through your rotation based' and just thought-provoking enough to make you forget you're even waiting 2.5 seconds between spells and it's wonderful.
The game has a unique system in which 100% of the content the game contains can be completed on one single character. Every class, job, craft, quest, etc can be completed on one character to the point where there is genuinelly no practical reason to ever make a second. This makes for a unique attachment to that one special character who will likely be with you from beginning to end. All classes (including crafts) can be changed at a whim (outside of dungeons and PvP) by simply changing your weapon. You're given a bonus 25 slots per gear slot to hold every single piece and an easy 'gear set' system to quickly swap between entire sets of gear for your variety of classes.
FFXIV has a pretty decent story with likeable characters and hit-or-miss voice acting. The only major complaint is how you're supposed to be the 'hero of light'... along with all the other thousands of players on your server. Even looking past that, it delivers a classical Final Fantasy adventure that hits all the right notes possible in the MMO setting.
Leveling is rather easy and straightforward; but at the same time allows for an impressive amount of freedom in how you want to go about it at all. Your first class/job will primarily follow the main story line supplemented by FATEs (randomly spawned group content in the world) and dungeon queues to level at a solid pace. The pacing was excellent and was a rather mild curve in the time between levels as you progress. Part of what makes leveling great is that after progressing a little bit into the game you gain access to 'Duty Roulette', which allows you to queue for a random dungeon and upon completetion, receive a tremendous surge in xp on top of the already solid dungeon xp. This allows people on time restraints to level at a very reasonable pace as all you really need is about 35 minutes. After having one max level class, all future classes gain +100% xp to almos everything, partly because they dont get the main story and partly to speed you along.
This is an MMO with a definite PvE focus, as the dungeons are execellently crafted progression of difficulty from the start to the end. A complaint does lie in the first set of dungeons aquired very early on as they were very devoid of mechanics and give a bad impression of future content. Lategame PvE offers a multitude of challenge tiers to accomadate what you as a player are looking to do. Duty Finder raids, unlike other MMO counterparts, don't offer an easy mode, and its nice to see the game respect the playerbase by demanding a minimum skill requirement to start getting your hands on decent gear pieces.
A special mention should go out to this games crafting system. While earlier I mentioned this game has a strong sense of polish to the genre, this area was given a revamp compared to virtually every other MMO with a focus of creating depth, choices, strategy, and a purpose. The crafts are actually classes with their own gear avaiable to them to boast the crafting potentional. Every craft class has their unique spells used during the hard-to-describe act of actually crafting, which plays almost like a classical turn based game balancing many factors such as the progress towards actually finishing the item vs the actual quality of it, among other factors. Craft classes also have certain abilities that benefit other crafts, encouraging you to do them all even if you only really want to use one. Honestly if you've ever wanted to go hard on some crafts, this is DEFINITELY the game to do it.
On a final note, this game has the best soundtrack and the most cinematic, epic bosses in any MMO I've played. I genuinelly don't want to really spoil any of by showing you, but it's pretty freaking great.
Pros
+ Single-character system builds strong bond with your player character.
+ Content that will appeal to any audience that already likes the MMO genre, and many newcomers (are there still any?)
+ Combat that requires some actual mental usage regarding what abilities you're using.
+ Best MMO on a console (but you're reading this on steam...)
+ Great story that blends into the game almost seamlessely.
+ Heavily teamwork-based group PvE content.
+ The content updates are HUGE. The latest one (3.2) required a hefty time investment just to read through all the patch notes.
+ Heavy timesink game based around progressing the overall state of your character rather than locking you behind time/grindgates. Always something to do~
+ Most fun I've had crafting in an MMO to date.
+ Amazing soundtrack that makes bosses feel larger than life. Many bosses have multiple songs, with one even having 5 whole songs. FIVE SONGS!
+ System in place to help new players learn the game, from decent tutorials to a whole network of matching new players with highly experienced ones for guidance.
+ Amazing community from my personal experience.
Cons
- There's a large divide between emptier and fuller servers. Definitely do your research before commiting to a server.
- Early game dungeons are pretty awful.
- Endgame gear/stat choices for each job is very linear. This is lessened since you can play all 13 classes on 1 character.
- The gathering classes are really runescape-y in their grind... but I mean theres not much you can do with collecting rocks.
- Some of the voice acting in English sucks. Some of it is pretty great. But mostly mediocre.
- When you reach level 50 theres a 100 quest slog to get through before you can start the Heavensward (50->60 content.) It's pretty rough, not gonna lie. At least you only have to do it on one character!
Closing thoughts: This game is epitome of taking the fundamentals of a game type and making them perfect. If you're feeling a little burned out by games like WoW or any of its plentiful clones, it may be time to give FFXIV a whirl. If you're just looking for a really comfy game to play and always have stuff to do when you log on, this game is great for that. If you want that classic hardcore PvE content found in the earlier days of WoW, this game delivers on that front too!
Overall rating: 9/10

In
, you play as Mach (who can be either a man or a woman as you choose), an American that is currently living in Seoul, South Korea to further his/her skills as a professional video gamer. S/he is an avid player of
, a real-time strategy game. However, hitting it big on the
scene is not easy, especially for a foreigner.
This game is a visual novel, a game that is entirely story-driven. Despite the number of choices that are offered, the game is ultimately fairly linear. I only came across one bad ending during my play, but it gave me an instant redo. I would estimate it would take around three hours to read through this.
To start off, I thought that the art in this game is pretty good. All of the background art especially is pretty detailed and nice looking. The character sprites are well-drawn and distinctive. There are only a few CGs in the game, but their quality is on par with the other art in the game.
The story is a little difficult to review. As said earlier, the main premise of this game surrounds the South Korean
scene, certainly a niche subject for a visual novel. Now, I will admit that I know nothing about
.
includes a short introductory video for those in a similar situation, but it is extremely superficial. Because of my lack of background knowledge, I honestly had no idea what was going on during parts of the game, mainly during the actual gaming scenes. There is a glossary included that explains some fanspeak terms, but it is inadequate. If you are like me, chances are you are going to find this difficult to enjoy if you are not already familiar with
.
Even ignoring that issue, I found the story to be rather boring. It mostly boils down to characters talking about
, characters playing
, and some side story about Mach recruiting
players to form a team. The characters themselves are another frustration with this game. They pretty much run the gamut from boring to annoying. The main character, Mach, for example, is so obsessed with
that even s/he admits at one point it is difficult for him/her to talk to people about anything else. How does such a broken person even function? The other characters are the usual clichés like Jett, the tough team leader, Reva, the Spock-like analytical one who only speaks in technical language, and Stunt, the overly obnoxious teenager that already thinks he is the best. There is hardly a likable or interesting character in the game.
Overall, though the art is quite good, other aspects of this game fall short with a boring story and weak characters. Perhaps fans of
or eSports might get some enjoyment out of this, but if you are clueless on those subjects it is best to skip this one.

I really want to like this game, but it's too "beta" to be enjoyable. I understand it used to be early access, and has launched (good on them for not abandoning), but the launch version doesn't feel like "release", it still feels beta.
Physically half the matches i played got dropped before they finished, meaning that my progress didn't count for half my playtime, so i couldn't buy upgrades or new blueprints.
There are distinctive jerks of lag every few minutes, even though every player is <50ms ping (i guess maybe there's some error margin that builds up?).
Playing with friends is difficult at best - to join them you need to click rapidly on their icon ingame, but there's no indicator that your client is trying to join the game. So you just keep clicking until the menus go away.
Some blueprints have TODO text on them, or are missing images.
Worst, the game doesn't match what it says on the tin. The front page claims "customizable weapons", and shows a little chart of a gun seemingly with multiple attachments. But those are killstreak rewards - not customizable attachments. You can pick which armors you buy, but that's not "customizable", really.
And saddeningly, the sound was underwhelming and didn't communicate what was going on. Weapons sounded weak, and a lot of times between the pitiful sounds and  the underwhelming animations, i couldn't even tell if my weapon had fired. I was left confused when I was sure i'd fired, but the game didn't seem to think so (even though my ammo went down). Better sound can do wonders to convey state changes to a player, but this game eschewed all of that.
On the plus side, like the titan mode, I think they nailed the balance of titans, creeps, farming, temporary level-ups, and melee/ranged weapon balance. It's competently designed, and when it isn't screwing up, there's a real feeling that I was playing something cool and innovative, a new blend of game.
But overall, when the bugs strike, and when rubber meets the road, it feels like the game was slapped together as a moneymaker. The indie aesthetic, the Unity-level production quality, the bugs, and lack of content screams of a game that was pushed out as quickly as possible for money. The aesthetic itself even feels disingenuous - it's not an indie game, it's just borrowing indie tropes for selling points and lower production cost. I can't begrudge that, we all need to make a living. But it leaves a sour taste when the store page misleads you about the kind of game you'll be playing.
Maybe in a year they'll have the bugs ironed out, and it'll be enjoyable. But will it even have a community in a year? Probably not. So I wouldn't recommend it.

Right, so where do I start... Once upon a time there was a game called "Yakuza" for PS2. At its time it was highly advanced and innovative, open-world (ish) beat'em-up with an interesting story, several side-quests and a street-fights to die for. It was one of my long time favourites and I was really frustrated that it never actually came out for PC.
And then I just happened to stumble upon this little masterpiece. And let me tell you - it's everything the "Yakuza" ever was and more. This game takes standard "GTA" theme but manages to do something a bit different with it.
So let's look at the few positive and negative things that, in my view, pretty much make this game what it is.
POSITIVE:
FIGHTS - Figts, fights and more fights. This is the primary attraction and activity throughout this game. I have seen some reviews that compare this game with another great beat'em-up games - the "Batman" series (in favour of the latter). I was really surprised by this fact as "Batman's" fighting system is completely different, far less realistic and far less controllable (although just as entertaining). In "Sleeping Dogs" you have almost full control over your every punch, kick, counter or grapple. Punch twice and do a jumping kick in the head? Easy. Punch, knee and kick in the face? Can be done. Run at your opponent, dive-tackle him and punch his face in on the ground? No problem. Or just grab your enemy and throw him off the balcony, plant his head in a fish-tank or a burning furnace, smash him into a phone-booth or the bonnet of a nearby car... then kick him in the nuts while he's down. Anything goes. Like I said - it's pretty much like good old "Yakuza", where you could utilise your environment to your full advantage. There're also plenty of weapons to be used - knives, hatchets, tire-irons, police-batons, even lady's purses and hand-bags (although you'd look a bit gay, fighting a bunch of big-*** guys with a purse, but hey - if you want, who am I to stop you?).
ATMOSPHERE - pretty interesting mix. It's something in between GTA, Deus Ex Human Revolution and Yakuza... I know - you're getting pretty tired of reading the word "Yakuza", but this is what this game most reminds me of... so... yeah... YAKUZA (get over it). Hong-Kong really feels like lively, immersive and interesting place to be in. The city really lives - offering plenty of things to do, apart from main or even side quests. Explore, shop, race, gamble, pick a fight with random guys, parkour your *** around alleys and rooftops or just get a massage and buy some food and drink. As it was once said - the man who never eats pork-bun is never a whole man :)
STORY - not the most original part, but quite solid and enjoyable. Missions are a good mix of serious, bloody and gory gangster and double-agent work, to completely ridiculous and funny tasks.
OUTFITS - yeah, I know - not the most important thing in any game, but one has to agree - running through the city dressed as shaolin monk or hurling people around, wearing an extra-large straw sombrero is quite a bit of laugh. Clothing is plentiful and you can choose anything to fit your style and mood.
SHOOTING - pretty basic, but works and can be entertaining in slow-mo, as you jumping over various obstacles.
MUSIC - there is good variety of stations to listen to, while you're cruising around the city. And they all fit the atmosphere pretty much spot on.
NEGATIVE:
Mind you - there are no real negatives in the game. I consider things truly negative, when they spoil the gaming experience and there are no such flaws in "Sleeping Dogs". Just several areas that could be improved to make this game even better.
DRIVING - ok... developers have clearly focused the most of their effort on hand-to-hand fighting and "out of the vehicle" movement. First thing to note about driving - it's hugely unbalanced. Sometimes, you drive a really high-end sport muscle-car and have trouble catching up with an old and beaten mini-bus, you are chasing. Same goes for all races and the police-chases. No matter what you drive - they never f***ing fall behind and leave you be, untill you ram them off the road or shoot up their vehicle. Other thing is that some cars are downright uncontrollable (same goes for boats), with either too sensitive steering or oposite - heavy handling and cornering ablity of 747 jumbo jet.
Having said that, there are also plenty of cars that are actually fun to drive. There are some especially good drifters, with which you can do some crazy stuff - like drifting around the corner, flying sideways in between of oncoming cars, stabilise the drift and proceed as normal. Such things really put a proud little grin on your mug.
GAMBLING - a huge miss-out in my view. Gambling is done as pretty basic mahjong-poker and cockfights (it's not what you've just thought, you sick b*****d - I meant birds). First one is being quite plain and without any character and the latter is completely random - no skill involved, just choose your bird and hope for the best. So come on devs - if you want to include gambling in your game, watch and learn from Witcher, Far Cry 3, Fallout NV, RAGE and so on. You've already created a brilliant atmosphere in everything else - it's not so hard to also add some character to the gambling, now is it?
SIDE-QUESTS VARIETY - side quests are plentiful (which is good), but can get a bit repetitive. I'm being picky here - there's quite a good variety of things to do, but I personally would like just a little touch more of the good thing. I mean - you're undrcover cop and an imposer-triad - there got to be more things for you to do, than resolve petty fights, catch pickpockets, chase cars and respond to a random shoot-outs. But like I said - I'm being picky.
And that, pretty much, sums it up.
So if you like a bit of everything - bit of driving, bit of parkouring (is there even such word? ... nevermind), bit of exploring, bit of just wandering around the city dressed up as Agent-47 (yes- you can do that) and a lot of fighting, by all means buy this game. If, like me, you are an old Yakuza fan and looking for something similar on PC - than you simply must buy this game. Or if you are just looking for something new to play and can't quite make up your mind - I would give this one a shot. Solid piece of work.
P.S. Oh yeah - just in case, I have not said this enough, during my review... YAKUZAAAAAAAAAA.

Not gonna lie. My last review on this game was garbage, so now, I'm rewriting it. I am a DIE-HARD hunter in real life. I love to hunt, mostly for deer with rifle or crossbow. I recommend this game to people who love the outdoors and love to hunt. If you don't and you're a braindead PETA worshipper? Yeah, don't even play this. Now, to the pros and cons.
PROS:
Graphics and sounds are beautiful, the firearms and bows are very well put together, and it's just thrilling when there's a monster whitetail or mule deer buck or a giant bull elk. Of course, if you're into waterfowl hunting, it's almost as realistic as when you're in the duck blind down in the bayou. There is also exciting mission packs and competitions that you can do and earn em$/gm$ that hook your attention to persevere to complete/beat them. You can experience this if you're willing to pay for a membership or not. However, you don't need to necessarily buy membership, you can just refer your friends to the game and if they decide to buy membership, you'll get membership and some pretty cool stuff, like the carved wood deer grunt, which is quite a rare item among the community since not very many people have it, I do though, and you can too!
CONS:
Not all animals are free to hunt, there's the three animals (Whitetail deer, Pheasant, European rabbit) that guests can hunt plus two member animals that change every Thursday. A lot of the stuff in the game needs to be purchased. There's also plenty of bugs that the devs set aside for a while, such as the recent bug where you get sent flying into the air after being charged or falling off a cliff, and sometimes animal AI can be quite buggy. Sometimes shots can be odd, you will aim for the lungs on an animal and end up with intestines, then there's some tracking that can usually end up to lost animals. I once shot a muley buck that was 200+ with a very powerful body shot, and the last track I found from it was a 1-15% blood track, and after that, I couldn't find the buck and had to give up after an hour or 2 of retracing the area (I guess that shows why scent hounds are useful lol).
CONCLUSION:
I give this game an overall 8.5/10, due to the fact I'm a hunter and I personally love this game, but there are bugs that the devs set aside and they really just want your money, which is why you have to pay for literally everything. However, I really recommend this game to people who love the outdoors or people who want to hunt in real life but can't.

I think the best way to describe Fingerbones is "fine".
It's a short game where you explore an abandoned house place and solve puzzles to access new areas that contain more parts of the story. Classic formula for a storytelling game, but in Fingerbones, you move at a snail's pace between the same two areas for 20 minutes, solving "puzzles" so badly made that they can only be thought of as a filler, some excuse to let the developers say it's got puzzles.
So, the game itself is pretty bad. I say it's "fine" overall because the plot does involve things that normally you'd never see in games, and I like when games have the balls to reach new ground like that. The game has good audio to set the scene, but the pixel style didn't add anything to my experience.
The gameplay consists of going between two rooms reading bits of paper left around the place, figuring out passwords to enter into a terminal to unlock a door, and then reading more bits of paper. It's a bits of paper collecting simulator, which is a genre that's been done enough at this point, and it's only redeeming point is its unusual plot.
It also warns that it's not to be played by people who are easily triggered. ♥♥♥♥ that. If people are getting OFFENDED before they're getting scared when playing what is supposd to be a horror game, then I don't want to live anymore.
TL;DR: I don't regret playing it, but I wouldn't recommend it and wouldn't play it again.

I hope Supergiant can continue this streak of excellent games!

It's a fun game and as others have stated it has alot of potential but the game isn't quite there yet.  Be greeted by "coming soon" and greyed out boxes once you load up the game.  The game has two competitive modes, TDM and Titan...the prior being probably the most fun and later being really unbalanced at the moment because so many players are new and don't know how to play the game yet.  In my experience, Titan mode is a crap shoot to whether or not a match is competitve (maybe 10-15% of the time) and this is premiere feature the game is sold on.  It should improve as more players learn the game and if the community stabilized but its too early to tell if player will be sticking around.  But right now the most fun I've had was in TDM...and well, it doesn't really stand out against other shooters with TDM.
There is a cash shop and you can buy items that provide boosts to your stats (while also providing negatives so as not to make the players that pay for items not over powered).  There is no server list, matchmaking only, I really didn't have too much problem getting into a match but I did get a lot problems staying in match because of connection time-outs, others seem to be saying they are having similar problem and I imagien the devs will fix this shortly.
The game is more complicated than I expected, there are alot of weapons that "level up" as you make kills through out a match, as you would expect, they get more powerful.  But when you die it resets to normal.  There are armors that you can craft and you better use them otherwise you will die quickly.
One thing I found annoying was that I couldn't change my loadout while in a match.  They give you 6 slots for different load outs that you can customize prior to the match but this hardly enough considering the number of different weapons.  It would really be easier just to allow players to customize their load out throughout the match.  If I die and the loadouts I have are inadequate, well I'm out of luck for that match.
This is not a twitch shooter and there is alot of sword users in the game, so you should know going in, this isn't really an arena shooter.  Swords require little skill and thus are the favorites of players new to shooters or bad players.  So as a result, they often times can rack up as many points and kills as a seasoned, skilled player.
Overall it's a fun game but that is missing A LOT of features and is going through some early growing pains as people adapt to the game.

Now, I've seen a couple bugs. If you're pressing/holding a directional key when a match is starting, your character can sometimes get stuck moving in that direction. I'm talking about with the keyboard here, so I imagine the same issue might be present on a controller (a positive that it's so easy to set one up if you wish).
The only other problem I've seen is a number of one-sided matches, whether I'm on the winning side or not. This can almost entirely be attributed to how new the game is, however. Everybody will figure it out given some time. FYI the ability to run and gun outweighs the benefits of swords at least in the early/mid game.
Despite minor stuff as above, this game feels like a good shooter, and it feels like a very polished game considering how small the dev team must be. It's graphics are simplistic (or minimalistic, as the title plays on), but still very pleasant to look at, especially when maxed out.
There's plenty of depth and longevity to the crafting system and progressive power curve in each match. When it comes right down to it, what any MOBA or MOBA-lite needs is solid combat, and this game delivers.
GIGANTIC looks like a great game as well, but to some extent, it feels like Minimum has already accomplished what that game intends to do.
Great job devs. Anxiously awaiting future updates as this game hopefully continues to grow.

I'm going to try really hard to write an unbiased review here as I know the writer for this novel personally, but everything I write here will be an honest representation of my thoughts on the game. But first, some minor background to the expectations I had.
I've been playing visual novel games for several years. In a similar comparison, I've also played JRPGs for years. On that note, there exists a well-known engine called RPGmaker that has slowly built itself a notorious reputation in the world of game development. What I mean to say is: most RPGmaker games are middling (which is the nice way of putting it).
Most does not mean all. Likewise, I've been around the block with the world of VNs (which is largely a dark and esoteric extension of the anime fandom); there exists a similar engine created called Ren'Py that largely opened up the accessibility of VN creation; particularly on the international front.
On that note, there are a great many Ren'Py novels that are... not great. Let me be clear that creating a VN of any proportion is an incredible feat. It requires a great many resources just to make something complete, many of which may not be accessible to most typical indie developers. That being said; VNs are not exactly a thriving business in the west due to low demand and serious quality control.
To create something memorable is an extreme challenge and worthy of praise. Sorry for all the exposition, here's what you actually came for:
SC2VN is unique for its subject matter, but does not immediately differentiate itself outside of its setting. The strongest part of this novel is easily its readability and pacing. It is just the right length for a kinetic novel, the kind that doesn't offer meaningful choices and generally reaches a singular ending. The story quickly identifies key characters and differentiates them enough to stand out in the player's mind.
While it does not necessarily offer the most original or in-depth story, what really draws you in is how seamlessly the novel ties realistic reprsentations of the Korean eSports scene with meaningful plot progression. It is made to be very easily followed along, even for the casual reader. Whether you are an enthusiast of Starcraft or completely oblivious to the franchise, the writing easily carries the player along and allows you to enjoy even the more exclusive concepts of its theming.
To make things even easier, it even comes with an in-game glossary to offer definition for jargon and some Korean vocabulary used throughout the novel. This is a really nice feature.
A powerful thing to make your VN really stand out is good presentation. Small attention to detail, especially in GUI, can make a huge difference in my experience. SC2VN applies this concept quite well; one of the nicer touches is how character names (and their appearances to an extent) are color coded to increase distinction from one another. On top of this, an especially nice touch is how there is a small icon next to the names that identify the race that each character plays. Even tiny things like this can go a really long way!
The standard features of a typical VN engine apply, thanks to Ren'Py's great versatility. You have your history log, easily accessible by scrolling up with the mouse wheel. Main menu is right click by default, mostly just the intuitive stuff you'd come to expect from reading PC novels. You think I wouldn't have to mention this stuff, but then you'd be wrong. A lot of Ren'Py novels keep the default options like having to scroll through previous text one block at a time. For perspective: even Key's 'Little Busters' does text history like this. That novel is the GOAT, but holy-muh-convenience dude. Having an actual log come up that you can leisurely scroll through and cancel at any time is doing it right, plain and simple.
No event skip/navigation menu, but this is a superfluous feature for a novel of this length. For the most part, save states are more than enough to secure and recall your favorite scenes if you are inclined to do so.
The visuals and sound are an influential part of this medium. The musical score doesn't sound at all out of place, but it isn't all too memorable. It does borrow tracks and SFX directly from Starcraft, which is a great thematic element. The character art and backdrops exceed the par for quality in indie novels. While it's not the type of work you'd jump to frame on your desktop, it's more than enough to promote the game and appeal its presentation. The art style is also fairly distinctive from your typical 'moe bishojo meta' spam, which is refreshing to say the least.
I've been mainly positive so far, which is intentional because the novel is good. While I definitely recommend it, there are faults that I'm more than willing to address.
The plot is probably the weakest part of the novel. The characterization is fantastic, but I have little to say regarding
the actual story. In the novel's climax, it unwittingly spirals into a very clichéd scenario between the two rival factions. There are some character tropes established throughout, but it would be unfair to criticize this without nitpicking as archetyping is a fairly common approach nowadays (why fix what isn't broken?). Despite this slight defect, the novel promotes itself off of its theme alone, which it does very effectively. An honest glimpse into the Korean pro Starcraft scene makes this more than worth the read on its own.
Choices are strewn throughout, but are more to elicit player interaction than any sort of actual influence on the game's outcome. I'd say this is a plus and a minus, because it serves its purpose well (it explains Starcraft to you. T H E M I N G B O Y S). It is simply not a gratifying way to present choices that the player can easily reload and correct, leading to what becomes more of a roadblock than actual gameplay.
Finally, the length is just okay. Keep in mind that this is a free to play game, so that says a lot. You can complete the read in about 2-5 hours, depending on how meticulous you are. For some, this can be a negative. You could say, it's too short. Finishing the novel is quick, but then it feels like a letdown when you find out that its over. Of course, being short means that the chances of you actually finishing the novel are extremely high, which is a very strong feature in the VN market. It also cuts out a lot of the obligatory 'filler' you see in a lot of Japanese VNs. It's important to note that this game isn't a dating sim, so the construction and focus is quite different. It would simply be nice to prolong the experience, but such is the reality of indie content.
Overview:
Presentation - A+
Music/Art - B+
Story - C+
Characters/Setting - A
+ Strong thematic elements throughout.
+ Memorable characters.
+ Unique Design
+ It costs the low low price of "nothing but your time."
+- Length
+- Depth of plot. It's effective and realistic, though. Satisfying conclusion.
- Obligatory choice gameplay.
- Shallow route deviations.
Overall, this is probably one of the best indie VNs I've ever read by a long shot. It's a very impressive offering, and I'm looking forward to seeing what the sequel has in store (Yes, there is a [pre]quel in development. Look up "Don't Forget Our eSports Dream"). A great glimpse into the Starcraft eSports culture in a clean, easy to digest visual novel format.

Wei's story will resonate with anyone who grew up in two cultures or is Asian-American. You will go through what pulls him in two directions as he struggles to find his place culturally. If HBO, did a miniseries about a cop infiltrating the mafia in Asia, it would be Sleeping dogs.
Compared to GTA:
- Better fighting. Like infinitely better
- Better environment/immersion. Looks like Asia/HK even down to stuff like the air conditioner and bongo trucks.
- Better RPG. You can customize your abilities towards cop / triad.
- Better car management. You can get a car from any parking garage.
- Better side missions. There's racing like GTA, but also fight club. Also, your side missions not only give you money but also mafia XP or police XP.
- Worse driving, but only slightly

Right, so where do I start... Once upon a time there was a game called "Yakuza" for PS2. At its time it was highly advanced and innovative, open-world (ish) beat'em-up with an interesting story, several side-quests and a street-fights to die for. It was one of my long time favourites and I was really frustrated that it never actually came out for PC.
And then I just happened to stumble upon this little masterpiece. And let me tell you - it's everything the "Yakuza" ever was and more. This game takes standard "GTA" theme but manages to do something a bit different with it.
So let's look at the few positive and negative things that, in my view, pretty much make this game what it is.
POSITIVE:
FIGHTS - Figts, fights and more fights. This is the primary attraction and activity throughout this game. I have seen some reviews that compare this game with another great beat'em-up games - the "Batman" series (in favour of the latter). I was really surprised by this fact as "Batman's" fighting system is completely different, far less realistic and far less controllable (although just as entertaining). In "Sleeping Dogs" you have almost full control over your every punch, kick, counter or grapple. Punch twice and do a jumping kick in the head? Easy. Punch, knee and kick in the face? Can be done. Run at your opponent, dive-tackle him and punch his face in on the ground? No problem. Or just grab your enemy and throw him off the balcony, plant his head in a fish-tank or a burning furnace, smash him into a phone-booth or the bonnet of a nearby car... then kick him in the nuts while he's down. Anything goes. Like I said - it's pretty much like good old "Yakuza", where you could utilise your environment to your full advantage. There're also plenty of weapons to be used - knives, hatchets, tire-irons, police-batons, even lady's purses and hand-bags (although you'd look a bit gay, fighting a bunch of big-*** guys with a purse, but hey - if you want, who am I to stop you?).
ATMOSPHERE - pretty interesting mix. It's something in between GTA, Deus Ex Human Revolution and Yakuza... I know - you're getting pretty tired of reading the word "Yakuza", but this is what this game most reminds me of... so... yeah... YAKUZA (get over it). Hong-Kong really feels like lively, immersive and interesting place to be in. The city really lives - offering plenty of things to do, apart from main or even side quests. Explore, shop, race, gamble, pick a fight with random guys, parkour your *** around alleys and rooftops or just get a massage and buy some food and drink. As it was once said - the man who never eats pork-bun is never a whole man :)
STORY - not the most original part, but quite solid and enjoyable. Missions are a good mix of serious, bloody and gory gangster and double-agent work, to completely ridiculous and funny tasks.
OUTFITS - yeah, I know - not the most important thing in any game, but one has to agree - running through the city dressed as shaolin monk or hurling people around, wearing an extra-large straw sombrero is quite a bit of laugh. Clothing is plentiful and you can choose anything to fit your style and mood.
SHOOTING - pretty basic, but works and can be entertaining in slow-mo, as you jumping over various obstacles.
MUSIC - there is good variety of stations to listen to, while you're cruising around the city. And they all fit the atmosphere pretty much spot on.
NEGATIVE:
Mind you - there are no real negatives in the game. I consider things truly negative, when they spoil the gaming experience and there are no such flaws in "Sleeping Dogs". Just several areas that could be improved to make this game even better.
DRIVING - ok... developers have clearly focused the most of their effort on hand-to-hand fighting and "out of the vehicle" movement. First thing to note about driving - it's hugely unbalanced. Sometimes, you drive a really high-end sport muscle-car and have trouble catching up with an old and beaten mini-bus, you are chasing. Same goes for all races and the police-chases. No matter what you drive - they never f***ing fall behind and leave you be, untill you ram them off the road or shoot up their vehicle. Other thing is that some cars are downright uncontrollable (same goes for boats), with either too sensitive steering or oposite - heavy handling and cornering ablity of 747 jumbo jet.
Having said that, there are also plenty of cars that are actually fun to drive. There are some especially good drifters, with which you can do some crazy stuff - like drifting around the corner, flying sideways in between of oncoming cars, stabilise the drift and proceed as normal. Such things really put a proud little grin on your mug.
GAMBLING - a huge miss-out in my view. Gambling is done as pretty basic mahjong-poker and cockfights (it's not what you've just thought, you sick b*****d - I meant birds). First one is being quite plain and without any character and the latter is completely random - no skill involved, just choose your bird and hope for the best. So come on devs - if you want to include gambling in your game, watch and learn from Witcher, Far Cry 3, Fallout NV, RAGE and so on. You've already created a brilliant atmosphere in everything else - it's not so hard to also add some character to the gambling, now is it?
SIDE-QUESTS VARIETY - side quests are plentiful (which is good), but can get a bit repetitive. I'm being picky here - there's quite a good variety of things to do, but I personally would like just a little touch more of the good thing. I mean - you're undrcover cop and an imposer-triad - there got to be more things for you to do, than resolve petty fights, catch pickpockets, chase cars and respond to a random shoot-outs. But like I said - I'm being picky.
And that, pretty much, sums it up.
So if you like a bit of everything - bit of driving, bit of parkouring (is there even such word? ... nevermind), bit of exploring, bit of just wandering around the city dressed up as Agent-47 (yes- you can do that) and a lot of fighting, by all means buy this game. If, like me, you are an old Yakuza fan and looking for something similar on PC - than you simply must buy this game. Or if you are just looking for something new to play and can't quite make up your mind - I would give this one a shot. Solid piece of work.
P.S. Oh yeah - just in case, I have not said this enough, during my review... YAKUZAAAAAAAAAA.

Since I've been at it for a while, and I'm waiting for servers to come back up, I think it's time for a bit of a review.
Pros:
-Beautiful if your system can run it, but the ability to downgrade graphics settings enough to run on a fairly low end machine makes the game possible for more people.
-Great controller support if that happens to be your thing.
-Everything feels fluid. Classes are given very large kits and balance spamable abilites with complex rotations and cooldowns. Things are smiple enough to let casual players compete most content but exceptional players exceed and tackle the highest level raiding conent when it's released.
-Large amounts of midcore content while still providing hardcore and casual content.
-The learning curve while long is actually fairly short compared to most mainstream MMO I've played, and you are able to gain an understanding of things faster due to the ability to level/hotswap out different classes as you please.
-Reasonbly diverse class list genrally offers a lot of different and unique playstyles.
-The dev team is small, but very dedicated and seem to listen to fan feedback reasonably well and puts out major content updates every few months with smaller minor patches to hold everybody over.
-A lot of stuff to do, and plenty of replayability.
-Final Fantasy tier sound track is naturally beautiful.
-You can have all classes on one character. Hotswapable, including crafting and gathering classes.
-Fishing
-Catgirls
-The game is absolutely full of references to different things and amusing humor. Sometimes it's subtle, sometimes it's not. Either way they know what they are doing tears at your soul and they aren't sorry. I like to think of the Square Enix FFXIV dev team as Dr. Evil from the Austin Powers movies.
-It comes with an actually good story, this is extremely rare these days in MMOs but it will destroy your heart.
-Full cutscene/story replay feature for all those people who skip everything and want to figure out the story later.
-It also comes with absurd amounts of side content that only exist to amuse you.
-Everything is put together so nicely. One of it's best features overall is that it doesn't do anything badly.
-Catgirls
-Lots of in game events, probably about once a month or so there is some kind of seasonal event. During some seasonal events including Halloween, Christmas, Easter, Valentines Day, and many more they actually update massive portions of the game thematically. These may also give everything for aestetic gear to mounts.
-Magnificently done atmosphere and fight design.
-Lots of unique content in terms of fight/boss design. Some fights may have overlapping mechanics that were used in other fights but nearly all of the content feels completely different.
-It is still very early in the game's life cycle. If it's anything like it's mother MMO, Final Fantasy XI, then we are close to a quarter done with thousands of hours of content already in the game.
-Y'shtola
Cons:
-The game is an MMO and can be grind heavy.
-Some gear is gated behind time gates (ie only a few pieces of gear a week) and while this cap always gets removed after a while, it adds an unneeded wait for gear.
-The difficulty spike can get a bit high at times when you are new to the game and running content for the first time without watching a proper guide.
-Old content is reused a lot and that's ok to many because much of it is heavily replayable, but the way gear syncing (Limiting stats on gear that has outpaced older content) is done makes some old content far too easy due to stats not being synced low enough and making non-current content faceroll easy.
-While the devs are actively trying to fix things, sometimes the ends don't justify the means with gear. The best example of this would be the relic weapon questline where you grind for gear comparable or better to the best raiding gear at the time, but the steps are meant to be a masochistic grind so it kinda fills it's own purpose.
-On the North American servers excluding Gilgamesh and Balmung (Which are both often locked from character creation due to high population) have rampant amounts of RMT offers sent through private chat and not enough is done to combat it.
-Crafting can often feel trivial in terms of actual combat gear, but as of 3.2, this issue seems to have been eliminated for the most part.
-Much of the seasonal event gear is free if you attended the event, but is put in the cash shop after a long period of time downing the exclusivity of having experienced the event. This is more of a personal gripe.
-There is a cash shop purely for visual items (Almost only special sets that were free at one time and a few other special items)
-Dps que can occationally become unreasonable
-The selling system/overflow storage system works off retainers, basically servants that you can customize. You are given two by default which is enough for many players, but they offer more (Up to six) for a small monthly fee. Very upsetting considering the game is purchased plus pay to play although extra retainers aren't that neccessary for most.
-You will re-run old content a lot. While this keeps que times shorter for people trying to level alternate classes, it can be old after a while, but you are given many options for how you level.
-Still no dedicated damage parsing feature implemented by the devs, but many parsing utilites do exist (Banned but ok normally as long as you don't talk about them in big public chats). This is only essential for end game raiding for the most part.
-The game is still young (First expansion was less than a year ago) and the devs are still working on their proper flow, so occationally they will do some experimenting and ♥♥♥♥ stuff up, although they do normally fix things.
A bit of a summary: This game really is great. Overall, having played many other MMOs, I think I've never found another that put everything you could want in a fantasy MMO together so fluidly. It's not that it's unique. If you are looking for some super never before seen gameplay then go be a loli with a giant axe in Tera or go warp into a gatecamp in Eve Online. This game's actual "Uniqueness" literally comes from how well everything is put together, not because it tried to change the key formula. Visually it is stunning. The music goes above and beyond what anybody could ever expect of an MMO and keeps on going. The atmosphere in fights is absolute insanity. I still get shivers when I think about how amazing some of the 8 man raids were. While some of the older content had been defamed due to the added "Unsynced" feature and the lack of proper gear syncing, much of it is extremely enjoyable to go back and play due to the nature of the game. Do not go into this game thinking you are going to be amazing fast. The lack of proper level syncing makes some of the early content too easy and it's unfortunate when new players get haymakered in the jaw because they weren't sufficiently prepared. This is being addressed by the dev team slowly, but it is still a problem that exists. If you can afford the monthly bill and want to ruin your life, then this game is absolutely worth getting.

Shakes and Fidget is a very fun and compelling game as long as you know what you're getting into. Namely, it's an idle starical free to play RPG. You can go on quests, collect loot, do PVP, and eventually enter dungeons and build a fortress. The game is very light hearted in its writing and humor. It is very much a parody of a lot of modern RPGs, especially World of Warcraft. I like the art style in particular. It's very ... German if that makes any sense.
When you go on a quest, there is a timer that counts down until the quest is completed. And this is where the idle aspect of the game fits in. This is a small game designed to run in the background while you do other things. I usually had my character going on quests in the background while I played WoW and FF14. I honestly have had a lot of fun leveling and gearing my character and pitting her against other people's characters in the arena. And the dungeons are actually tough which is something I kind of miss in modern MMOs! There is a premium currency in the form of mushrooms, but I never felt forced to spend money on any as the game is pretty forgiving in giving you mushrooms as you play, allowing you to go on extra quests or do an extra arena if you so desire. And when you decided you've had enough for the day, you can even assign your character to guard duty so you can continue to earn gold even when you've turned the game off.
Overall, I have had a lot of fun with this game and I highly recommend everyone at least give it a try.

Grand Theft Auto, NARC (if NARC wasn't a horrible game)
You play as an undercover cop who grew up in Hong Kong, and just came back from a recent takedown in America. You contact a childhood friend who helps get you in as a foot soldier in the Triad. Armed with a certain set of skills you must prove yourself to fellow gang members in order to climb the latter and bring the brotherhood down. The game behaves like a GTA clone for the most part. Where it mainly differs is in the hand to hand martial arts combat system. Will you get a major bust taking down the Triad or will your old roots to the area cause you to forget your a cop?
The martial arts combat works quite nice. The car combat is very over the top in a good way. The story is done fantastically making you really feel it. There is a ton of content here and the town really gives you a great Hong Kong vibe from street vendors selling knockoffs all the way to singing karoke at a bar. The Triad main quest, cop main quest, and girlfriend quests are all extremely unique.
The collectables are everwhere so if you have OCD about getting everything this game can be a problem, but you do at least get rewards for doing it. It is actually to easy to get away from the cops making it no big deal to steal cars and go ped hunting. Which brings me to the final point. Your a cop... yet you can kill tons of pedestrians, steal cars, and a number of other things without any penalty from your department? I mean even Dirty Harry didn't kill civilians left and right. The game also could have benifited from multiple endings. The side missions wear thin very quickly.
Sleeping Dogs really managed to find its own identity by taking cues from other games and improving upon them. The story and voice acting is highly successful, but you won't feel like freestyling and doing side missions as much as you would in a GTA title.
In terms of the Definitive Edition I'd say the improvements aren't worth it if you already have the regular game. When it comes to DLC I liked the Year of the Snake only. The main game itself is easily a $30 value which is the price of the Definitive Edition. So go ahead and buy this game, and especially if it goes on sale.

Writing this review at the end of my first month, 120 hours played. I've reached level 51 so far, out of 60, and still have a way to go before the end-game content.
The Good:
-Pleasant aesthetics. Music and graphics are both charming.
-Nice community. I was invited to a social group early on, full of highly active people who are chatty and helpful.
-Lots of content. It's a huge world to explore, with varied environments and monsters, and plenty of quests. Also many classes and tradeskills to level up.
The Bad:
-Button-mashing combat. Fighting enemies consists of hitting the '1' key over and over, occasionally tapping '2' off cooldown, and sometimes stepping out of a telegraphed attack area. Of course the late-game raids have more involved mechanics, but the other 90% of the game's combat is mind-numbingly dull.
-Boring quests. The overwhelming majority of my time in game so far has been spent running between NPC's for quest updates. I wish I could pay NOT to play this part of the game. Unfortunately, these quests are required to access the raids later on. If you're thinking about buying this game, know that you'll be spending 150+ hours of running between NPC's before you can get to any sort of raids or interesting combat.
Final Word:
I bought into this MMO for two reasons. To socialize with other people, and to experience challenging raids. The former was easy enough, but the latter was gate-locked behind hundreds of hours of mindless tedium, which was not in any way worth my time or money.

Every now and then I come across a game that's different. Transistor certainly fits that description in the most positive way.
Gameplay wise, I quickly realized that Transistor truly shines in it's skill system. It gives you complete freedom to play in hundreds of different ways. Nearly all of them being completely viable.
I had a ton of fun trying different combinations of my functions, upgrading them with different upgrades and seeing their effect in battle. Even though the game is rather short, the replayability is high. You won't experience everything in your first playthrough at all.
Story  wise the game is a breath of fresh air with a special type of narrative. 99% of the game is narrated solely by your companion. While that may seem like a dangerous choice for creating a coherent story, it works completely well. Especially because it gives off an eerie feeling of loneliness and despair. Feelings that are very much in sync with the setting of the game.
All in all I'm glad I bought this game and I can one hundred percent recommend it to people who enjoy a good story, and also like experimenting with their gameplay style.

This is easily one of my favourite games of 2014 and of all time! In
, you control Red, a singer who, after one night is nearly assassinated, must use the mysterious Transistor sword to fight wave after wave of enemies as she travels through the city of Cloudbank to find the people who tried to kill her.
+Story is fantastic. Very heartwarming, epic and will tug at your heart strings.
+The art and scenery is just absolute eye candy. To see more from the artist, check out Jen Zee's DeviantArt
+Soundtrack is an absolute eargasm. With vocals from Ashley Barrett and Darren Korb, it fits the mood of the game perfectly and is great for listening to outside of the game.
+Gameplay alternates between real-time combat and turn-based combat in the same vein as the 'V.A.T.S.' system from the
video games by Bethesda/Zenimax, making for very fun and creative combat scenarios.
+Customisation is left entirely to the player to choose EXACTLY how they want to play. With the ability to equip moves as direct attacks, passive affects or attack bonuses, hundreds of different combinations are available to players.
-Enemies get a little repetitive after a while, especially in the game's later levels.
-You'll wish it lasted a little longer.
Ultimately, I cannot recommend
enough. It's not everyday that a game THIS good comes out for people to play, and quite frankly, I think Supergiant did WAY better than most AAA developers did in 2014 when producing what I could consider one of the best games I've ever played.

Each player has a ball they must roll through the enemy track and hit the enemy gate with as much force as possible. Defence structures on the track damage the ball, breaking off it's mass. When the ball is destroyed or reaches the gate at the end, the player has some time before a new one is built to reinforce their track with defensive structures. A game ends when one player crushes another's gate and rolls over their avatar behind it.
This is a fun game to play at parties, especially if you are short on weed or value your health yet still want to f*ck with people's minds. Also if you think a 4 ton stone boulder can squash a cow - you are wrong. Cow>stone.

Here's why I don't recommend this game. Each point will be explained into further detail later. Please note, if I appear harsh or spiteful, I want the game to be fun and hope that this is taken as constructive critisism, and this review is susceptible to change as the game's life progresses and if the devs make necessary changes.
1. Not completed, far from it.
2. Paywalls, for guns, armor, asthetics, you name it.
3. Unbalanced gameplay
4. Gameplay itself is poor
5. Very quickly gets repetitive
6. Progression for someone who doesn't pay cash to get guns is ridiculously slow.
7. Devs prefer to have more items available for you to buy than having completed features.

So, to begin with, the game simply is not completed. It has an absolute plethora of features- Except you can't access them. About 1/20 of the features are actually there, from things such as crafting, upgrading, or in general, unlocking items. This also ties into reason number 7, where despite these features being unavailable, they STILL have more items for you to buy with cash than they do items you can unlock naturally. This is something that would be expected from a game in need of funding i.e. a F2P game, not a 10 dollar game at full price.
Next up, gameplay. The gameplay, put simply, can have a winning team be determined within the first minutes of deathmatch, the first hour of titan mode, and the co-op of course doesn't apply here. The way the game works is by getting a kill, or picking up a "powerup" when dropped by an enemy or a turret of theirs, the weapon equipped increases in power. However, when you die, that weapon's level is reset when you respawn. The devs have "fixed" this by making the primary weapon start off with three levels in the late game. This is inherently flawed, since the team who gets luckier first has players that are constantly capped out with max weapons that dominate everyone, even with the minor boost that you're given since the level 5 of every weapon is just God Mode. The most common retort to this is, "Well, you keep your armor, so it's fine." In truth, your armor makes little to no difference in combat when there's some guy with a sword that can kill you with two hits, with or without the armor.This happens in deathmatch and titan mode, the only difference is that one just takes longer to end.
When the I say the gameplay is poor, I'm referencing certain mechanics and design desicions. When taking damage, the only indicator you have is when your character begins to glow, and there's a soft hum. This is an absolute pain in the♥♥♥♥♥when in a huge firefight with particles everywhere that are the same color as the character's glow. You often find yourself dead without ever noticing that you were taking any major damage to begin with, and have to restart your progression of weaponry. This especially hurts the game because this isn't just getting unlucky, this happens with a 50/50 chance depending on if your team is winning or not. Having to deal with this constantly is absolutely one of the game's biggest killjoys, especially when you see some guy with a set of armor and weapons that you can't get without spending anther 10 bucks or so.

The final reason for this game's bad impression on me is because one of it's arguably most important reasons, for me at least. In the game, I've reached level six, and I have only managed to craft one, count em, ONE gun. This is a huge pain for me personally, because even if guns could be bought with money, it would still be somewhat fair if the average player could obtain those as well through natural progression, and without needing to spend a few hours for one gun. The game would be so much more balanced with just a simple fix, and yet its quality suffers because of the direction the developers seem to want to take the game. It isn't impossible to have microtransactions in a balanced game, but the way it's being promoted in this game is just horrible and is hurting the experience as opposed to helping it get players caught up.

Reign of Kings, an underated gem...
A friend of mine gifted me this game about a year ago, I had heard about it before and excited to play. I played it for about an hour and didnt pick it up again, untill recently and i finally realised how great this game really is.
Reign of Kings is an open-world survival game. I know that many open-world survival games have been released recently and how repeatitive and similar they feel, but I believe Reign of Kings stands apart from the crowd. It is based in medieval times and you craft many medieval weapons and structures to survive and raid other bases, such as enormous catapults, crossbows, swords and shields. There is also a very good building system in this game wich is a good change from some other open-world games on the market today. I am a big fan of survival games such as Ark: Survival Evolved and The Long Dark, and this has to be one of my favourite building systems i have seen. I am a big fan of buidling systems in games and it was so enjoyable to use this one.
However Reign of Kings does suffer from some issues. One issue I noticed in the building system was that the game will not let you place blocks sometimes as the game thinks a player is in the way. This can get annoying at times, but is easilly fixed by placing the block form a different angle but, it still gets annoying in some situations. This the only bug i have experienced in the game so far and believe me it is annoying. However the game also has problems with servers, as there is not a large player count and there is no private servers or private sessions, wich can get annoying if you only want to play with your friends and not with others. Reign of Kings also only has few dedicated servers but it is easy to join a server near you as i said before there is not many people playing.
The game also has many interesting features  such as plague villages (filled with people infected with the Plage or Black Death), a Ruler system in wich one player can become king and collect taxes from others and so on. This game is surprisingly unique and stands apart from the crowd.
Reign of Kings has been a joy to play recently and if you have some friends to play with, oh boy it makes this game even better. My experience playing with friends was so much better that flying solo, but it can differ between people. It was great to see devs like these to step up and build upon the existing open-world survival genre and finally make a game unique and different. If you have a few bucks to spare, I highly recommend you should pick this game up.

This is an... interesting visual novel. As it was free, and I had heard good things about it, I thought I'd try it. Aside from a few trap choices, there isn't really much in the way of the good ending. And it is fun enough (as well as informative in its fashion).

A very well designed Visual Novel which is tailored to but not limited to Starcraft II players as well as eSports fans in general, however, it is done in a manner that allows it to be played by even those that are not in either of these categories.
You follow in the life of Mach, a protagonist who is trying to make his own as a competitive StarCraft II player, the art-work is clean and top-notch, as well as the overall background sound doing a good job of maintaining itself constant to the atmosphere of what's going on, the story is immersive, and the characters are well fleshed out, detailed and allow yourself to relate to them in the situations that transpire over the course of the game.
I have no real complaints, it is definitely worth your time and a good addition to your library, it's completely free and a very good Visual Novel, a lot better than some of the paid ones on the Steam platform, only really losing to them in the amount of playtime that it provides, but given that it is a freebie, it's to be expected, nonetheless the game still gives you a fairly good amount of time playing it, easily over an hour+ if you take your time reading every line, as well as tuning in to the extras that the game holds for you.
This game is well deserving of a sequel, and i recommend it to anyone whether you be a hardcore gamer or someone who's simply looking for a Visual Novel to read out.
Entertaining, and a good way to burn a few hours. If you make a wrong choice (somewhat easy to do if you're not a StarCraft player), SC2VN lets you retry fairly quickly.

Grand Theft Auto, NARC (if NARC wasn't a horrible game)
You play as an undercover cop who grew up in Hong Kong, and just came back from a recent takedown in America. You contact a childhood friend who helps get you in as a foot soldier in the Triad. Armed with a certain set of skills you must prove yourself to fellow gang members in order to climb the latter and bring the brotherhood down. The game behaves like a GTA clone for the most part. Where it mainly differs is in the hand to hand martial arts combat system. Will you get a major bust taking down the Triad or will your old roots to the area cause you to forget your a cop?
The martial arts combat works quite nice. The car combat is very over the top in a good way. The story is done fantastically making you really feel it. There is a ton of content here and the town really gives you a great Hong Kong vibe from street vendors selling knockoffs all the way to singing karoke at a bar. The Triad main quest, cop main quest, and girlfriend quests are all extremely unique.
The collectables are everwhere so if you have OCD about getting everything this game can be a problem, but you do at least get rewards for doing it. It is actually to easy to get away from the cops making it no big deal to steal cars and go ped hunting. Which brings me to the final point. Your a cop... yet you can kill tons of pedestrians, steal cars, and a number of other things without any penalty from your department? I mean even Dirty Harry didn't kill civilians left and right. The game also could have benifited from multiple endings. The side missions wear thin very quickly.
Sleeping Dogs really managed to find its own identity by taking cues from other games and improving upon them. The story and voice acting is highly successful, but you won't feel like freestyling and doing side missions as much as you would in a GTA title.
In terms of the Definitive Edition I'd say the improvements aren't worth it if you already have the regular game. When it comes to DLC I liked the Year of the Snake only. The main game itself is easily a $30 value which is the price of the Definitive Edition. So go ahead and buy this game, and especially if it goes on sale.

Every now and then I come across a game that's different. Transistor certainly fits that description in the most positive way.
Gameplay wise, I quickly realized that Transistor truly shines in it's skill system. It gives you complete freedom to play in hundreds of different ways. Nearly all of them being completely viable.
I had a ton of fun trying different combinations of my functions, upgrading them with different upgrades and seeing their effect in battle. Even though the game is rather short, the replayability is high. You won't experience everything in your first playthrough at all.
Story  wise the game is a breath of fresh air with a special type of narrative. 99% of the game is narrated solely by your companion. While that may seem like a dangerous choice for creating a coherent story, it works completely well. Especially because it gives off an eerie feeling of loneliness and despair. Feelings that are very much in sync with the setting of the game.
All in all I'm glad I bought this game and I can one hundred percent recommend it to people who enjoy a good story, and also like experimenting with their gameplay style.

Forward note! For my opinion on the Sleeping Dogs in general, I assure you I'm a fan. I've bought the game triple times now, and my disregard about "definitive edition" concerning only how little I got, paying for the game that third time. You can see my review on the Sleeping dogs there:
In short, if you have the Sleeping dogs game already, you don't need to buy that "Definitive edition".  But if you've missed it earlier - don't wait until it's become completely obsolete, give it a shot!
What is new in "Sleeping Dogs: Definitive Edition"? Well, there are many small things redistributed here and there, mostly to the better. Example: there was a bind to the right mouse button, so if you click it while driving, Wei Shen jumps off the venicle with the gun ready, in slow-mo, of course. Cool feature, very cinematographic, but almost never used. I remember more than dozen times in the original Sleeping dogs when I occasionally clicking that button in the middle of the chase... and have to restart all sequence. Because of the one stupid button binding. Good news: they fixed it in "Definitive edition"! Sweet? Yeah, for sure!
But hey, key binding is a very small thing, do we really need to buy all the game once more to have normal controls?
Sorry, if I'm talking too long, but I'm gonna give you a full comparison of the two products now, so if you're not ready to read it all, goto 10, or skip to the bottom.
Like I said earlier, developers of Sleeping dogs redistributed all the secondary stuff in the game. That means that original game, all its mechanics, practically all its glitches - remained the same. Remember dying in the "Election" mission in jumping sequence? It's remained the same. Stupid taxi mappings? There. And so on. Yep, if we take a general look, they refurbished some textures. But that was made with great price of tossing away all 32-bit systems. "VIP only" now! But if you ask me, if the game looking better now, I'll answer "No, it remained almost where it was. You'll not see the difference even if you try to".
All about secondary stuff, that's it. Notorious DLC. Now, in the Definitive edition, they seems much more logically connected with the main story. Side missions appears connected with the main quest progress, experience they giving now is not enough to quick levelling. All is much more fair now. And dull. And dumb. See, from the first place, the main story itself is not logical and well-implemented with the real (or cinematographic) Hong Kong. It is not a comic book, thank God, but very close to it - naive, sketchy and simplesized. Was made that way to fit "normal" user, of course.
What I'm trying to say there is that all that developers gain in logic and balance, they lose in general fun out of the game. Take a Retro-Triad suit for example. In general sense, Wei Shen cannot wear a suit like that no matter what. It is not fit into story. Yet, it is fun to wear. So it exist. But there's a difference. In the "old edition" you can wear some (any) parts of that suit separately. I, for example, liked gloves. Someone liked the haircut (yeah, it's part of the suit). So everyone could pick it's own look. Sorry, but no more. If you want Retro-Triad suit, it's there, but only as whole. Makes even less sense than it was before.
Let me put it once again:
+ Added some high-res textures for graphics freaks. Still not comparable with the Rockstar product, though.
+ All DLC, all the seconadary stuff now structurized and appears with the progress of the main quest.
+ Some new missions were added! They are quite short and linear, but new is a new!
+ Some small glitches and questionable game features was fixed

This is easily one of my favourite games of 2014 and of all time! In
, you control Red, a singer who, after one night is nearly assassinated, must use the mysterious Transistor sword to fight wave after wave of enemies as she travels through the city of Cloudbank to find the people who tried to kill her.
+Story is fantastic. Very heartwarming, epic and will tug at your heart strings.
+The art and scenery is just absolute eye candy. To see more from the artist, check out Jen Zee's DeviantArt
+Soundtrack is an absolute eargasm. With vocals from Ashley Barrett and Darren Korb, it fits the mood of the game perfectly and is great for listening to outside of the game.
+Gameplay alternates between real-time combat and turn-based combat in the same vein as the 'V.A.T.S.' system from the
video games by Bethesda/Zenimax, making for very fun and creative combat scenarios.
+Customisation is left entirely to the player to choose EXACTLY how they want to play. With the ability to equip moves as direct attacks, passive affects or attack bonuses, hundreds of different combinations are available to players.
-Enemies get a little repetitive after a while, especially in the game's later levels.
-You'll wish it lasted a little longer.
Ultimately, I cannot recommend
enough. It's not everyday that a game THIS good comes out for people to play, and quite frankly, I think Supergiant did WAY better than most AAA developers did in 2014 when producing what I could consider one of the best games I've ever played.
TL;DR: ADD TO CART

Do you remember the late 90s? A time of .GIF filled websites, AltaVista and America Online or AOL as it was more commonly known. Back then everything was big and proud and come 2001 it all got bigger and prouder as Windows XP hit us squarely in the jaw with its big blue windows and incredible OS power. It was around this time that AIM, AOL’s Instant Messenger service was at its biggest. We all had an AIM username and like mobiles today we all sat there furiously typing away to friends and workmates over our monitors. We made relationships and we broke hearts, we arranged meets and gaming sessions. AIM was king.
To do this you have conversations with Emily about various aspects of yours and her life, from music to video games, movies to social anxieties and more. The game is a simple one to play. Emily pops up in AIM and says hello, which leads you to a multiple choice of answers. By picking your answer you then ‘converse’ to Emily by pressing random keys on your keyboard. It may sound overly simple and even dull but rest assured, it is not. It feels like you are having a conversation with a real person and in this the developer, Kyle Seeley, really must be praised. Emily will annoy, tempt, tease and laugh along with you for all of its 45 minutes average gameplay per session.
Emily feels so real that at the end of my second playthrough I was desperate to make her fall in love with me but by the end of the fifth I was content to insult her and be as cold as a person in love can be to the other that constantly scorns her/him no matter how hard he/she tries! Come my sixth attempt I just wanted to be loved by anyone and was quite relieved and happy to know that it was all just a game.
Emily Is Away is a game that pushes buttons, your own emotional ones and for something consisting of basic text and very little else it does a surprisingly good job of it. Sure, it may not work for everyone but anyone out there that enjoys interactive fiction, choice and consequence this will no doubt bring more than one emotion to the fore once you really get into the game and determine your goal.
Multiple paths exist so one session is unlikely to feel like the last or next one but you will probably find that five or six attempts is enough to have seen most of it. This is not a bad thing though as those five or six attempts will likely take up to three hours or more of your time and for a game that has no set price you cannot ask for much more.
Without giving away spoilers it really is quite hard to explain the things you will come across when playing and so this will, like the game itself, be a short but hopefully fulfilling review of a beautiful little title that everyone really should experience at least once.

Remastered original, and a beautifully detailed remaster I might add.  Five chapters of awesome puzzles based on observation and logic with an eyepiece to see though quantum flux to find invisible puzzles and clues.  Each chapter is a self-contained singular overall enigma designed to be solved by progressively solving a mirade of other puzzles.  In Chapter 1 the point is to open the safe.  In Chapter 2 the point is to open the puzzle box found in the safe.  Chapter 3 starts with the now unopened box which has converted into a much larger table.  As the player goes through each chapter the player is drawn deeper into the overall mystery at the same time the quantum compressed original puzzle box gets bigger, changes shape and dimension (literally) and becomes more complex.
As far as a storyline goes it is briefly explained through various notes of encouragement, explaination and clues left behind by a mentor and friend.  Me, personally I think I would be upset with my mentor friend after dragging me through quantum leaps and alternate dimensions then not having the decency to at least explain my whereabouts at my final destination.  (The game is basically left as a 'to be continued'.)  However, this should not be a discouragement for playing this progressive logic puzzle game.
NOTE/WARNING:  If the player is having trouble on the very last puzzle (a simple slider maze) and finishing the maze because the piece gets stuck, change the frame rate to say 60 FPS.  Being an older game, it seems a too high frame rate causes this tiny glitch at the end of the game.
