The game tried to counter the behaviors imprinted into gamers for decades, it targeted our trained reations and tuanted at us like those a-holes in school (but smaters)
Playing this game, I felt frustrations, but in a good way... because instead of doing things I've been doing for all these years before finishing the game and move on to another one, I got to think hard about how to proceed each of my steps because I know the game would always throw some nasty things on my plate along the way.

Boring, tedious, and repetative. There's fans of this type of game and unless you're the kind that enjoys endless mindless memorization combined with trial and error and very very loose controls then avoid. There is a noticable and most likely deliberate lag in the controls regardless of what method you choose. So sloppy controls combined with pixel perfect gameplay and non-sensical rule on what is and is not safe makes for a rather bland dull game. Oh, and the music, you'll end up turning it off immediately. It loops and repeats forever over every death and never changes. And to add to all this, the deaths take forever to respawn. First you die, then you bounce, then other things bounce, then you have to wait for all that to fall off the screen AND the musical WAHWAAAAAAAH to finish, and god help you if you trigger another trap at the same time.

Imagine if Bowser used cheat codes against Mario, giving him an unfair advantage.
Eryi's Action takes some of the most frustrating moments of platform gaming design and piles it on top until you almost want to scream "THAT ISN'T FAIR". But in the world we live in, where few things are fair, I think this game is perfect. It sets you up to fail...and fail...and fail. You end up learning from your mistakes, memorizing where the pitfalls are.
This is a game where EVERYTHING is trying to kill you, and you don't have much to defend yourself with. I think some will find it TOO frustrating, but others will enjoy the adventure where you learn by dying a lot.
....It took me 119 deaths to make it through the first level.

This game is a monument to every annoying, frustrating, BS death you've ever experienced in a platformer. No two methods of dying are the same, and this game will utterly troll you anywhere with yet another creative way to die. You start out with two lives, you'll probably finish in the negative hundreds. That aside, the difficulty in the normal game ranges from "moderate" to "fairly tough", and some sections will force you to problem solve.
If this game has a drawback, it would be the length it's a pretty short game. Otherwise, the graphics are clean, the controls are fantastic, and it makes endless dying fun again.
I had my own epiphany in the second level when, after crossing an entire screen's distance without dying, I doubled back to make sure I hadn't missed any opportunities for death.

Eryi's Action is a fun little platformer that punishes the player for doing the norms of video game platforming.  It doesn't punish you by making you replay long section however, as it is actually quite generous with it's checkpoints.  It's deaths are amusing, as is it's general story.  It is challenging and fun, and makes you have to think about things in a different manner.  After dying numerous times, I still find the game to be quite fun and have never felt completely lost on how to beat a certain challenge.

The description says Eryi’s Action is “additively challenging and FUN.”  The game is none of these. Challenging implies a degree of fairness and a possibility of winning, fun implies you’ll actually enjoy the experience and additively doesn’t even make sense in that sentence.
Eryi’s action is cheap.  Right now it’s selling for 4 bucks.  If you get the right trading cards and sell them in the market for the right price, you can almost get the game for free (not really free, but if someone is willing to pay 75 cents for an imaginary trading card they deserve to be buying other people games. )
It’s also cheap, as in grossly unfair.  The only clue to help you find the traps is being killed by them.  Unlike the memory game from Robot Chicken, there is enough randomness to keep you from learning from your mistakes.  SPOILER ALERT!! The traps also kill you in places and ways that have always been sacred in platformers.  Giant pans fall from the ceiling in your house (that does technically meet building code in China).  Spike balls that you could easily jump over land in your path after you raised the level complete flag and no longer control you character as she walks to the end of the level.  Monsters even kill you on the stage selection world map.  They might as well kill you just for pressing start.
In conclusion (yes, again,) if someone asks you what your safe word is and you have to think about it, don’t buy this game.  If on the other hand, life isn’t unfair enough or you just hate yourself, then pick it up.  Don’t say I didn’t warn you.

I had never played a visual novel before, and I have never played any Starcraft game (although I do follow a bit of competitive LoL, so I do know about esports). Despite this, I really, really, loved this game. In short, it's simply beautifully made. Yes, you are not given a lot of choices (to be honest you're barely given any), but the story alone makes it worth it. I liked the story as it gave you some insight on the world of esports in South Korea, the country of esports. Also talks about how hard it is for a top player to find a team, how hard it is for someone to actually make a team even if with the right players.
Not having played SC before hasn't made it less enjoyable (well, probably a bit, but not too much). There were some jokes, strategies, unit names etc., that I didn't understand or I had to Google (liquipedia helped A LOT, by the way), but in the end the experience was still very positive. The parts with SC games are very well explained and easy to understand. I even found myself actually panting during the last part of the game!
As it's also a free game, so I'd recommend everyone who's up for a good story and no gameplay to play this visual novel!
Loved it! The writing was excellent, it definitely stirs up real emotions,  music and art were exceptionall as well.
An eye-opening look into how competitive the world of Esports is. Kudos to all who dedicated their lives to chasing this dream.

Has several decision points with bad choices and several decision points with uninportant choices .  Check in forum for a guide to finish this VN.
Try it, maybe you might like it if you like visual novels.
For more info:
Walkthrough

SC2VN - The eSports Visual Novel Review - Raymond KT
Summary: SC2VN is a visual novel about the South Korean StarCraft 2 scene. You play as Mach, a foreign semi-pro trying to make it in eSports who soon learns that success in StarCraft takes more than in-game strategy.
While I like the premise of the game, it is rather short and fails to live up to it's hype. The real dealbreakers though for me is the fact that aside from a couple of choices that would instantly lead to a game over is that this is basically a linear kinetic novel rather than a visual novel, as well as how the final "battle" was done. I was excited I was thinking of what kind of choices and strategies to do, then nothing. You win. That's it. The final scene would work well for the end of the first part of a VN but rather hanging as an ending.

Solid plot, interesting characters, a protagonist with an internal conflict anyone could identify with, and an indepth peek into a world with a steep barrier to entry: this VN has all the working parts for a good story. I appreciated the solid writing. The conciseness of the language was a pleasant relief from translated japanese hits.
If anyone was wondering whether they could enjoy a VN, this would be my first reccomendation. I can't wait to see what this writer/director/studio will be putting out in the future.

I came into this game expecting another "GTA-ish" game, but Sleeping Dogs was more than that. I'm not a good reviewer, but my friends asked me to do this, so here goes:
Set in Hong Kong, you play as man named Wei Shen. Without diving into details, Wei went to America with his family to try and escape the life they had in Hong Kong. He eventually comes back, and becomes an undercover police officer for the HKPD. Throughout the game, you face the hardships and stress of being on both sides, as betrayal and death are everywhere.
One of the it's main strongpoints is the storyline and characters. It's deep, and you'll find yourself bonding with the other characters better than others. You'll be emotionally and physically sad when something bad happens, and happy when something good happens.
The graphics are on-par, as well. Having played the standard edition, I can say with confidence that this game looks much better. From lighting to weather, you'll find that this game truly is beautiful if you actually pay attention to the details. The game is also fairly optimized, and I had no trouble maintaining a steady FPS on high-max settings. Although, I did find a bit of a drop whenever I get near water, but it's barely noticeable.
There are many things to do in the city of Hong Kong, and when you're done with the main storyline, you can load up the two extra expansions that come with the game. This game easily has 50+ hours of gameplay in it.
Well, get to it officer. Who should you side with when the people you're spying treat you better than your employers? Will you stay loyal to the ones you work for, or leave in favor of the ones who take care of you?

This was a 7/10 for the original release but the Definitive Edition gains the extra mark for having remastered graphics and including all the DLC for 1 price.
The game itself is great and it is simply awesome to run around Hong Kong and brutally beat your way through hoards of gangsters and martial arts challenges whilst cruising around in cars, bikes and boats.
Graphics are great with the lighting and characters getting big facelfts, the audio was always great and the voice acting second to none but the big pull to this game is that it is an Open World Story Driven Beatem Up as I am now labeling it.
Some have called it GTA with a martial arts focus rather than relient on firearms but it really gives you more of an immersed feel than GTA making you feel like a young Bruce Lee back in his early film career.
My favorite part is the Tournement (DLC) which is a copy of Enter the Dragon (Bruce Lee) but the whole game is epic.
If you already own all the DLC and obviously the original game then its not a smart purchase unless like me you are a big fan of this game and can happily spend time doing it all again but in a more refined edition.  If you don't have all the DLC then buy now and enjoy one of the most surprising and entertaining games I have played in a couple years.

Potentially a great game, but still needs a lot of work. This is definetly not finished.
The design:
It looks great, the minimalist approach is very pleasing and makes me feel like I'm battling using legos, a good thing as far as I'm concerned :)
The different level designs are diverse and nice to play in, vibrant and fun.
A bit more customisation would be great though, colours, shapes or other visual effects without game effects, only making you look different.
After a few matches you can choose some specific armour bits, aimed at your playstyle, most of them looking the part.
The game itself:
Potentially this could be great, especially the game-mode with the titans. However:
Controls:
Everything feels slowish, not as streamlined as a shooter should. Somehow the controls feel a bit sluggish, can't put my finger on why.
Gameplay:
The winner takes all, again and again and again.... This doesnt work very well. Shoot a few guys and upgrade your weapons and it gets ever easier to kill the other guys.... those guys that you allready demolished several times over. They lose their upgrades every time you kill them, making you (the winner) stronger and keeping them (the loser) weak. After a while it gets rather easy to kill the others because of this. I feel there should be something to even the odds, because once you lose, it's generally a downward spiral.
Not much fun for the losing guys, but not much of a challenge for the winning team either.
Bugs:
Quite often you will "jump" back and forth, putting you back in the smae spot several times. Seems laggy, but there is no connection spike, really weird.
The moneygrab:
The options to simply buy "skins" (stff that makes you better armed and armoured) is a cheap ploy though, making this a pay to win unfortunately.
In my book this brings the game down about a million nothces unfortunately.
Do I recommend it? For the few bucks it costs, yes. But only just; if the developers put some effort in this could be a great game. At the moment it's a mediocre game with a nice gimmick.
I hope it gets better, I reaaly, really do.

I played this game for 7 hours yesterday 9/12/2014 after purchasing it for 5 dollars.
I have 20 years of gaming experience, playing from the OG Hexxen and Doom up to the new Unreals and Far crys and everything in between. So take some of my comments on tactics or ways to play, coming from bringing old game knowledge into a new game with old gameplay style.
TL:DR If you don't like fast paced, twitch based combat, with no bullet drop, no lead time, and point and click weapons ALA unreal, or OG CS. you'll hate this game, because it will punish you for being a bad player. if you like those things and have always been good at them, enjoy your 23/0  score (hint: BH+SSG+Grenade = gg). The game is not completely finished! but has really tight controls and movement, feels like a solid game, and has lots of potential! Support these guys, they have created a really great hybrid. First off this game is SOOOO much fun! IF! you like twitch based shooters and MOBA esque gameplay smooshed together with a fun simplistic blocky style to it that keeps your attention focused on the action.  <---- If that turns you off, DON'T BUY IT!
You don't need to aim ahead, there is no bullet drop, quick scoping is a thing, and if your a high speed mofo, who used to love playing insta gib on unreal, playing snipers in this game will be cake, and will net you ALOT of profit.
MAJOR DISCLAIMER: This game is JUST barely out of early access, it's basically a beta right now. Meaning, there are alot of coming soon, and not implemented yet, for different upgrades and such on weapons and armors and what not. It literally says the build is like 0.5#### right now.
that being said IMHO it is totally worth 5 dollars, hell i would pay ten (provided i have the information i have now after playing it).
Gameplay and Asethetics: The graphics are simple, yet convey quite well what's going on, with the glow of weapons giving off an idea of your opponents weapon levels, and armor being able to usually distinguish what someone is wearing, if your willing to get that close. The ability to mix and match armor sets, as well as choose your own loadouts is very satisfying, as you get to compliment your weapon build with your armor build, getting things like +20% or +15% damage. You get to earn resources and craft your gear from blue prints. The progression is very satisfying.
Titan Mode: It starts, you have enough resource to craft one piece of armor, of three that you can wear. Helmet, Chestpiece, Leggings. You have your two weapons, and a extra item, grenade or mini gun turret.
So you immiedieatly go out to find your opponents and shoot/stab them to death. Did i mention their is melee!? So much fun.
Your titans have also spawned and are marching to meet in the middle of the map, you want to go put as much damage on your opponents titan as possible as an early pressure can really hurt them if they are not paying attention. Usually though, if both teams are somewhat competent or decent, or just paying attention. Both titans die quite quickly, then it goes into creep farming phase. In this phase, you want to kill the wee little creeps for crystals (which add +1 to your titans strength) and give you resources to upgrade your armors! (+20% health? yes pelase! 15% MOAR damage?! yes please!). Keep an eye out for the GOLDEN CREEP! when it dies and drops it's ONE golden resource the team to secure this immiedieatly gets +10 strength to their titan. When the timer ends for this phase, then it's back to tians smashing eachother and your (or hopefully the enemy teams) walls and eventually base. That is the game currently.
Current Game Balance IMHO: The overall balance is solid, with only a few weapons seeming kind of meh, and everything else feeling strong to use. The two main starter weapons are easily the strongest in the game sans snipers. but that depends on your skill level. Melee is strong, but low skill entry low ceiling, easy to kite.
I had a lot of fun playing this game. I highly recommend that everyone tries this game out!

Transistor is definitely one of the most unique video games I've ever played, and easily stands as my game of 2014. It's a linear, narrative-driven action RPG with a lush, beautiful and unique art style. It's the aesthetic of this game that hits you first; it looks incredible and obvious love and immense skill have gone into the hand-drawn environments, giving the game a very "textured" feel. Although the game is linear, the detailing in the art makes you feel like you could wander off the rails at any moment you choose.
The second thing that hits you with Transistor is the music. Employing moody, atmospheric trip-hop style soundscapes, Transistor's soundtrack is achingly beautiful and complements the melancholy story and cyberpunk visuals perfectly. The soundtrack is further enhanced by several incredible vocal performances by Ashley Barrett, who brings a languid, jazz-inflected feel to the songs. Not only does Ashley Barrett's voice add a poignant humanity to the music, it also enhances the story through its lyrics.
Speaking of story, this game employs a sparse narrative, creating a sense of roleplay by having you piece together events at the same pace Red does. This game does not hold your hand through the narrative and you'll have to read every scrap of lore, listen to every bit of dialogue and take in every cryptic clue in the song lyrics to help you make sense of Transistor's enigmatic narrative. This put some people off, but I personally loved it. This narrative pieceing makes it feel like the story unfolds organically, with any furthering of the narrative being a result of *your* actions, as opposed to have bits of story crammed down your throat when the game deems it necessary. It's a very Dark Souls-esque way of doing things and I loved it.
As to the narrative itself, I won't spoil it, but Transistor tells the story of Red, an enchanting singer in the city of Cloudbank whose voice has been taken from her, and a mysterious man whose soul (taking the form of computer data) has been trapped in the assassin's blade meant for you. Together, you undertake a journey to get revenge and find out what's happening to your city as it is overrun by aggressive robots known as "the process."
Now, on to gameplay. Transistor employs a mixture of real time combat and a pseudo-turn based system, whereby Red freezes time, chooses attacks to perform and then executes these actions at lightning speed. It's an interestng gimmick that allows you to deal with the often overwhelming number of enemies you'll face on your own. Where Transistor's gameplay really shines is in its "Function" system. Functions are essentially abilities that can be slotted as either passive or activated, granting passive buffs or usable abilities. However, each function can also be slotted as an upgrade to another function, augmenting it with different characteristics and buffs. This means that you have essentially endless variety in your ability loadouts, with each ability changing itself drastically depending on which other functions you pair it with. It's an elegant and extremely fun system, if a little poorly explained in-game, and it makes Transistor a very unique experience among action RPGs.
I could honestly wax lyrical about Transistor all day, but what it really comes down to is this; do you want an action RPG with a unique and inventive combat system that encourages creativity, visuals and sound design to die for, and a sparse, melancholy story that unfolds in a slow, organic manner? If not, don't buy this game.
If that sounds like your kettle of fish, then welcome to Cloudbank.

/windowed /noborder

I'd recommend this game to anyone who doesn't feel that every game must be beatable for the first time without dying.  Because, that's just not what Eryi's Action is all about.
Before you buy / play this game, you should know what you're getting into.
This is a troll puzzle / platformer.  It will kill you as most traps you don't see coming until they're sprung on you, and then you need to figure out a way past them.  Most of the time, this is easy.  Sometimes, the solutions could stomp you for a while - I ended up using a walkthrough to get past a few traps.
That said, I found this game quite fun, and the traps funny the first time they killed me.  Afterwards, I'd laugh at myself for falling for the same traps over and over after forgetting they're there, while I'd hurry from the checkpoint to the latest revealed trap.
My favorite traps are the multistage ones, where you think you have a way past them, but that just springs another trap :)
P.S.  This game is *not* one of those "tough as nails platformers."  Some parts are moderately hard, yes, but nothing close to what's required in the likes of Super Meat Boy, They Bleed Pixels, Electronic Super Joy, or Gianna Sisters.

There are a lot of poor, bad reviews out there from people who didn't put very much time into the game to actually try it out, so i wanted to make this review for those who don't want to miss out on a great game for it's price now and a potentially even better game down the road.
I played this game for 7 hours yesterday 9/12/2014 after purchasing it for 5 dollars.
I have 20 years of gaming experience, playing from the OG Hexxen and Doom up to the new Unreals and Far crys and everything in between. So take some of my comments on tactics or ways to play, coming from bringing old game knowledge into a new game with old gameplay style.
TL:DR If you don't like fast paced, twitch based combat, with no bullet drop, no lead time, and point and click weapons ALA unreal, or OG CS. you'll hate this game, because it will punish you for being a bad player. if you like those things and have always been good at them, enjoy your 23/0  score (hint: BH+SSG+Grenade = gg). The game is not completely finished! but has really tight controls and movement, feels like a solid game, and has lots of potential! Support these guys, they have created a really great hybrid. Thanks alot devs :)
First off this game is SOOOO much fun! IF! you like twitch based shooters and MOBA esque gameplay smooshed together with a fun simplistic blocky style to it that keeps your attention focused on the action.  <---- If that turns you off, DON'T BUY IT!
You don't need to aim ahead, there is no bullet drop, quick scoping is a thing, and if your a high speed mofo, who used to love playing insta gib on unreal, playing snipers in this game will be cake, and will net you ALOT of profit.
MAJOR DISCLAIMER: This game is JUST barely out of early access, it's basically a beta right now. Meaning, there are alot of coming soon, and not implemented yet, for different upgrades and such on weapons and armors and what not. It literally says the build is like 0.5#### right now.
that being said IMHO it is totally worth 5 dollars, hell i would pay ten (provided i have the information i have now after playing it).
Gameplay and Asethetics: The graphics are simple, yet convey quite well what's going on, with the glow of weapons giving off an idea of your opponents weapon levels, and armor being able to usually distinguish what someone is wearing, if your willing to get that close. The ability to mix and match armor sets, as well as choose your own loadouts is very satisfying, as you get to compliment your weapon build with your armor build, getting things like +20% or +15% damage. You get to earn resources and craft your gear from blue prints. The progression is very satisfying.
Titan Mode: It starts, you have enough resource to craft one piece of armor, of three that you can wear. Helmet, Chestpiece, Leggings. You have your two weapons, and a extra item, grenade or mini gun turret.
So you immiedieatly go out to find your opponents and shoot/stab them to death. Did i mention their is melee!? So much fun.
Your titans have also spawned and are marching to meet in the middle of the map, you want to go put as much damage on your opponents titan as possible as an early pressure can really hurt them if they are not paying attention. Usually though, if both teams are somewhat competent or decent, or just paying attention. Both titans die quite quickly, then it goes into creep farming phase. In this phase, you want to kill the wee little creeps for crystals (which add +1 to your titans strength) and give you resources to upgrade your armors! (+20% health? yes pelase! 15% MOAR damage?! yes please!). Keep an eye out for the GOLDEN CREEP! when it dies and drops it's ONE golden resource the team to secure this immiedieatly gets +10 strength to their titan. When the timer ends for this phase, then it's back to tians smashing eachother and your (or hopefully the enemy teams) walls and eventually base. That is the game currently.
Current Game Balance IMHO: The overall balance is solid, with only a few weapons seeming kind of meh, and everything else feeling strong to use. The two main starter weapons are easily the strongest in the game sans snipers. but that depends on your skill level. Melee is strong, but low skill entry low ceiling, easy to kite.

It's a bit on the short side (though the expansion does give some extra hours of fun) and the minion controls are a bit imprecise at times, but really. If you've ever wanted to be an evil overlord, command an army of minions willing to follow your every command and even die for you, build your dark castle of doom and make the villages of all those pesky fantasy creatures bow down before your iron fist, there is nothing quite like Overlord. The graphics are very nice and colorfull and have a lot of charm. The music is fitting and the minion-talk is still a running-gag among some of my friends. The best thing about the game though is probably its charm and humor.

Overlord: Raising Hell is a mix or real-time strategy and RPG where you are an awoken dark Overlord that rises up the stairs of might and power by controlling minion horde and rebuilding an own dark tower.
The gameplay consists mostly of 3 buttons - left mouse button for sending your minions to kill, destroy or use something, right mouse button to call them back to you and space bar for melee hitting enemies. Rarely, if your mana levels allow it, you are able to cast some spells. The story and gameplay develop really slow since you first have to gather different types of minion hives to even be able to progress in some areas. The story is not really making out a big picture, instead you mostly get a small mission when visiting an area from your older minion. The missions and areas are definetely enjoyable on their own, but putting them into a connected story would have been far cooler.
Since the combat is quite passive in Overlord because you mostly just have to wait for your minions to trash everything or at least let them charge and support them by casting spells or hitting some enemies from behind with melee attacks. The game definetely lacked challenge since you always have enough minions to crush all enemies and even if you let them die, there are always enough waiting in the hives. The further I got into the game, the easier it actually became since some objects increase your HP, Mana and forging weapons allows you to progress even quicker without breaking a sweat.
The graphic is neat - the minions look cute and evil at the same time. The humans have an oddly stupid look on them, besides the princess you will meet. The interface has almost no elements to keep it clean and the icons fit the play style of the game. Some areas are more detailed than others, especially if they are unique in the game. There are sadly barely any effects in the game, the game could use something more flashy.
The progress - as mentioned in the gameplay section - is quite slow since you have to ignore multiple areas / objects that you have to retract later once you get different types of minions that help you either solve puzzles or simply are the only one that can reach certain objects. After few hours the game started to feel a bit like its trying to look like it has more gameplay time than it actually does by letting you slowly run around areas that you have visited before already. There are multiple puzzles, that especially in mid and later game require some trying outs till you can figure out the correct way to solve it. Besides that you sometimes have to control a single unit to grab an item, multiple minions to perform a special action or kill an enemy you cant reach yourself.
The audio rarely felt impactful, mostly I was lacking audio feedback about my action. You still get a certain level of immersion, especially when playing with headphones and having all sounds on, but do not expect it to be some superior quality or give you any chills. Sound does its job, but sadly nothing more.
I would not call Overlord a classic, but some people definetely enjoyed it years ago. It is in my opinion a mediocre game that lacks a bigger story and action feeling. Still, it is enjoyable in its own way - being an evil overlord that commands hordes of cute minions is quite fun. There are multiple different looking areas where you also get the feeling of progressing in a different way, meeting different enemies and situations, killing some bosses. If you expect an awesome audio or graphic, deep story or total immersion, I would not suggest trying it, but if you enjoy oldschool simple but fun games, try it out.
I hope this review helps you making the decision if its worth buying this game. Rate and leave a comment if you enjoyed reading it.

Transistor is a top-down, turn-based adventure game that takes place in a utopian society. The gameplay is very different from Bastion; in this game, all attacks are planned beforehand during each turn. This game is beautiful to look at and holds a beautiful story within.
Pros:
+From the music, to the voice acting, to the writing, to the art, this game is beautifully executed. I like the gameplay, but this is definitely a game you buy for the music, story and artwork.
+The romance in this game felt genuine and believable to me.
+The gameplay is entertaining; different "functions" (attacks) can be combined in a multitude of combinations, and there are multiple ways to win each battle.
+Like Bastion, there is a new game plus mode where you can restart the game at a higher difficulty and continue levelling.
+For those who like the battles, there are bonus challenges, similar to Bastion.
Cons:
-While planning your turn, you can't pan the screen to look at far away enemies. This is a minimal problem, as you can usually see far enough anyways, and you can also simply walk where you want to see and then cancel the move.
This game took me ten hours to complete, but my girlfriend completed it in four hours, which I find amazing. I think most people will take at least six if not 7-8 hours.
I really loved this game. While they don't have the big budget of a AAA company, Supergiant has managed to craft something that is both more unique and more impressive than most AAA games.

This is my first review so it might not be the best.
Plague Inc: Evolved is a game whose ultimate aim is for you to destroy humanity. Think of it as a brain exercise for all the evil geniuses out there. You start with the lowly bacteria with "unlimited possibilities", and unlock other plagues as you destroy humanity time and again with the previous plagues. There are also a good number of powerups that you can "equip" your plague with. Each plague have their own unique properties, such as the virus being able to mutate easily (allowing the infected to show more symptoms, but ultimately useful in killing people off), and the fungus, which is difficult transmit across the globe. However, most of your plagues have similar transmission and symptomatic properties, making the game slightly repetitive.
What the game has added, however, is the neurax worm and the necroa virus. These two are completely new plagues and adds a different dimension to your gameplay, each with their unique transmission and symptoms. These are the kind of improvements and uniqueness that makes the player think more and come up with different strategies, especially with the necroa virus. The neurax worm seems slightly overpowered, but its quite hilarious what you can do with it.
Certain game modes are still unavailable in this game, but for a game still in Alpha, it can already compete with other, more established games out there. It might seem expensive, but trust me, it is worth every dollar. It is a game with unlimited replay value, unlike others that you might play once and never play it again.
Overall, a great game with bright prospects.

So play golf with an overweight halfling, mow the lawn with a chained-up Paladin and - perhaps my favourite of all - gate-crash an eye-wateringly terrible theatrical production about the Elven race. Where the original title kept things relatively straightforward, here we have a much greater array of creative puzzles and challenges, pushing minion control to new depths.
They've tried a new twist on crafting: Providing specific recipes for magical items with fixed abilities, as opposed to the open-ended style from before - though most, if not all, of these are quite forgettable and cannot rival fully-upgraded conventional kit.

This isn't a reveiw of the game as a whole. More a knock against Steam's horrible quality control for games that just don't work on modern systems. The old idea of a consoles best selling point of games just working when you push play, and PC games being better everywhere else but sometimes games might need some configuring, is well and alive here. I didn't go into this expecting Bloodrayne (all one word) a fifteen year old game to work on my modern-ish rig, but the amount of hoops you have to jump through to get it working is ridiculous and to have it still have bugs on top of that, is all kinds of bad. It really shouldn't be on steam, even if you see it on sale for $1 (as it always is every major sale) don't bother. Barring some person or the maybe (God willing!) the rights holders doing some serious retooling/dev work it shouldn't be a product for sale on Steam.
Bloodrayne (all one word) however is a favorite of mine. My short five hour nostalgia trip through this game for the first time in years was enjoyable. I remembered certain story beats, some fights, and my favorite part: The Guns! This was one of those games that had the whole gun-fu flip trick thing from the matrix going for it. Rayne equips two guns to shoot down the opposition and a cool auto aim feature makes it so Rayne can shoot two fools at once in opposite directions! Is that exciting!?! Doesn't that sound AWESOME!?!
But yeah its kinda dated now. Your mileage may vary with this game and if you read this far then, hey. You should know not to buy it anyways.

You play as a giant stone ball (with various faces inscribed) and you must roll through the levels while avoiding opponent laid obstacles to stay intact enough to smash into the enemy fortress gate.  Each time your stone ball is destroyed and must be rebuilt.  You use the downtime to purchase and place defenses because your enemy is rolling his/her giant ball at your gate. The first person to break the gate and roll over the tiny person inside wins.
Interspersed throughout the game are massive boss encounters such as the giant winged baby head or a giant Michealangelo's David statue (which you must of course smash in the fig leaf). This helps break up the gameplay a little with unique experiences often involving some laughs.
It's a great little title that smashes art history, mythology and humor together for great fun. Can't recommend this enough at sale time. You'll always get your value's worth.

The Room is a fun puzzle game. The game essentially boils down to flipping switches, turning knobs, and pushing buttons on various puzzle boxes that progress some weirdo occult story. The puzzles weren't too challenging, but I got stuck a few times for a little bit during the 4 hours it took to finish the game. This game is probably more fun on a tablet as interaction with elements of the puzzles was definitely designed with touch controls in mind. The mouse is moved to simulate swipes and it's a little clunky, but still functional. I'll certainly play its sequels if they're ever ported to PC.

I quite enjoyed it, myself.
The combination of puzzles, occult themes and audio reminded me of something akin to the Hellraiser books/movies, which I confess a deep love for. (Well, the first two anyway.)
Albeit with less sense of impending agony as reward for their solution.
The story itself is not terribly deep so I imagined it as if Philip Lemarchand moved up from creating the smaller puzzle boxes like the Lament Configuration to larger, deeper mysteries.
Aside from my own morbid film nostalgia though, I found it to be a decent little puzzler.
The puzzles themselves are beautifully ornate with rich textures.
I did run into one issue with one of the puzzles, which apparently was intended for tablet which requires the tablet to be shaken or turned or something-or-other?...
Being on a PC, I confess I had to look up what was up with that step, because I thought I hit a bug or something.
However I did end up managing to get it to agree with my mouse clicks when I repositioned myself and clicked again.
It was really stumping me at first though, not being on a tablet.
Took about 3 hours for me to 100% the 5 achievements.

Pros:

Cons:

If you can get it cheap and have a lot of patience go for it. Otherwise move on and save your money.

I bought "Papers, Please" without any information about it but that you are checking passports (I didn't even watch gameplays or screens). I heard one opinion about it - I asked my friend "Is >>Papers, Please<< good?" and he said "Yes". Really. But I decided to purchase it. It wasn't really cheap, I bought e.g. Witcher 3 in my country for about 22 euro on premiere but, fortunately, I had money from all CSGO skins I sold.
Sorry for this ♥♥♥♥♥♥ talking but I want you to realize that it's good to buy a game for other genre of games you usually play because maybe, just like I did, you'll find a game that you'll love.
I will tell you the story in the shortest way as possible. You are an immigrate inspector. You are living in a communist country called Arstotzka. You have to feed your family (you, wife, son, uncle, aunt). After checking each passport you gain $5 (let's say you use dollars in this game) and after detaining each two people you obtain $5 too. You don't have much time so you have to do it quickly. But it is not as easy as you think! First few days in this game are pretty easy (e.g. people who live in Arstotzka can get through and immigrants can't) but last are hard. People are trying to deceive you using even forged seals or they put different date on two documents (you have to check up to five (?) documents). You have to spend your payment well everyday - medicine, heat, food. But this is rather easy part of this game.
The hardest thing is to decide who will cross the border. It is just psychological. An old woman from Kolechia (terrorist country from which come suicide bombers) is asking you to cross the border because she didn't see her son for months and her passport is expired. She is really credible but you know it's risky. What will you do? Now imagine the moment when a guy with a mask gives you encrypted list of people from organisation which "wants to finish this terror in this communist country". It is risky because you can do only two mistakes per day. What will you do? Maybe you'll change something into better? And the clock is is ticking: tick, tock, tick, tock. Choose the right side! Your choices are extremally important. There are about 20 endings of this game.
This game has only two problems:
First: you won't play it all the time just before sleeping to anti-stress yourself after (and before :( ) school or work. But maybe you are a type of a guy (just like me) who doesn't stop playing this game. However, I think this is not a good game if you have good mood. Second thing is resolution. While you're playing on fullscreen, it's only a small part of your monitor. I didn't even notice it until I finished this game but I wanted to point it. Maybe you care about small things like that.
So, have fun!
Regards,

Eryis Action is what is right about this type of platformer. By the type I mean the tough as nails and brutal sort which repeatedly hits you again and again and yet, somehow still has you coming back for more punishment. In this game everything is trying to kill you from the obvious (Spikes, Enemies, Lava) to the non obvious such as windmills falling apart as you walk under them, blocks that throw spikes out without warning, traps to stop you from finishing the level unless you play smart.
And thats the key thing here, smarts. Yes, some trial and error is involved but that is the reason you are given unlimited lives yes? The way through is simple and thats this. Dont think this as a platformer game. Thats only going to keep you angry, fustrated and at times totally unable to move along. Instead think of this as a PUZZLE title as soon certain things keep appearing, certain areas become noticeable as you go along and on reaching new areas, you already have a good idea on what to do and not to do.
Thinking this as a puzzle title also helps when the game gets to its most brutal ways and can have you thinking of alternate solutions, ideas and 'experiements' Does this go here? What would happen if I made this do this and so on. It works brilliantly and I find it so much more fun thinking of it this way!
The controls are fine, nothing to comment on. Precise enough when you get the hang of them and usually if you fall into an open pit (one that hasnt just appeared out of nowhere that is), its your own fault, not the game. The graphics too are bright, colourful and pretty to look at. Okay though... some of the backgrounds are a bit dull but thats about it.
Essentially: Not a Platformer - Its a Puzzle. Think that way. Go in too with a 'Screw you game! You cant beat me!' attitude along with a never give up one and you are definetly going to have a good time.

I'm just about the right age (late 20s) for the format to be incredibly nostalgic for me, so it had points right away there. (I used to spend so much time on AIM.)
When I realized that you type out the messages by hitting keys, I thought that was kind of cool. It's kind of fun to just type randomly like a guy playing a "hacker" on some dumb TV show, randomly mashing keys and somehow making stuff happen anyway.
The story takes some interesting turns. I've only played it through twice, (I was curious how certain choices would lead to different outcomes.) Some of the changes were really interesting, though the story still followed a similar enough format that I wasn't interested in seeking out all the different versions. (I feel like it could get tedious after more than a couple playthroughs.) So that could be a point against it.
All in all, though, I liked it a lot! The conversations felt very authentic, and it was full of nice little touches (you can see the lives of the other characters, including people who never factor into your and Emily's little drama, progress and change if you read their profiles each year.) It's up to you as the player to interpret whether you or Emily might be being manipulative, or whether you're both just a couple of emotional teens/twentysomethings who are just being your messed up selves.
I entered my own name, and since I'm female it added another little wrinkle to the story that made me enjoy it a lot more, personally.
Anyway, it's free to play and one playthrough takes just a few minutes, so the novelty alone makes it worth a rec in my book.

Eryi's Action is an unfair, occasionally brutal platformer...and I wouldn't have it any other way. While challenging, it is still beatable and you will start to learn the tricks before they appear. Get it if you like a truly difficult platformer

Eryi's Action is exactly what's wrong about tough-as-nails platformers. It's entire foundation exists merely to frustrate and aggravate you as quickly and cheaply as possible. That ordinary looking patch of grass? Spikes. Those previously stable boxes? They disappear now. That completely empty piece of space right where you need to jump? There's actually a box there to bump into. You can't even select a level without an enemy jumping out to kill you, or pass the end flag without a spike dropping on your head.
This isn't clever, and this isn't fun; it's cheap and annoying trial and error with no explanation or point at all. Everything unfolds like a bad Loonytoons sketch, where Eryi dying is the butt of every joke, and nobody is laughing. Sending the sinking ship into the abyss is the poor presentation, consisting of simply drawn barely animated sprites, blurry backgrounds, and abysmal music. Controls are stiff and your character floaty as if she's constantly trying to walk on ice, which only adds to the ridiculous difficulty imposed on you.
If the developers sole intention was to make a game that was an unforgiving lesson in frustrating, well they absolutely succeeded. I somehow made it through three levels before realizing that there was no way I hated myself enough to finish it. This is hot trash which wouldn't cut it as a free flash game, but as something released on Steam you are expected to pay for it is simply insulting and you should stay far, far away. If only Nyu Media had done the same.

I found the premise of The Room very intriguing. The idea of mysterious, intricately built mechanical puzzle boxes hiding unimaginable secrets appeals to me greatly, probably because of my love for Lovecraftian tales of revelation, and my liking for the puzzle box concept in Clive Barker's Hellraiser stories (of course The Room is not a horror per se, but that's okay). The progression gave me a good sense of achievement, although it was a bit linear; then again it would be silly to deviate from linearity given the game style - successive solving of the intricate puzzles which lead you onto the next step of the larger puzzle.
Sometimes the camera angle became frustrating; I was tempted to look around the environment surrounding the puzzle's focus because I was quite eager to soak in as much atmosphere as possible; I wanted to approach those things in the background but couldn't. Perhaps the developers could flesh out a slightly more interactive environment around the puzzle-focus, some sugary fun around the meat of the puzzle itself, for those of us who would like to explore the environment around the puzzle, perhaps even little mini puzzles around the main one for those who like to explore.
I was disappointed when the game ended; it was too soon. I hungered for more. I did obtain the game on special, so I did not feel cheated regarding the price vs length ratio. All in all, this gets a firm thumbs up. I would love to play much more of this sort of thing. I heard there was a chance that sequels would not be distributed via Steam on PC which would be such a terrible shame. I play games on PC and refuse to pay much - if anything - for gaming on mobile devices, since mobile devices cannot offer a fraction of the same quality of atmosphere that a pc or even a laptop can. Please release sequels (all of them) on Steam for PC.
Yours faithfully

TL;DR - Easily the best open world game of any kind available in the last decade. Period. So much so that it actually redefines an entirely new standard of the potential of the genre. It's the first time I have played something that feels "new" in years. This is the standard. This is the open world action game you have been waiting for. Forget GTA, forget Saints Row, forget Just Cause, this is it. All of those games are fine, this one simply puts them to shame by showing what they could be.
I didn't want to do this. I knew it would end up being long and this review is still incomplete. In some ways I am sad to play this game. It clearly shows the potential of the genre in ways that completely shame every other attempt. In so doing it also sets the bar so high that I can't imagine a follow up or spiritual successor doing anything but failing. Even so, for now I can live in ignorant bliss and enjoy the completely insane experience to the full. If you think you have felt a rush in-game before, wait until you take the police bike through Hong Kong at full speed weaving through traffic like you always wanted to. This game WILL make you smile.
Every time I play it I can't believe it. I can't believe this isn't the only game being talked about and I can't believe anyone even has interest in GTA or its many clones. Sleeping Dogs does so well what other games fail to do so consistently that it really puts them to absolute shame. I have not played a game in many years that seems to be something entirely new, entirely on its own and I hesitate to say it now but this game is that good.
The mini-games alone are better than most standalone titles. The racing is the most exhilarating and fun I have played in years. Also, if you don't like your car just jump to another one! I have never been without a useful vehicle in this game unlike every other. The hacking and stealth mini-games are more fun than most indie titles completely devoted to the material. The graphics are incredible, truly amazing to look at. The acting is even good with somewhat believable cinematics, something basically unheard of these days.
The main character is great with a well-developed personality and believable dialog and the world is highly immersive. This may be its biggest feature. Saints row is filled with targets, GTA is filled with dummy NPC pylons, Just Cause has inconsequential set pieces that vanish the second you turn around. Sleeping Dogs has a world that is immersive and has loads of character. In addition, the cops don't chase you for hours on end the second you start to have fun. This is another great feature; unless you smash a guys face directly next to a cop you will probably not be chased and the chases end quickly with AI making very real driving mistakes. Some might say it’s a bit easy but I think it strikes the perfect balance and difficulty curve ensuring maximum fun is had while keeping the player interested and engaged BUT without holding their hand or yelling at them the entire time.
This game also spins most glitches and oddball occurrences in the player’s favor; everything that goes wrong makes it more fun. It’s the gameplay of Saints Row, with the beautiful world of GTA, with a story I haven't enjoyed this much since Heavy Rain, and a world filled with an entirely unique character complimented by a highly rewarding fighting system that is miles better than any Arkham game it keeps getting compared to.
Easily one of the best games I have played in years. I laugh hysterically every time I play at the insane things that happen. I played Far Cry 4 for about an hour. I’ll play it eventually but that was enough to get a feel. I have not been able to put this game down. Most open world games hope for a "gestalt" factor where all the crappy parts make something enjoyable. Sleeping Dogs does the same thing but it is the only example that shows the potential for many excellently executed individual parts making a whole that can hardly be described.
Play this game. Play it now.

Sleeping Dogs might just be a better GTA-style game than the GTA series itself. Now maybe it's just the location, but my oh my, Hong Kong is a lively and beautiful setting contrary to Los Santos in GTA V. Lights, cars, people... everywhere. However, what this game lacks is traffic. That might sounds stupid, but traffic, in my eyes, helps to convey the atmosphere of a busy city, as a New Yorker myself. Mind you this is only a personal request and the lack of which does not take away much. Traffic or no traffic, Hong Kong is still amazing.
Speaking of beauty, the textures, for the most part, are very detailed. I say for the most part because often you will find a stray texture that looks horrid in comparison to the ones around it, such as the door to Wei's apartment, as an example. The models for the main characters look great, especially when you can appreciate them up-close in real-time cutscenes. The voice-acting is great too, but the facial animations are pretty mediocre. Lips are synchronized and that's great and all, but the rest of the facial muscles aren't very expressive. Lighting effects convey a vibrant and realistic setting and the reflections are accurate and organic. And the rain.. (OH THE BEAUTIFUL RAIN)... I cannot get enough of the rain, let's just say that. Colors, wetness, all around me... I like it ( ͡° ͜ʖ ͡°).
And while we're still talking about beauty let me just point out that Sleeping Dogs looks better and runs wayyy better than Watch Dogs. Sleeping Dogs gets an average of 40 fps on my GT 755M and that's on pretty high settings. This is a perfectly playable framerate and serves as a happy medium between 30 and 60 fps. There a few bugs like sometimes not being able to attach to cover for a few seconds in certain spots or a civilian getting stuck in geometry, but these don't really affect your gameplay experience.
Hong Kong offers a lot to do: you can buy pork buns, other food, get a massage, and do side quests like stealing a car for someone, distracting the cops, or other various activities. Cars offer great arcade-like style, but sometimes it could feel like you're driving on ice which sometimes gets annoying. But there's a mechanic I've never seen in another game: action hijack. This feature, which lets you hijack another vehicle while driving, emphasizes the Asian-action movie vibe this game successfully accomplishes.
While on the topic of action movie, by every mechanic you can see that this is the style the developers were going for. The combat system is wonderfully satisfying and complex in that you can upgrade it to earn new moves and skills such as a leg break or a roundhouse kick. Another mechanic which emphasizes the action-movie vibe is bullet-time. Just like in Max Payne, you can enter slow-motion to do some next-level-human stuff to ultimately wreck your enemies. In Sleeping Dogs this can be triggered by vaulting over cover and aiming or by aiming at enemies while driving. In one side mission, more than 100 motorcyclists were shooting at me consecutively while I was riding shotgun in a car, delivering dope, as gangsters do.
In open world games, the story might be a trivial path for some players for its usual mediocrity. However, in Sleeping Dogs, this is not the case. The plot is surprisingly well-written and interesting. It involves Wei Shen, an undercover cop who is becoming too attached to his gangster role. The story, while not as amazing as, let's say: The Last of Us, is still much better than average and is certainly worth playing through.
Overall, Sleeping Dogs is an open-world game done right. With an interesting story, great use of freedom, challenging yet satisfying combat system, bullet time, and decent driving, you can't go wrong. Sleeping Dogs is a standout in the genre and a game that melds many features in a manner which works.

I suppose it's time for me to review this.
Well, I haven't been playing this for a year (I started late October of 2016). I was invited and got curious. Apparently, I have few accounts to observe further the mechanics of the game. Gameplay-wise, the game is impressive, as most abilities require ability or skill to predict and hit (Nu Wa's ult is the hardest. Kidding.), and only a few, counted abilities can be considered as auto-target/lock target or whatever you call such abilities (Neith's ult, Ao Kuang's ult). Graphics-wise, in the subjective point of view, I'll say that this is easy in the eyes and comfortable to play with (as I played MMORPGs of similar graphic quality), but objectively, I would say the game is quite behind, as most games nowadays tries to acquire the 'realistic' looks, or similar to that (for example, Paragon, which is another MOBA/ARTS that I like, though I still prefer SMITE). Developer-wise, I'd say Hi-Rez Studios made a great job in maintaining this game, despite the issues regarded by the gaming community (balance) and the religious community (the Hindu issue).
The factors to be stated below can be considered optional, depending on the reader:
-Player base: SMITE has a high player base, with a few thousands in Steam and more players from the external client. The player count can be considered impressive and the game is functional as queue durations only last for a short while.
-Community: Surprisingly, after creating approximately 3 accounts (pardon me), I find the lower-levelled players more toxic and immature than the older and veteran players, regarding Casual gaming AND Ranked gaming. So, if you want matured and respectable allies, I suppose you should rush your levels.
-The Gods: Not much issue here at all, except for the few balancing issues from the previous patches and patch notes. Some gods, in my subjective view, seemed to have lost their purpose in the battlefield, and some gods have buggy effects (one of which is The Morrigan, whose ultimate sometimes needs to be clicked 2 to 3 times (in my case, in Instant Casting) to activate.
-The Skins and Cosmetics: Not much of an issue here as well. Some are poorly designed; some are amazingly designed; some are just right.
-DLCs and Purchasable Goods: This is one of the best traits of SMITE: the Goods and DLCs. SMITE has an in-game currency, the Favor, which can rent or purchase gods in the discretion of the account owner. Favor can be received through playing, either victory or defeat. In such case, one could say that this game is not Pay-to-Win, as the cosmetics and DLCs have no direct effect to the gameplay.
A lot more can be say to the game, but I'll consider only some of the factors. Enjoy gaming!

This is my first review so it might not be the best.
Plague Inc: Evolved is a game whose ultimate aim is for you to destroy humanity. Think of it as a brain exercise for all the evil geniuses out there. You start with the lowly bacteria with "unlimited possibilities", and unlock other plagues as you destroy humanity time and again with the previous plagues. There are also a good number of powerups that you can "equip" your plague with. Each plague have their own unique properties, such as the virus being able to mutate easily (allowing the infected to show more symptoms, but ultimately useful in killing people off), and the fungus, which is difficult transmit across the globe. However, most of your plagues have similar transmission and symptomatic properties, making the game slightly repetitive.
What the game has added, however, is the neurax worm and the necroa virus. These two are completely new plagues and adds a different dimension to your gameplay, each with their unique transmission and symptoms. These are the kind of improvements and uniqueness that makes the player think more and come up with different strategies, especially with the necroa virus. The neurax worm seems slightly overpowered, but its quite hilarious what you can do with it.
Certain game modes are still unavailable in this game, but for a game still in Alpha, it can already compete with other, more established games out there. It might seem expensive, but trust me, it is worth every dollar. It is a game with unlimited replay value, unlike others that you might play once and never play it again.
Overall, a great game with bright prospects.

A game with a visual style reminiscent of the Terry Gilliam cartoons in Monty Python's Flying Circus. In Rock of Ages, you face off against various historical nemeses, such as Vlad the Impaler and Cardinal Richelieu. It's a mix of bowling, pinball and tower defence, if that makes any sense. It has things in common with gaming classics, such as Marble Madness, in that you control a ball rolling downhill under gravity. In the case of Rock of Ages, the ball is a rock, and there are various types of rock, with power-ups to help you on your way, plus you have the ability to jump. The aim is to amass score by smashing into things, but hitting the wrong things results in the rock getting crushed and flaking into an ever smaller boulder, with less mass. It really is a lot of fun and hilariously funny at times. It even has split-screen and a competitive mode, where you can build defences to counter and block your oponent's  progress.

Rock of ages is a game about rolling down a hill; to squish a little man, literally.
In Rock of Ages, there is a very minor story, hardly relating to the game. This isnt a bad thing because the game doesn't need a story to be enjoyed, however the story is humorous.
The core gameplay aspect of Rock of Ages is rolling your rock down a slope riddled with defences in order to smash down an enemy gate. The opponents, are not only people from history, also attack your gate and the player must build their own defences in order to slow down or stop the other rock. You gain in game gold in order to pay for defences, and to upgrade your rock.
The defences range from towers, elephants, catapults and even bombs. These are used to slow down the enemy rock, if enough damage is done to the rock, it shrinks, dealing less damage. The upgrades for your rock are simple, adding metal spikes or lighting your rock on fire, dealing extra damage. Damage is also decided by the speed of the rock when it collides with the door; the faster the rock, the harder it hits.
Rock of ages also has a few mini games, one of which is skeeball. Rock of ages also has trading cards, and very easy achievements, making the game apply to a larger audience.
Rock of Ages does things right
Its story is humorous
The gameplay is overall enjoyable
Easy 100% achievements
The co-op is good fun with friends
The mini games are mostly fun
The in game destruction looks good
Its overall very original
Rock of ages does some things wrong
It can be repetitive
Slightly boring to some older gamers
The Defences aren't overly effective
The respawn locations can really mess with the player
Lacks real substance
Overall rock of ages isn't bad, it's just basic. The $10.99(CAD) price tag is way too high unless the player is planning to 100% it. Its a fun game to play with friends, however. It also makes the game lots more fun.
If this game is exactly what you are looking for, get it. If you wonder if it is the right choice, avoid it.

Transistor is a story driven blend of the RPG/Hack and Slash genres; it features an interesting skill mechanic where your sword is like a hard drive and you install abilities based on how much memory you have left. You have actives; which are the skills you interact with in battle. Passives; which occur by default constantly and Upgrades which you can use to bolster your actives with additional effects.
Any of the functions can be used in any of the three categories and do different things based on where you utilise them and what functions you combine together. This sounds a lot more complicated than it actually is but you would need to do it once or twice before you got the hang of what you want your actives and the like to achieve.
While in combat you have the opportunity to into a kind of pause-state. This allows you to plan out and chain together moves up to a cap; each active takes up memory(some more so than others) so you will have to manage your skills in this state carefully to maximise damage or efficiency. These take place before the proccesses (antagonists) get a chance to retaliate giving you that blink of an eye feeling.
Beautiful art style; interesting mechanics/story and edgy beyond all reason. Definitely worth a play if you're on the fence.

-"Memory" Mechanic
-Unique art style
-Interesting story and characters

-They could have fleshed out the main character(s) more but that's mainly because she/they are such  interesting concepts in the first place

A dark, oppressive and tense game about terrorism, security, doing your job and keeping some shred of humanity all while you process immigration paperwork.

A mechanically simple game that contains enormous depth.  Sorting and stamping papers can get hectic and stressful, but it's the moral choices that are the real challenge.  You can overlook a discrepancy to allow a wife return to her husband, but if you can't afford medicine for your family then you have to realistically consider having her jailed and use the commission to pay for treatment.
Papers, Please puts you in many of these scenarios and stretches your ability to act in a moral way.  You will eventually realise that some situations cannot be resolved without something horrible happening to someone - and you are the pivotal deciding factor.  A lot of time is spent afterwards justifying the decision to yourself.
A very unique game that provides insight on how people can act in terrible ways, and how anyone, under the appropriate circumstances would act the same, including you.

I have played the original Sleeping Dogs quite a bit since 2013 and it has grown to be one of my favorite games of all time. So much so that I figured it would be a crime if I did not buy the new Definitive Edition. After play for an hour, I have to say that I am impressed by the Definitive Edition. Right off the bat, the menu is ultra-sharp, even in 1920x1080p. Even the menu sounds and menu music quality have been improved! The introduction is better than ever; I had an absolute BLAST with the new destruction mechanics in the beginning chase and fights. I threw an enemy at a cabinet and the drawers of the cabinet actually came out and papers flew out. Then, I slammed a metal gate in the market on top of an enemy and it actually bent in the middle. This kind of stuff never happened before... I love it! The electronic street signs have been improved (all the textures too) to make Hong Kong look better than ever. The rain effects look phenomenal, and I have realized that the map, loading dragon, in-game floating HUD icons, etc. are almost 4k sharp. Many other elements of the game have been improved as well
If you already have Sleeping Dogs and love it to death (and have extra money), get it. If you have not played it at all, get it. If you already have the Definitive Edition, play it! :)

Transistor is a story driven blend of the RPG/Hack and Slash genres; it features an interesting skill mechanic where your sword is like a hard drive and you install abilities based on how much memory you have left. You have actives; which are the skills you interact with in battle. Passives; which occur by default constantly and Upgrades which you can use to bolster your actives with additional effects.
Any of the functions can be used in any of the three categories and do different things based on where you utilise them and what functions you combine together. This sounds a lot more complicated than it actually is but you would need to do it once or twice before you got the hang of what you want your actives and the like to achieve.
While in combat you have the opportunity to into a kind of pause-state. This allows you to plan out and chain together moves up to a cap; each active takes up memory(some more so than others) so you will have to manage your skills in this state carefully to maximise damage or efficiency. These take place before the proccesses (antagonists) get a chance to retaliate giving you that blink of an eye feeling.
Beautiful art style; interesting mechanics/story and edgy beyond all reason. Definitely worth a play if you're on the fence.
Pros
-"Memory" Mechanic
-Unique art style
-Interesting story and characters
-Can be quite challenging at times
Cons
-None to really speak of; it is only the story so I can't see too many people putting in 50+ hours into it
-They could have fleshed out the main character(s) more but that's mainly because she/they are such  interesting concepts in the first place

A dark, oppressive and tense game about terrorism, security, doing your job and keeping some shred of humanity all while you process immigration paperwork.

A mechanically simple game that contains enormous depth.  Sorting and stamping papers can get hectic and stressful, but it's the moral choices that are the real challenge.  You can overlook a discrepancy to allow a wife return to her husband, but if you can't afford medicine for your family then you have to realistically consider having her jailed and use the commission to pay for treatment.
Papers, Please puts you in many of these scenarios and stretches your ability to act in a moral way.  You will eventually realise that some situations cannot be resolved without something horrible happening to someone - and you are the pivotal deciding factor.  A lot of time is spent afterwards justifying the decision to yourself.
A very unique game that provides insight on how people can act in terrible ways, and how anyone, under the appropriate circumstances would act the same, including you.

Nostalgia trip, and remembering why this game was fun.
A) Dismemberment and gibbing things.
B) Feeling like an immortal beastie grabbing the nearest Capri Sun of blood.
C) Physics of an appreciable kind.
And the things that sucked.
A) Saving only occurs at the start of a level. Even if you save during the level, it notifies you that it will start the level again at that save.
B) Inconsistent attacks on enemies. I.e. melee attacking one guy, kill him in one hit. Melee attack another, and it takes the entire string. And they're both basic grunts.
C) Inconsistent healing on enemies. I theorize their remaining health affects this, but if it does it makes elite enemies completely stupid since they're immune to it all the way up until they're a step away from death.
D) Ammo is surprisingly lacking despite every enemy with a gun dropping said gun on death. I.e. fully automatic weapons but you only get one clip max.
E) Cutscene issues. (This could be something I did that I didn't need to do, but gonna leave it since it's something mentioned by others)
And the things that are eh.
A) Aiming is automated. This is both okay and not okay. Okay is when there are enemies in opposite directions, and this allows you to shoot in both. Not okay is when you're trying to aim for a specific enemy, and Rayne's ability to aim at unseen enemies.
B) The aura sight. Allows you to see the objective and enemy health bars. But essentially makes you have the vision of someone who forgot their prescription glasses.
C) From the few levels I've played, human enemies are in the minority. And it's weird to hear lewd bloodsucking noises when the thing you're bloodsucking from is a mutilated walking corpse/puppet.
D) Bloodrage turns you into a harbinger of Death. Good. You can turn it off and conserve it. Good. You have to be at maximum charge to even use it. Bad.
tl;dr - Game is flawed but it scratches that itch to be a monster in human form. Recommended to those who enjoy the novelty of living the violent dhampire life.

Your reward? An ugly pile of mediocrity and palpable budget cuts.
Bloodrayne starts off strong. And then, after an extended period of boredom, it even ends off strong. But for every smart piece of dialogue, genuinely well done setpiece or interesting idea there's fundamental design flaws, lack of polish and jank that just prevents this from being worth playing.
Most games are frontloaded, starting with their best content and gradually petering out. Bloodrayne reverses this trend, starting you in a reasonably alright level, then flatlining into 4 hours of spamming melee attacks in long concrete corridors, with 3 enemy types and more reused generic assets than a Greenlight game, before packing all the best content in the end.
Throughout this, the plot is great. As in stupid. Your thrice-dead mentor leads you on a wild goose chase after a villian in search of a demon's lost body bits. You get KKK-decked occult priests preaching and flirtatious colonel twins toting one arm and ninja stars. When Bloodrayne indulges the absurdity, it's at its best.
There's something inherently funny about genderbending Dr. Mengele and giving him a massive rack.
But this is kept back from one fatal flaw in its incredible b-movie glory: it's not fun.
The camera spazzes out so much it's nauseating. It can't cope with the interior areas and will jerk back and forth as it struggles to navigate the environment, which is always. Melee "combos" are nonexistent, there's just a series of attacks that mostly trigger in whatever order they feel like while you fish for a decapitation.
Hit detection is a shot in the dark. It quickly devolves into pseudo-QWOP, throwing your limp fish of a half-vampire into the fray and dancing about while hoping that decapitation RNGesus favours you. Ranged isn't much of an option due to the absurd ammo limits.
Bosses are so damage spongey and ridiculously offensive that they quickly just turn into puzzles into how to cheese them. Perhaps this time you'll spam Rage mode, or abuse their terrible tracking to chip away at them from the back. Perhaps you'll just one-shot them with a rocket launcher. They range from disappointing to infuriating with no inbetween.
You can try gamepad or keyboard, it's not fun on either.
Despite this core inability to be a fun game, I was almost warming up to Bloodrayne. After hours of aggressively boring me into a hole, it suddenly opened up. A litany of airstrike avoiding, mech combat, open-arena platforming that gets vertical and takes advantage of Rayne's ludicrous jump height, I was ready to like it as a flawed gem.
But then the final boss happened and annoyed me so much that I never want to see the game again.
Bloodrayne is a crippled game that reaches for the stars and fails to even get off the floor.
If the idea of a ridiculous grindhouse title appeals to you regardless of the gameplay, feel free to give it a look. But to people who see a pile of rusty razorblades and don't think to stick their hand in because there's some chocolate underneath:
I'd advise moving on, and leaving Rayne in 2002.

Like a lot of ACE games, Rock of Ages is a diamond in the rough, and well worth the price of admission (especially how often it's on sale and how deeply discounted).
The premise is fairly simple: you roll a giant boulder through an obstacle course trying to mash in a set of gates at the opposite gate.
It has a great sense of humor, interesting graphics, and mechanics that are at least something different.
In my opinion the only downside is the combination of building defenses for your opponent along with trying to run through theirs: you can only place obstacles while you're waiting for your next boulder and this is also the only time you can try and pinpoint-catapult the enemy. Annoyingly, the computer opponents in single player seem to be able to catapult you the entire time (because of course) and have ridiculous accuracy, which can be frustrating.
So it's not perfect, but it's often only a few dollars, and is easily worth that, if not quite a few more.

I'm just about the right age (late 20s) for the format to be incredibly nostalgic for me, so it had points right away there. (I used to spend so much time on AIM.)
When I realized that you type out the messages by hitting keys, I thought that was kind of cool. It's kind of fun to just type randomly like a guy playing a "hacker" on some dumb TV show, randomly mashing keys and somehow making stuff happen anyway.
The story takes some interesting turns. I've only played it through twice, (I was curious how certain choices would lead to different outcomes.) Some of the changes were really interesting, though the story still followed a similar enough format that I wasn't interested in seeking out all the different versions. (I feel like it could get tedious after more than a couple playthroughs.) So that could be a point against it.
All in all, though, I liked it a lot! The conversations felt very authentic, and it was full of nice little touches (you can see the lives of the other characters, including people who never factor into your and Emily's little drama, progress and change if you read their profiles each year.) It's up to you as the player to interpret whether you or Emily might be being manipulative, or whether you're both just a couple of emotional teens/twentysomethings who are just being your messed up selves.
I entered my own name, and since I'm female it added another little wrinkle to the story that made me enjoy it a lot more, personally.
Anyway, it's free to play and one playthrough takes just a few minutes, so the novelty alone makes it worth a rec in my book.

So I have a rough time figuring out how I feel about this game.

The combat, the music, the environment were all beautiful. The character design was striking and really I can't say how much I enjoy playing the game for what it is. I enjoy the narration to, which comes from your sword, though sometimes his commentary is pretty empty or generic. I feel a lot more could have been done there.
My problem here is the story and the characters.
A lot of this game is ambigious and parts of it are meant to be. However too much of it is. We don't know a lot of the things our characters would, concepts and ideas are brought up but we never get a decent explanation. I feel like knowing what the 'country' is would be nice. I mean it could be implied to be death, or it could be people logging out of the virtual world...which is confusing.
Some text in game makes it sound like many people are dying, yet other commentary makes it seem like people might have just left. Afterall it seems the world is virtual...to some extent. It makes you wonder about how it all works. Yet this is never really explored. I get wanting things to be mysterious, but in thise case it feels like it would just be basic information. Maybe it's not too important though....
Afterall this is a love story in the end, but I think things could have been done to make the player feel more satisified with the ending and more invested in the characters. While the story isn't terrible by any means, it feels like we could have seen a lot more interesting interactions, explored what this utopia was really like and made it all feel more meaningful.
To me though...the game was fun, I did like the style and while the characters weren't all that fleshed out I did want to know about them and I did end up caring about what happened to the two main characters.
