I wasn't initially that interested in this game, but I fancied something a little different to what I usually play and it was a cheap alpha version of a new indie game.  After playing it a few times, I have to say that it is incredibly addictive.  And don't worry about it being in alpha, this is probably the most stable alpha I've ever played.  It is only in alpha because it is currently lacking a few of the game's final features, such as the lack of a tutorial.
When you first start playing you only have access to the basic
type plague that has no special advantages but also no specific disadvantage either, an ideal place to start.  If you can wipe out humanity on Normal difficulty or above, you unlock the next type of plage, the
+ one of 25 genetic modification codes that can apply additional attributes to your plague at the start of a new game.  Then if you can beat
on Normal or above you unlock the next type of plague + another genetic modification code etc. etc. until you have unlocked all plauge types and genetic codes giving you the ultimate in flexibility.
There are four difficulty modes, Easy, Normal, Brutal and Extra Brutal (these might not be the actual names but you get the idea) and these relate to the simulation of humanity, which is incredibly realistic.  At Normal difficulty, you have a fairly good representation of the real world: 65% of people wash their hands and when a new illness is detected a cure is researched at a fairly realistic rate which is dependent upon the severity of your plague.  Brutal and above get substatially harder and reflect a global population that is way more vigilent than that of the real world.
This simulation of the world's human and animal population lies at the heart of Plague Inc's attraction.  I guarantee that you will think a lot more about how you can prevent the spread of illness after you have had your first couple of "successes".  It is really quite scary to see how easily a virus with the right characterists could wipe out the human race.  And make no mistake about the level of realism here; school teachers have used the game to teach children about the spread of illness and the author of the game, James Vaughan, was even invited to the CDC to discuss the simulation.  They are apparently quite interested in using this model as a way to educate the masses.  James himself has stated that he put in quite a lot of research to develop the game.
You have a number of options available to slow the speed of cure development:  At the molecular level, your plague can mutate rapidly and try to outpace the scientists, you can develop a highly complex genetic structure which will require lots of research to understand and you can develop resistance to drugs and different environments / climates.
For a more direct approach you can develop a certain combinations of symptoms and trasmission characteristics.  For example, you can mimic swine flu to mislead scientists or you can develop a combination of highly infectious symptoms, slowing development by forcing researchers to take rigorous precations.  Or you can just simply infuse the virus with a quick kill mechanic or two, like total organ failure for example, to try and dispense with the population before they have the time to combat it.  Careful though, if the disease kills quicker than it infects, it will kill off all of it's hosts before it spreads to the entire population.  There are many more facets to the simulation too which affect both the speed at which your illness spreads, and the speed of the cure development.  There are various combinations of a number of factors, including whether infected countries are rich, poor, arid, humid, hot, cold, rural or urban.
In terms of difficulty, I initially found it quite hard to defeat humanity on normal difficulty.  However, after a few attempts, I developed varous strategies that worked depending on where the disease started out and it eventually became quite easy to win, even without any genetic modificatoin codes, which is why this game scares me so much.  On brutal, I believe you will need the assistance of one or more of the genetic modifications.  It is worth playing for though, as you unlock various "cheat" modes if you manage to win the game on brutal or above for every type of plauge available.
This game really does deserve attention, not just because it is so addictive, but also because it will educate us, and hopefully decrease the chances of this ever actually happening.

It may be short but Fingerbones leaves a strong, emotional impact on you after it's all over. With the game being free, that's enough to warrant a recommendation in my opinion.
There's not much to talk about with the gameplay. It's just WASD (move around) and interact with objects with the click of a mouse. (Not significantly different from Serena, another free short game.) This game is about exploration and reading scattered texts to unravel a dark mystery as well as learning about the former, celler-inhabitant's psyche. The only true game elements are the clues you must gather and decipher to unlock the doors and progress.
No monsters and no cheap jump scares exist to startle you. Fingerbones scares you on a deeper level in both your heart and your head. I personally found it so disturbing because the story felt so human...and so real. And this kind of horror, that which echos with reality, tends to stick with you long after.
With that said, I'm not going to pretend this is a masterpiece. It's only 20 minutes long and perhaps it could've been something grand with more time, development and depth. But as short as it was, I truly think the the developer did a sastisfying job with it.

I shouldn't like this game. This game feels like work. And yet, I adore it. Papers, Please takes the terrible-sounding idea of putting the player in charge of checking passports and identifications of people entering a very controversial country and somehow makes it fun.
Depending on what is happening with the country, you are given new or different tasks, often ones that conflict directly with the previous day's rules, just to keep you on your toes. It's stressful, it looks boring, and yet I found a lot to love in this game. You find yourself rooting for the people coming back each day, desperately trying to gain entry. You want to let that woman through to be with her husband you just let in. And you can! Or you can stick to your job, and crush her dreams with apparent stoicism. It's up to you, and there's intrigue and choices to be had every in-game day. I recommend it highly!

Informally dubbed "Slav Simulator 1984", this is by far one of my more favourite titles.
Like Orwellian themes? This is essentially a must buy. The dark communist eastern vibe that is painted within this game is nothing short of amazing.
What's so unique and great about this game is that it shapes it's gameplay in a unique fashion pertaining to the scenario of the game, as opposed to being a fixed genre that the game's narrative and world has to at least somewhat acommodate. Have you ever seen a border control "simulator" before of a similar ilk? Me neither.
You are the father figure of a poor village family that lives in Artztotzka, a totalitarian country held together with pride and an iron fist. You work as a border controller officer, checking passports of all border entrants. The story itself is very neatly tied together, with a plethora of decisions you can make in the scenarios of the game and consequence that will unfold because of your actions. Everything is moody and gloomy, as you would expect from such a world. It can hold moments of light-heartedness, and it is definately something that should be experienced and appreciated firsthand.

The gameplay itself is fast paced and very thorough. You need to check every meticulous detail too see if documents are in check and valid, corresponding to the entrant correctly. The difficulty curve in the late game gets even harder as more documents that you need to check pile up as the game progresses.
Should you buy this? If you hold an appreciation for a dark, Orwellian world, absolutely. If you enjoy unique, intuitive gameplay that will keep you on your toes and isn't too pretentious, take it into heavy consideration. It can hold a little less ground when it comes to complete replayability (frankly I can't see myself playing this game for TOO long in say, endless modes, as it can get somewhat repetitive, albeit challenging), but it is still very much an amazing game for it's price and you should seriously buy it if you haven't.

While the game has terrible keyboard and mouse controls and feels jaggy and awkward, the game has some strong supports. Those supports being on the foundation of a fantastic story and lore. The supports themselves being Rayne as a character with a great cast and variety of other characters, including other strong, female characters. There are tons of fun weapons, good graphics for the time of release, the gratuitious violence we -- as fans of vampire lore -- come to expect in a video game where you play as a sexy, half-vampire, clad in leather, that kicks *ss with blades on her arms and stilettos. Voiced by Laura Bailey -- someone completely different from the character's personality -- and does an absolutely fantastic job, with a small cast of other VOs that are done quite well. It's not amazing in any particular way, but as vampire games that aren't VTM Bloodlines, it is a really strong game. A villain you grow to hate rather quickly, some small antagonists that are easy to conjure up the rage to kill violently, a group of Nazis not Nazis to kill and feed on. Everything just works.
It's a rather nice touch when your vampire doesn't heal passively, but actually has to feed, and when some enemies need to be weakened it's particularly interesting. Rayne has multiple visions, including one that allows her to spot weak prey to feed upon, or if they need to be damaged for her to hold her grasp, or she will be kicked off. Another thing this game has is some interesting technology that's surprising for its time: You can cut or shoot holes into the various Nazi not Nazi flags you find around, and the blood decals stay until you finish the level. Weapons carry over, and you get upgrades as necessary. There are water physics as well, not that you'd notice considering one of Rayne's vampire traits is that water burns her, stemming from old lore that vampires could not physically cross bodies of water on their own, and instead needed to be caried or some such lore as that.
Anyways, onto the PROS and CONS:
+ Nazis are always fun to kill, even if they're technically not Nazis
+ Vampire lore
+ Fantastic protagonist, anti-hero
+ Great cast of antagonists, particularly the sexy butcher
+ Water and cloth physics, plus tearing the flags, and and jiggle physics too. YEA
+ Has a very serious story but a number of dark joke from Rayne
+ Laura Bailey
+ Soundtrack
+ Gratuitous violence that suits the game's lore
+ Arsenal of weapons to choose from
+ Tons of fun to kill
+ BIG LEVELS
+ Rayne's different visions
+ Feeding to recover health
+ Vampires AND demons
+ That final boss, yo

- Other VOs aren't as strong as Laura Bailey's performance

Writing about the Hunter is a huge crying shame because it could be one of the most enduring success stories, but the developer Expansive Worlds has completely ruined the concept by sheer incompetence and mismanagement.
This is truly an "expansive" game to play, but at first people didn't mind to spend the extra money to get a quality sim. It was still a but like that when I came to the game, in early 2013. But some time after the change from English Emote to an affiliate of Swedish Avalanche Studio (EW or aka "Expensive Worlds") everything had begun going downhill, and today I can say I have zero respect left for this company.
As I wrote, people didnt mind to pay 10$ for a new rifle and scope, or 5$ for a tent or a set of clothing, because it was a premium game. But at some point the developers realized they could also keep charging the premium prices without doing anything. Whatever it is they have been releasing nothing but a bugged mess and garbage ever since ca 2014.
I bet they are just coming to the office and play around a little bit with some 3d models and otherwise enjoy themselves, because no one understands the 10 year old source code any longer, and meanwhile the time of the customers is spent chasing bugs and constantly losing hard earned accomplishments. I have seen pictures where not one of the developers is over 25 or looks like they have any experience at all. I guess they use this as a trainee program for people who come to Avalanche, the good ones are later taken over to work on Just Cause, and the bad ones stay with The Hunter or even bigger garbage like The Hunter Primal, another game they released and sold and apparently never planned to support.
Just some examples how the game will **** you, after years of people making bug reports that no one takes serious any more:
animals that cannot be shot
animals that cannot be picked up when shot
shooting ranges that don't work
server crashes
crashes to desktop
connection bugs where no one can join your multiplayer games for days on end
if you dont use the Steam version but their own launcher, on certain configurations the installation will repeat every Thursday and you have to download 2 GB of game data again
animals that just dissapear within a blink of an eye when they cross a magic 200m "render distance" - in a hunting sim! that's just totally ridiculous, when some of the weapons in the game can easily reach over 1-2 kilometers
Well, what more can I say. I was a fantastic concept, but after I spent hundreds of % I just wonna say: "**** YOU EW"

SC2 Visual Novel is a really entertaining and easy to read VN about a person (male or female, your choice) who moves from the US to Korea with the dreams of becoming a Starcraft 2 champion.  As someone who played Brood Wars and SC2 a ton, I have to say it was filled with feel good moments, even if some of it was a little rushed and cliché.  It is really accurate with the terminology and general demeanor of the Starcraft scene for dedicated players.  I have to admit, I felt really nostalgic reading it -- always a plus.  Because it is relatively short, the story progresses at a totally unrealistic pace, but that’s Ok in my opinion as I assumed that going in, and be considered a plus to some people who want a quick and good story
I am really torn between Positive and Negative, but I chose to go with positive because that is a reflection of the content, however I will explain my negatives.  After reading more reviews, I learned that this game was on Kickstarter
and raised $8,370.
As copied from reviewer “burning.phoenix”, here are some ways it fell short of what it promised
1. Game will be finished in 6 months: Failed. It took 2 years
2. Game will have romance options: Failed. No romance options exist
3. Game will have multiple paths: Failed. It's an absolutely linear story
4. Game will allow you to choose training partners: Failed. There is no choice in the storyline. There are no "stats" to train.
5. Game will allow you to choose which team house to train in: Failed. There is only one team house and it's simply a backdrop to an end-of-game scene
6. Game will allow you to enter online amateur tournaments to test your character's skill: Failed. There are no tournaments in the game.
In the end I chose to give it a positive review, because in my opinion it was worthwhile and enjoyable content.
Pros
-	Easy to read / relatively short (1-3hrs depending on pace)
-	Nostalgic feel
-	Accurate terminology
-	Likeable characters (albeit one-dimensional)
-	Free
Cons
-	Situations are pretty cliché, as are characters
-	Only about 2 choices and both were pretty inconsequential – didn’t care that much because I enjoyed reading it, but some people may want more options
-	Failed to deliver on the Kickstarter end, which is important to me.  Hesitant to give positive review to people who don’t fulfill their end

What if Pikmin had evil goblins instead of cute plant aliens? Overlord is the answer. This is a game where you're the villain - something you don't see too often in gaming - and your goal is to be the overlord (duh). To do that, you must go through series of missions where you gather resources, amass armies of minions and slay the heroes who have since fallen to the seven deadly sins. You can either choose to make the inhabitants of the land your subjects or simply slaughter everyone.
Overall this game is a simpler Pikmin. There is not much to it that Pikmin does not also do, other than obviously the completely different setting and a smaller army of creatures in your command. The Overlord character's animations are... lacking at best and goofy at worse, but then again, why attack yourself when you have an army of obedient minions? It's nothing too spectacular, but it's a fun experience nonetheless.
Remember to murder every sheep you see.

This is one of the classic videogames from the times when vampires were dark and cool, before Twilight came out and made them into a parody fitting a soap opera rather than the horror stories from which they've emerged. Video games like Bloodrayne and Vampire: The Masquerade were made and they were part of a trend for 3rd person action that featured gloomy locations and characters from the realm of the undead.
Bloodrayne is a female protagonist, pretty much a half vampire version of Lara Croft when it comes for when you try to compare the impressions of how the game looks. You get to play a 3rd person action game with a heroine who uses both melee and guns. The story is a bit silly as is the main character's background -  a half human, half vampire red headed lesbian wearing leathers and using blades as a favorite weapon is looking for her father, who's a nazi, to kill him.
When you get through the ridiculous story background, you receive an amazing action-filled dynamic video game, very peculiar in mechanics for an early 2000s game, along with graphics that are very outdated when compared to current standards.
If you haven't played Bloodrayne before, you might be a bit disappointed as it is one of those games that became groundbreaking milestones for the gaming industry. For those who played Bloodrayne soon after it came out, it's a title that might bring out nostalgia.
I highly recommend Bloodrayne.

I have a rule of thumb when it comes to paying for games. I'd like to get an hour of play for each dollar spent. That's not a lot of money for a decent amount of time. That being said, I have paid for 2 years worth of game time, and bought some additional gear, and I still have room to spare for my rule of thumb.
For those compaining about the money, and you intend on actualy playing the game, the money shouldn't be an issue. You pay money for a weapon, and you can use that weapon forever. after your premium runs out, you can still use that bow you bought, or the clothes your wearing, or the dog you bring with you out on hunts. Now, they're even rotating the free animals, so shoot away.
For those of you complaing about it being slow: well.....yes, it is. But honestly, if you went out hunting in real life, do you think you could go running around the woods an not have the prize elk run away from you? After 200 hours, I find myself roaming the map crouched the whole time, and not even thinking about how slow I'm going.
Bottom line is this:
If your looking for a casual, relaxing experience, THAT YOU PLAN ON STAYING WITH, spend the money, and you won't regret it. If it's not something you think you'll play that much, don't. Just remember my rule of thumb, and you can't go wrong,
Cheers,
Xaphian

This game is made by a bunch of assclowns. I have absolutely no idea why it is so highly reviewed everywhere I look.
Lets start with the pros:
-Game world is gorgeous.
-Unlike boring♥♥♥♥♥GTA games, Hong Kong is set in a vibrant exotic city (unless you're from Hong Kong of course) but with the same "lets all be criminals gimmick" (except this time you're an undercover cop)
-Story seems to be great and the game immerses you quite nicely alot of times.
-Driving a fast car at night in HK..particularly if it is raining is something spectacular.
Here are the cons:
-Completely game breaking ♥♥♥♥♥♥ mechanics....particularly when it comes to the fighting. (The thing you will spend 95% of your time doing in Sleeping Dogs). It is the same mechanic that the Batman Arkham and Assasins Creed games employ. But where those games don't fail at the whole "Click button to counter" thing...this game does....by the♥♥♥♥♥♥tons. The problem is simple -> The game simply does not reccognize inputs. Example 1: I click a bunch to regular attack. Some taps some hold for power attacks. I see a guy shine red (which signals I need to counter) so I press the counter button. My guy continues to regular attack...gets hit....then continues to regular attack...and continues to regular attack (I have not even touched my mouse for the past 3 seconds now) and the game literally beeps at me. (It is the a similar noise to the sticky keys noise...but it is not sticky keys and shift was not ONCE pressed). This is an issue that there ARE forum posts about. Most♥♥♥♥♥♥♥will come back with "DERPAHERP ISH THE SCHTICKY KEYZ" (It is not. And may those subhumans die in a glorious cleansing fire) Example 2: "Fix" problem by enabling "double click" to fast under my mouse settings...apparently the game couldnt take that many inputs and literally♥♥♥♥♥♥itself and died. STILL however I notice pressing the counter button at times...and Wei (the character you play) will literally NOT do that...get hit, and THEN (once again...have not even TOUCHED my mouse for the past 3 seconds) will do a "counter stance". That counter stance is what happens when you press counter with zero attacks coming at you. So breaking this down...the game cannot handle inputs...unless at a delay sometimes. I don't know if it is because it's a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ port (and may all consoles and console games burn in hell eternally so the master PC race can finally enjoy some non-crap video games), or if the game is simply coded by ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ monkeys. This is by far the greatest con as it IS game breaking and pervasive throughout the game, and as such the biggest entry in this review.
-Bugs. Lots of them. Lots of buggy bugs. People popping in and out of existance. Npcs getting stuck on nothing (nothing better than having the guy you are chasing get stuck on a corner for literally eternity. I am serious..you can get out of your car and go buy some noodles...he won't move).
-Cars for the most part (at the very least the earlier cars that you will spend a whopping 50% of your game time using) will move as if in tar. They move DAMN fast forward, but their turn rate handles as if the parking break was on the entire time...insert asian drivers joke here. I am also suspicious that this may be a part of the "does not accept input"♥♥♥♥♥♥mechanic of the game.
-Ok I get it...it's a fighting game. It's fun to kung fu around...but I have the same issue with this as I did with the arkham games...I don't know how many times i can pound the same group of differently color clothed bad guys (that boil down to 4 archetypes with like 2-3 models each) before the ENTIRE game becomes just a blur of mediocrity. Why? Why do I have to punch every bad guy in this city in the face. That seems like the worst, most obnoxious approach to solving crime in this city. How would that even work? I'm pretty sure by the time I was done, a whole new generation would have been born, and raised into crimedom. You would think its a good thing to just put nonstop action in a game...but it is the equivalent of saying "oh my god...pineapple is my favorite. I hope I get to eat pineapple for the rest of my life...and only pineapple!" Guess what...you will literally♥♥♥♥♥♥yourself to death if you do that.
-Too many damned fetch quests. Why do I have to increase my health by driving around finding shrines to pray at for 8 goddamned real life hours. It's just needless padding to gameplay time. Instead of doing that...just make a better game.
-Like so many of these games, your actions do not seem to have consequences. You cannot turn a bad guy good or a good guy bad. It doesn't matter who you choose to save...or who you don't. You have no choice. All you can do is punch the same 10 character models in the face until the game ends. And you get to watch a nifty little cutscene movie in between. Not enough of a payoff. Literally every quest boils down to: Go over there and beat that group of 12 guys up.
If I had to guess...this game was thought up by a bunch of really smart people. They knew what gamers would want to experience. They hired artists that did a really bangup job of modeling everything. They hired voice actors that did their job very well and immersed you into the world (with the help of great writers). Then they threw the game to the actual coders...the game mechanics makers...the meat and potatoes of the game...and it turns out they were a bunch of mentally challenged lemurs all ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ themselves and banging the keyboard with their heads untill a game came out. It's a really bad game. I spent 7.50 when it was on sale...and honestly... it's 6 dolars too expensive.
I swear...square enix is such a hit or miss company.

Minimum, the American game company Atari throws its hat back into the ring, after years of silence. And, you know what, they came back in a good way, Minimum is a great game with interesting mechanics, and right now is the best time to get it, it's dirt cheap, I got it back when it still cost twenty, but now, the price won't burn a hole in your wallet, and for a game like this, it's best to get it while it doesn't cost too much.
So let's dive into the gameplay, Minimum, at first, seems like your everyday third person shooter, and it plays very similar. However, the mechanics of the game, are what seperate it from, let's say Gears Of War. The game features a blueprint crafting system, meaning you gather resources (simply by playing and leveling up), to later use to assemble new weapons and armor, there is NO pay to win here (though there are armor and weapon types that you can purchase, but it's not necessarily somehting that gives you more of an edge, it's more for show). Now, these weapons and armor, can be leveled up in game, armor you level up by collecting purple and black armor shards (black shards are also used to create the level one armor set) and you level up your weapon by killing enemies or destroying enemy equipment. Each weapon and armor set has unique properties, such as the samurai helmet, which boosts your melee damage, and the speedy shotgun, which grants the player the gift of a much faster running speed. Armor parts are crafted into 3 sets, legs, torso, and head, and you don't need to craft all of the same type, it's actually best to mix it up. Such as, using olympian legs, which grant you a fster running speed, with a ninja chesplate, which will allow you to recharge your health faster after killing an enemy, and the beserker helmet, which grants you a higher damage rate.
So, next, is the game modes, of which there are 3. Now, I know what you're thinking, only three? That must get old real quick. Actually, no, the game modes are all engrossing, especially the titan game mode. The first game mode is TDM, which is pretty self explanatory, but it's interesting because of all the armor combos, and the weapons are all interesting to use. The next game mode is Horde, which again, is pretty self explanatory, but there is a variety in enemies, ninjas, samurais, dinosaurs, astronauts, knights, this makes for a fun survival game mode. Lastly, the game's most hyped game mode, titan game mode. This game mode, is played by two teams powering up their titans, to destroy defensive walls (titans and walls, hah). This is done by killing creeps. BUt now I know what you're thinking, this is just like a moba isn't it? Well, yes and no, the game mode is like a moba, but it plays like a third person shooter, and you don't need to buy a ton of specific stuff and play a millon tutorials to understand it, it's simplistic, and fun, it's a moba without the complexity, but instead, giant robots that beat the hell out of eachother.
Lastly, even though it's not really the most important part of the game, it's still a part of it, the graphics. The game's minimalistic style (hence the name, minimum) gives the game charm, they aren't the pixelated blocks of Minecraft, but instead smooth blocks, which give the game an interesting look, and I don't think you need a fast pc to run this one, though it still looks great in my opinion.
So, overall, I feel Atari has made a solid comeback here, interesting mechanics, fun game modes, and charming graphics, and it's on sale right now, as a celebration that it's officially off early access (so all of you that are early access wary, put your qualms to rest, this game is no longer in the development stages)
Rating: 9/10

Don't be fooled, despite "leaving" early access, this is still an early access game. The menu shows it as 0.0.5-something, in fact.
Many of the menu options are greyed out, and the tutorials take the time to explain how this is because those features aren't done yet. For example, there's a "schematic" system that has you crafting items mid-match, and it talks about building structures and deployables, but the only thing that you can create is armor. Deployables and structures aren't done yet, apparently.
As if that weren't bad enough, the "titan" mode that the game sells itself on is nothing like what they'd have you believe that it is. My impression, from watching the videos, reading the store page, and looking at screenshots, was that it was somewhat Monday Night Combat-like, with both sides having creeps fighting alongside them, and players defeating the creeps as well as enemy players to power up both themselves and their team's titan, with the objective of ultimately pushing their titan into the enemy's base to win.
This is not the case.
Instead, it's team deathmatch, even down to the small, cramped maps, where little dispensers along the sides spit out "creeps," tiny cube-shaped robots that do absolutely nothing but arbitrarily wander around. These spawn whenever titans are inactive, and you kill them for "titan powerups" to improve your titan, which is never quite explained in any depth. "It makes it stronger," is about as detailed a description as you'll get. Once you collect enough, the titans spawn, and meet in the middle of the map to fight. The winner keeps moving and tries to break walls down until it is destroyed. This goes on, ad infinitum, until both walls on one side are destroyed, or you get frustrated and quit because the match has been going on for half an hour.
Possibly the most egregious offense, however, was having to create an account and log into a third party service upon starting the game, and then to be greeted with a cash shop on the main menu.
Also worth noting is that the game is extremely unstable. Matchmaking frequently does not work, inviting friends to parties can return a number of bizarre and unclear error messages, or leave you in an empty party that doesn't even display yourself as a member, and having the Steam overlay open (especially during loading screens) can cause crashes to desktop and graphical artifacts. Often these errors can only be resolved by completely exiting the game and restarting it. Even the tutorial glitches out if you try to use the menu, forcing you to quit the game rather than being able to return to the tutorial or do anything else.
Currently there are very few maps, even fewer weapons, and tremendous balance issues, which I won't even go into, as they're covered extensively by the other Steam reviews. I would really not recommend purchasing this.

And I can't ever see myself playing it again.

is a story-driven, linear experience that boasts a soulful blend of action-RPG and isometric hack-and-slash.  Beautiful graphics and the alluring, lullaby soundscape create a marvelously intriguing atmosphere that is sure to appeal to nearly any gamer.  The narrative is interesting, but doesn’t explain everything and leaves a lot of room for interpretation.  Together, these aspects create a very entertaining, albeit somewhat short, experience.
Probably the first thing you will notice is how aesthetically pleasing this game is.  If you are someone who enjoys games with graphics that feel like interactive paintings, you will definitely enjoy the art-style in
.  Complementing the beautiful art is the serenading, sing-song soundscape.  These elements are perfectly crafted and blended to create a truly inspired atmosphere.
The game drops you right into the thick of the narrative, and things are slowly explained as you progress through the story.  However, the explanations of things are far from “spoon-fed,” and much of the story is open to interpretation.  The tale unfolds during gameplay for the most part, so things stay lively rather than there being many plot-development inspired lulls in the action.  Be aware that because of this style of narrative gameplay, the game is very linear and it will continue to usher you from one spot to the next with little room for exploration.
The combat and actual gameplay mechanics are an interesting blend of RPG elements, isometric hack-and-slash, and turn-based tactical planning.  You will gain experience as you play and can unlock new abilities which can then be combined in various ways to keep things fresh as you progress through the game.  A dynamic difficulty system,
, is another appealing aspect of the game.  Using these, you can increase the difficulty of the game in various ways (more enemies, stronger enemies, less access to abilities, etc.) which allows you to customize the gameplay to your skill level.
One downside is that the game is rather short.  However, you also can’t even unlock everything in a single playthrough no matter how thorough you are— so the game is clearly designed to be played through at least twice.  That said, I personally would have much preferred if the game was twice as long with the ability to unlock everything in one playthrough.
In short,
is a very well designed game that certainly has a very unique identity.  This underlying novelty combined with the charming atmosphere provides a truly enthralling gameplay experience.  I would say any all-around gamer will enjoy this game, and obviously fans of the genre(s) even more so.  Expect 8 to 15 hours depending on if you want to do everything and play through a second time.

I purchased Overlord and Overlord: Raising Hell together at a discount, so my review is for both the base game and the expansion.
The varied environments and controlling the minions are easily the best parts of Overlord. The graphics are decent and environments look pretty, though character models and animations seem dated. I liked that combat in Overlord isn't solely through the minions, but that your character has upgradeable weapons and spells that allow you to get up close to the action. The music is good while the humor is hit and miss for the most part.
The expansion adds in a hell version of the main quest environments called abysses. After 1 or 2 abyss levels, I felt like this formula grew a little repetitive and tiresome, but some elements of them were humorous and enjoyable. The game gradually gets more challenging near the end, but sometimes I felt that excessive grinding/health bars in bosses made conflicts drawn out artificially, testing patience rather than ingenuity.
Overall, I was pleased with Overlord and its expansion which I found enjoyable. The game is very long for this genre and this compounds the problem of repetitive gameplay, but if you give yourself Overlord in small doses, you'll find a worthwhile experience.
Bottom Line: 7.5/10
If you loved the base game, you won't be dissapointed with this expansion.

is a story-driven, linear experience that boasts a soulful blend of action-RPG and isometric hack-and-slash.  Beautiful graphics and the alluring, lullaby soundscape create a marvelously intriguing atmosphere that is sure to appeal to nearly any gamer.  The narrative is interesting, but doesn’t explain everything and leaves a lot of room for interpretation.  Together, these aspects create a very entertaining, albeit somewhat short, experience.
Probably the first thing you will notice is how aesthetically pleasing this game is.  If you are someone who enjoys games with graphics that feel like interactive paintings, you will definitely enjoy the art-style in
.  Complementing the beautiful art is the serenading, sing-song soundscape.  These elements are perfectly crafted and blended to create a truly inspired atmosphere.
The game drops you right into the thick of the narrative, and things are slowly explained as you progress through the story.  However, the explanations of things are far from “spoon-fed,” and much of the story is open to interpretation.  The tale unfolds during gameplay for the most part, so things stay lively rather than there being many plot-development inspired lulls in the action.  Be aware that because of this style of narrative gameplay, the game is very linear and it will continue to usher you from one spot to the next with little room for exploration.
The combat and actual gameplay mechanics are an interesting blend of RPG elements, isometric hack-and-slash, and turn-based tactical planning.  You will gain experience as you play and can unlock new abilities which can then be combined in various ways to keep things fresh as you progress through the game.  A dynamic difficulty system,
, is another appealing aspect of the game.  Using these, you can increase the difficulty of the game in various ways (more enemies, stronger enemies, less access to abilities, etc.) which allows you to customize the gameplay to your skill level.
One downside is that the game is rather short.  However, you also can’t even unlock everything in a single playthrough no matter how thorough you are— so the game is clearly designed to be played through at least twice.  That said, I personally would have much preferred if the game was twice as long with the ability to unlock everything in one playthrough.
In short,
is a very well designed game that certainly has a very unique identity.  This underlying novelty combined with the charming atmosphere provides a truly enthralling gameplay experience.  I would say any all-around gamer will enjoy this game, and obviously fans of the genre(s) even more so.  Expect 8 to 15 hours depending on if you want to do everything and play through a second time.

Transistor is a masterpiece of visuals, story, and gameplay. It's not very long, but I'm really pleased with the length.

If I have only two options, to recommend or not and nothing between then I'll of course recommend this game. BUT it's not a strong recommendation.
The thing is, Transistor is more of a great piece of art than great piece of game. Which is not a bad thing but ... it's just not that great game.
It's "typical" Supergiant Games product, they have their own recipe and they stick to it. Which is great, it's nice to see a company with such a strong "personality". Because of this you'll get amazing looking game, with a nice soundtrack, interesting approach to story telling, great narrator, action adventure with a RPG elements and some sort of playground where you can try to get the best score while mastering the game mechanics.
But, even though the approach to story telling is novel and "fresh (bleh)" (even if it's the same as in Bastion), the story itself wasn't particularly entertaining for me. I just didn't care about what's happening that much. The world is again post apocalyptic, but now it's not a fantasy, but cyber punk. And it looks gorgeous, it really does. And again, at the end of the game the world changes, both in appearance and "physical laws" as did in Bastion.
The biggest problem for me were the game mechanics. You have 4 skill slots with one upgrade slot for each of them. Via leveling up your character you can gain additional upgrade slots. Also you have one passive slot and can get another three. You'll find a lot of different skills throughout the game and all of them can be used as a primary skill, upgrade or passive. So you have this huge number of possibilities, which would be great. BUT, there is no normal way of finding out the right combination other the trying out all the different combinations via clunky GUI (which looks beautiful but they somehow forget about the user experience) which is no fun at all.
And more often than not, you will want to use some skills designed for traversing the world, or hiding, so you will have two or three skills for attacking. Which results in really repetitive and boring fights. You'll finally find a good combination of skills and the fight will look like this: Run to the enemy, use debuff attack, spam as many damaging attacks(the same one over and over again) as you can, repeat.
The action combat is just no fun. It pains me to say that, because the planing phase is something I wanted to do myself in my dream game. It's a really cool concept, but it's not executed correctly. Well, that's not true. Planing phase is executed correctly, but the selection of skills is all wrong.
I don't think there is anything else what needs to be said. It's a piece of art with repetitive and boring gameplay. The game will take you around 7 hours to complete, 8 with all the challenges. After that you can play the game plus mode.
6.5/10

Plague Inc: Evolved has evolved beyond its roots as a mobile game, and its inspiration, Pandemic 2. Even at $15, it's worth it.
For those who have only played Pandemic 2 and are wondering if this is better or merely an inferior ripoff, it's definitely a more comprehensive, fleshed-out, less frustrating, more entertaining game, even if the premise is very similar. All the skills (from avian transmission to projectile vomiting) are useful, and while some strategies are more prevalent than others, there's no be-all-end-all way to win the game like there is in Pandemic 2. I'm ten hours in and I'm still finding new ways to win against the odds.
The visuals are vastly improved over the mobile iteration, with red transmission dots forming across the world map as countries fall victim to your plague, 3D renders of your plague hovering in the menus, and image feeds of the cities popping up as they descend from normalcy into chaos.
The devs will be adding online multiplayer, Steam Workshop support, and tutorials (amongst other features) in the upcoming weeks/months, but it's more than playable now and I definitely recommend it if you loved Pandemic and want a superior version of it.

This is less a review to state if the game is good or not, and more to let people know what they will be getting themselves involved with if they start playing. So bare that in mind when browsing the reviews. I also submitted more or less this review as a general complaint to Hi-Rez.
I will say the game can be very entertaining with friends, but that fun is put in a chokehold by the issues below.
Graphically it is also very pleasing.
Lets start with how much I have supported your company, and more specifically Smite. For 2.5 years I have invested hours upon hours into your product, 1100+ hours in matches (3000+ matches to be more specific) almost all of which was logged through the Hi-Rez client as a opposed to here on Steam. That's not to mention the countless hours spent in practice, adventure, and event matches that were not tracked. Then how much time it takes to try to read the ins and outs of every god outside of matches, looking up builds and strategies, watching streams to hone my skill for a game that was constantly frustrating. I couldn't seem to quit playing none the less. I've invested roughly 200 dollars into your company, Smite being the primary and Paladins the secondary investment. That is far more than I have ever given a developer for 2 games.
Lets touch base on some of these issues I have faced in Smite, shall we.
1) Server lag/Disconnecting Players: I would have to say 1 in every 10 or so matches I've played some one has disconnected and never returned, or has multiple disconnections through the course of the match. This is a team game. One man down and you are crippled in more ways than 1. There are no bots to take their place like in HoTS.
2) Matchmaking: Well this is the biggest joke you have presented us with, its like there really isn't any sort of matchmaking algorithm. It's so sporadic. Minimum in its concept is an interesting idea : a third person shooter where, during the match, you weapons evolve as you eliminate AI enemies and enemy players while protecting your own Titan and trying to bring down theirs so that you can smash into their base.
Sounds familiar? It is actually as it's a pretty good attempt at mixing the intensity of a shooter with the non-permanent progression found in MOBAs with a few key differences which I'll cover a bit later. It's a game about mobility since you have a melee weapon component which also evolves and armor you can craft that grants benefits while taking away from you at the same time (Want more melee protection? You become more vulnerable to firearm damage, etc.). This makes it so classes are dynamic in that you can mix and match armor parts so you can create a set that fits your playstyle or the current situation in the match.
Weapons usually evolves in 5 tiers, with the lowest tier being your 'basic ' weapon which usually does a pitiful amount of damage. With every player kill, your weapon changes forms and gains new attributes (higher fire rate, more projectiles, additionnal effects, etc.) which makes it perform better. Same with melee weapon, they grow larger, swing faster, are set on fire. Every time you get killed, that progression is lost and you are reset to the weapon's most basic form.
And here lies one of the glaring flaw in the game : momentum. A match's outcome is usually decided in the very first minute due to this system as the first team to have a player to do reasonably well will gain weapons that will make matching up to him nigh impossible. Once that player has a foothold, he can usually blast or hack away any enemy without difficulty and, by doing so, ready his armor faster than any other.
"Well, that's what happens in MOBA, right? You level up, gain better gear, kill more." Yes, except that in MOBAs, you aren't reset to level 1 each time you are killed. Add to that weapon balance which favors either very close range combat or extreme long range and weapons like an assault rifle becomes near useless in favor of people constantly running a shotgun, blades or a sniper rifle with the odd few which end up with launchers that will make any semblance of fair play tossed out of the window. A shotgun or blade user will rush you and can blast or cut you to pieces well before an assault rifle will deal enough damage to take them down and a sniper will likely one-shot you from range while your shots spread all over the place.
"But, your armor stays even when you die." It does, but like stated, it gives and takes at the same time; it only helps your playstyle, doesn't directly make you stronger whereas the weapons themselves are the factors that grants a direct power boost. If your armor does, for example, 40 damage and you are given a 15% boost due to armor, the guy which has the tier 5 variant of the same weapon which does 60 damage will still outclass you.
Don't get me wrong; this might actually appeal to people in that they find players who have tier 5 weapons during a match challenging to fight but the problem lies in that this becomes not a contest of skill past that minute but a constant David versus Goliath scenario where David gets constantly stomped unless Goliath flukes.
Level design-wise, the environnement are quite nicely presented, following the advertised style of having minimal detail. In fact, the style itself is perhaps one of the best point of the game as this simplistic approach makes level interestingly colorful and almost gives the impression of playing in different sport arenas, each with their own theme. This also means the landscape is clear cut and overall easy to navigate while still having enough Z-axis combat for variety.
Another downside is that despite its simplistic looks, the game tend to require rather capable hardware to run. Though it's possible to lessen the load by disabling a few graphic options, it feels at this point that the game might lack a bit on the optimisation side of things. It's surprising how even with an apparent low polycount for the environnement, the game seems to struggle that much to maintain a decent framerate.
Nevertheless, weighting both the pros and cons, I can't recommend this game unless you don't mind the inherent problem of momentum in the game; if that's the case, you might enjoy Minimum but otherwise, you'll find the experience to be frustatingly unfair due to the mechanical gaps created by the evolving weapons.

Sleeping Dogs fills an interesting niche in the sandbox "crime" genre of video games that seems so popular these days. The game mixes elements of a lot of different open world games together, largely successfully, but not without its flaws.
PROS:
-Engaging, deep storyline that lasts quite a while
-Solid gameplay, melee combat is actually pretty fun until the end of the game
-Game length is acceptable, can be longer if you play the DLC and side missions
-Soundtrack is wonderful; sometimes you just want to sit inside of your car for a little while to let a song end before advancing in the game.
-Outfits in game are pretty darn cool, especially with all the DLC included.
-Just generally fun - I had a hard time putting this game down after getting into the main plot.
-Memorable characters
-Atmospheric environment - even if largely inaccurate.
-It feels like a proper "RPG" in that you actually get into the role of the main character
There are also a lot of smaller issues that really detract from the overall experience. None of these are gamebreaking, but in hindsight they were pretty annoying.
CONS:
-Upgrade system makes no sense. You hoard melee move upgrades until the end of the game, only to unlock a powerful god move that makes melee combat irrelevant.
-The concept of "Sandbox" seems lost on the developers; there's nothing to do aside from story missions except run away from the police who are incredibly easy to lose.
-Side missions + DLC are lackluster at best. Especially the "Year of the Snake" DLC. I'd reccomend staying far away from that one if you want to preserve any good memories about the main plot.
-You never need to upgrade your "Face" meter past rank 4 to get the valet; all other elements of that progression tree aren't particularily useful.
-Game ends abruptly. I won't spoil it, but the last mission just sort of ends very suddenly.
-The frequency at which guns become available after the half-way point is immersion breaking.
-*SHOOTS TIRE* *GAME GOES SLOW MOTION* *SHOOTS OTHER TIRE* *GAME GOES IN SLOW MOTION* ad infintum
-AI is easy. Really easy. You pretty much can't die if you're an average skilled player.
-Graphics options are too limiting, especially for a "definitive" edition
-Lots and lots of plot holes
-No real villain except "Generic Hong Kong Triad Boss #40"
-Your best friend dies ;-; RIP
Despite all this, I still have to reccomend the game. Comparing all its flaws and its benefits, Sleeping Dogs is truly a fun game deserving of praise. There are issues, but they are acceptable - no game is free of flaws. I wish I had bought the base game when it was out, as a lot of the DLC made the game a heck of a lot less fun with the ease at which you obtain things. I did a single run through playing only small amounts of the side content, and it took me around 20 hours.

I have JUST finished THE ROOM. If it had been longer, or if there I'd owned any potential sequels, I would not be writing this now. I'd have continued playing sans hesitation. Yet, questions remain.
But there really isn't much to say without compromising the enjoyment of this puzzle game for new players, so I won't try. Simply that the "craftsmanship" of the items was superb, and the "supernatural" storyline eliminated any physics issues to arise in players' minds. The controls were about as simple as one would ever hope to encounter, and more or less intuitive. I only hope the developers had as much fun making this game as I had in playing it.
It didn't take long to realize that EVERYTHING of value toward solving each and every puzzle was immediately available. It was rarely even necessary to look further than a foot or so away, even though that slippery slope might easily have been provided more layered challenges. I dare say without spoiling too much, just about the ONLY outside information needed was a knowledge of the primary colors. Yes, about 3rd grade knowledge. Even a reference to a verse from something as universally accessible as the Christian Bible served a completely different, albeit more interesting and deceptively simple purpose.
Oddly contrary to expectations, the last part of this game became EASIER. The last section was by FAR the simplist, completed in minutes, very nearly without thought or imagination at all. Just by completing simple steps, as though the basic idea had run out of "steam", so to speak. Or perhaps, simply as restful reward for diligent players. Yet there were so many ideas unused. The notes might have been better utilized, much as the drawings began to be (though somewhat nonspecifically.) The surrounding environs perhaps put to some use, if only the walls and ceilings (which were by NO means ignored visually.) Perhaps various lenses. Not to say that anything more was needed in the existing game, but it could have been longer or more complex. Or, dare I say, to make the last section more challenging. In fact, I would not hesitate to say that the last section could have rather been one of the very first, to warm up the player instead of to try to scare some away, as seems to have been done with some of the stronger early challenges. Stronger, but NOT engineering student CRAZY hard. A reasonably curious mind with a minor bent toward lateral thinking is fully adequate. A sense of humor helps greatly. I enjoyed this game VERY much, and only wish I could continue, unabated, indefinately.
The HELP mode. Yes...and No. Admittedly, I used numerous hints, and they added to the enjoyment, though were far from perfect. (Forgive me if I sound as if I criticize my very lifesaver. They certainly added immensely for one not willing to commit to a single game for an extended time, regardless of the high quality of enjoyment.) They often gave hints that were past being of use. Perhaps that was to make a player feel smarter, but for me they often did the opposite by dumbing me down, though sometimes most amusingly.
Perhaps readers of this review can offer an assist. One hint told me I had missed something in the VERY beginning that was needed. Since there is only one SAVE, and that automatic, the only option to explore that hint was to restart the entire game. But despite that drastic step, the "item" was NOT available (confirmed by player generated video), nor was it mentioned again! Any thoughts, readers?
My only remaining question is if I will research a sequel BEFORE or AFTER I post this review....

Overlord: Raising Hell is the official expansion to the 2007 game 'Overlord'. This expansion was released on the PC, Xbox 360 and Playstation 3 all on 2008. The game promises new content for the single player experience by adding additional plot, more levels and new enemy types, new items, and new creative mini-games.
The game takes place several months after the events of Overlord 1 and serves as the prologue to the events that would lead up to Overlord 2. Having finally restored his dominion over the land and exacting revenge on the adventurers, the Overlord now faces a new threat to his rule when portals to another dimension starts opening around his territories. Upon investigating the nearest portal, the Overlord discovers that his 'loyal subjects' are attempting to flee into the portals with no intention of coming back. The Overlord now ventures into one of these dark portals in an attempt to conquer whatever is in the other side and 'persuade' his followers to come back. Little did he know however, that the portals were just the beginning of a much sinister plot by a being far much more powerful than him.
+ The core gameplay of the original title is still intact
+ Good new story that adds several hours to the game time
+ New enemy types are fun to fight
+ Each portal has a story of their own
+ Fun new mini-games and simple but satisfying puzzles
+ New minion equipment
- New items for the overlord sucks (mainly because they have prebuilt stats)
- None of the the original CONS from the main game was ever addressed
- Some of the mini-games gives no clue on how to solve them (gardening puzzle)
- Far more expensive than the Original game, but still requires you to own said original game
- No additional events to increase Corruption / Evil
although it could have used a bit more polishing specially since most of the CONS from the main game was never fixed, this expansion still gives fun additional content in story and in gameplay experience.
All in all, I still liked this expansion thus I give it my
.
If you're interested in this game, try and purchase the
which contains Overlord 1, Overlord: Raising Hell (expansion), and Overlord 2 either on Sale or Full price.
The game is worth the money for fans of the action adventure genre.

TL:DR - Only buy when on sale and only if you really want it because this game has so much forced padding it becomes a chore. It is fun but only for some time.
+ Cute design
+ Fun
+ VS
+ Level maker
- Forced to repeat levels
- Online VS is broken
- No window mode
(Open the game with DXWnd if you want window mode)
MAIN STORY
--------------
The game is fun I will give it that, I enjoyed the levels however I did not like the path choosing.
You are forced to repeat Level 1 every single time you do a set path. There are 4 goals in total so you need to play Level 1 at least 4 times and that is if you don't choose the wrong pathway to a goal you already done! (You cannot view the worldmap so hope you have Google images open)
I don't like this type of "padding", I want to choose my levels willingly not be forced to play stage 1 or 2 of the first two levels in each section just to get to a pathway I not done yet.
Like to point out the stages do not take long to complete but it is still annoying to force us to do the same level so many times.
VS
---
I have only played VS with bots, because Online VS is a bit broken to where you cannot connect to anyones port even if you give them the number the game tells you to give them.
VS is fun though even with the bots. They tend to mess up a lot but when they have 2x point bonus it canbe challenging. I do find it fun that not only do you need to be fast to get points but need to not get tripped up, stepped on or fall into holes otherwise you lose points.
My only issue with it is, when you are too slow or fall off the map you spawn into a bubble above the stage to where bots have done this just before the finish line, popped their bubble and landed on my head, stealing the +1000 points for the final goal, I find this so bloody cheap that if timed correctly anyone can steal it. A few times a bot has fell off the map only for their spawn bubble to put them JUST ahead of the finish line making them automaticly getting the goal points.
I wish I could get Online VS to play, not only for the achievements but I can see Online VS being a lot more fun than facing bots specially against players who know what they are doing. I hope someone finds a solution because that would make the game worth buying IMO.
For now though, do not buy it full price. This is a port of a mobile game and looks to have been abandoned. No updates, they just stuck it on PC and ignored anyone for the missing/broken features. Heck there is such lack of information the forums tend to be empty with posts from last year being at the top. There is not even any guides for the game by other players, showing how unloved the game is.
I really want to give this game a Yes but looking at it from other people's viewpoints, I cannot, they would not enjoy it for long. The achievement rates for this game are this low because people just lose motivation to play the game so quickly.

A mix between a 2.5D platformer and a racing game Angel Express/Tokkyu Tenshi has you running against either the clock or single/multiple adversaries that can be controlled either by the computer or by fellow human players.
The great number of levels,all excellently designed and littered with all kinds of hostile critters that will slow down your progress,the wide array of power ups that can be used to gain the upper hand or undermine your opponents and the sheer fun you can have when running against 3 other characters make this game a true hidden gem among doujin games...and the singleplayer campaign with different endings and branching paths makes for a sweet cherry on top of this cake.

Angel Express would have been a much more fun game had it worked smoothly for me.
To start, Angel Express is a platforming/linear/racing game that you have to race against the clock and do laps or against other players. That is essentially the core of the game. There are powerups, boosts, obstacles, and other things of the sort. Having played Recettear and Chantelise, which this game is related to I think, I appreciated certain aspects of the game, such as the gems to collect. The actual gameplay is relatively fun for some time, especially if you can get some friends to play with you.
Now on to the bad. The game crashed on launch the first time I played it, and it will still crash every now and then. However, that isn't as big a problem since it boots relatively fast. The biggest problem for me was that the game was ultra slow. I don't know why, but it was just slow, laggy, and off timing almost always. I even turned all settings to the lowest, which I should have to do, and it still ran slow. This made playing the game quite a bit less fun. Also relating to the slowness, it'd always take around 1 minute for a level to load or end, and this delay was quite frustrating.
Overall, not a bad game, but buggy for me. If it wasn't buggy, I would give this a recommend, however, it was quite difficult to play for me so I will not for now. If they change that, I will change my review.
Rating: 6.3/10 (higher if they fix the slowness and buggs)
Recommend Price: $1.49 or below

First, let me point out that this game is completely free. Not everyone will realize that right away. Second, you don't need to be familiar with StarCraft 2 at all to enjoy this Visual Novel. A great tutorial is provided at the beginning, giving the necessary knowledge about what SC2 is and how its professional scene works.
I only knew about StarCraft superficially when I began this VN. I knew that it is very big in Korea and the best pro-gamers there are as famous as rockstars, with legions of fans. I knew it was like Warcraft 3, but in a futuristic setting. I've never been a fan of RTS, MOBA or anything of the sort. Yet, I was thoroughly captivated by this VN, because it's not about StarCraft and its technicalities nearly as much as it's about being a pro-gamer in general, with all the difficulties it entails. In fact, one could go as far as to claim this is a visual novel about trying to make it big in any sport, virtual or real-life. They could have substituted SC2 for other sports and the core aspects of the story would remain the same.
The characters are well-written and the dialogue is very witty and funny at times. The character's psychological conflicts and doubts are well portrayed, and their personalities are all very different. Despite this variety, I liked every single major character, which is a difficult thing to pull off and shows how much love and hard work went into designing and writing them.
Overall, this ranks among the best VNs I've read (the best would be Katawa Shoujo, which is also free and also developed by a non-japanese team), and I highly recommend the play even if you've never heard of StarCraft. You're in for a great experience regardless.
It's hard to believe a game of this quality is distributed for free!

Great rerelease with a lot of new graphical improvements over the original. The game's story is still as good as the original.
I played the original game on the PS3 at the time and I will admit, it was one of the "rental" games I looked at since I pick it up and drop it after a while. Since I saw this game on the Humble Bundle store, and I have a decent computer, I decided to give it a second shot.
The overall performance on this game is great. The developers did not disappoint, and I am glad to see a lot of textures and overall visual improvements. The combat feels more fluent than the original, and it feels more responsive for the most part, I wish the driving can be done better though. The driving in the game a bit… how I describe it, "loose" and I mean in a way where it is difficult to chase people down especially in the chase sequences, but still plays fine for the most part.
The story is impressive and still does well to this day. You play as Wei Shen a cop from the United States and moved over to Hong Kong to solve a big case lead by Pendrew. Along the way, Wei meets Jackie, a childhood friend who is also in prison who wanted to join a big triad gang known as; "Sun on Yee.” Wei and Jackie were recruited by the gang leader Winston and begins to commit deeds ordered by Winston. Winston is a leader of the Water Street Boys gang who is also a “Red Pole”, a leader in the ranks of the Sun on Yee. Throughout the story, you will begin to feel connected with the main characters as their backstories and soft sides reveal of how cold hearted they are when doing business, but when personal conversations come to the mix, it gives a feel good connection between Wei, and other characters in the story. I don’t want to give any spoilers for the game, so I will leave it as that.
Now the gameplay resembles what most people refer to it as “Grand Theft Auto: Kung Fu Edition.” The game plays similar to GTA allowing you to roam and is a sandbox game, meaning you can do whatever you like as if you are playing in a Grand Theft Auto game. Unlike having various weapons, most of the time you will be doing fist fights involving marital arts, and you can pick up more skills as you rack up experience points. Experience points can be picked up through the following; side missions, main missions, and favors for people. The more you do, the faster you level up and can pick up more skills as you progress in the game. The skills are needed if you want to make the game easier since the game tends to get more difficult as you progress. As for fighting I will do a breakdown of that.
The fighting is similar to what you have played in the Batman Arkham games. If you have played those games, you will feel right at home. You have a counter, grab, run, and punch button. Using combinations based on the skills you picked up, the game would feel satisfying after pulling the numerous techniques you can learn. Triad, Cop, and Melee are the three categories you gain, and you pick up different points depending on how well the mission you do. Killing others and fighting dirty is what gains you Triad points, but if you do clean driving, (which is not hitting anyone while driving) and disarming are points for Cops. Melee can be picked up however through Jade Statues, and they are scattered throughout the game.
Now I should say, the music in the game is fantastic. It has it’s original composers, but also offers a lot of variety. You have: Classical, Rock, and Hip-Hop to name a few, and it does a great job. Cannot get enough of listening to “Miles to go” performed by Stateless.
Link to the song:
Fantastic music and it fits well in the certain moods especially near the end of the game, and it offers a variety so you will always have something catchy to listen to no matter what mood you are in for. Great job to the composers and developers.
Overall, the game is fantastic and is amazing in its visuals and improved gameplay. And if that does not convince you in buying it, then I shall address that the game has all the DLC content released for the game and it comes in for a cheap price. I recommend picking this game up when it is on a sale so you can get a bang for your buck.

I was suprised to find out out how much this game really lacks when it comes to it's features. Basic stuff like soundeffects such as footsteps is screaming with their lack of pressence. As of writting this it seems they have lately put out a fair amount of updates with a hint about keeping the pace up. I hope that is so because this came have a huge potential if it gets the attention and love it needs.
Right now you are tossed into a minimalistic world with customizable loadouts where you run around fighting, gaining rewards and as the match progresses you use the rewards to craft armour. Each kill drops a powerup that strenthens your weapon up to five times. All lost each time you die though. At the same time you use 2 different pickups to create on the spot new armourpieces and upgrade them.
The weapons have two firemodes. Depending on which weapon secondary might not even be an attack. There's a shotgun that has a highjump skill as secondary that is excellent to get out of fights or evade enemies. Meleewise you get a sword from the start that has a dash on secondary and as it you power it up it goes from one single boring plain stick to a dualwielding glorious flailing wall of death. All that seems really fun and proves the developer aren't afraid to break the classic mold of run'n gun shooters so we might see some awesome stuff in the future.
Besides primary and secondary weapons you also have a slot for a device in the loadout. Here you equip grenades, turrets and mines. Not to much options yet but so far all I've tried have been useful and served it purpose.
When it comes to gamemodes there are as of writting this three to pick from.
-Team deathmatch, just as basic as it sounds really.
-Horde mode, coop battling against waves of bots which seems a bit unbalanced and strange as bots can spawn on top of you. Clearly far from done.
-Lastly we have the Titanmode. this is the gamemode held up as whats it all about. Two teams fighting against eachother over creeps to strengthen their titans and have it push into enemy base for victory.
With all this said and from what I can see in the interface I really hope this game can get it together and accomplish its goals. But I wouldn't recommend it as a must buy for anyone. Only those interested in seeing a game evolve should really buy it as it is now. Is it fun? Yes, but it is so incomplete and lacking in features that it really is for curiousity and willing to support you should buy the game. Not to actually play it. Better not burn out on it now and get to have all the funs later when it is more fun to be had.

I'll start by saying that if you're a fan of Monty Python, this is for you.
I am sadly late to the party on this, but.. This game honestly stands out from most of my library just in the way of it spewing out the best form of crude humor, where fart jokes actually are well done, quite a rare find in anything, especially with how they seem to be thrown around now-a-days because of a target audience they seem to want to attract but it's not pulled off in any form of decent or amusing way, it's just there for the sake of being there. Now that being said on with my ramblings.
It steps out of the normal kind of game and steps into a comic like take on historic figures such as Plato and Aristotle, Napoleon, Leonardo Da Vinci etc, made into a tower defense video game, developed by the ACE Team. You are Sisyphus, a deceased character that was doomed to eternally rolling a cursed boulder up a hill only to have it roll back down before it can reach the top (Yes, I brushed up on my history for this), you suddenly get the bright idea to break out of your hell to then be the one rolling boulders over historical figures and amusingly squish them before they can squish you.. Which I must add, is more than satisfying. Especially with the little girly squeal.
The multiplayer is also an amusing little add with being able to squish friends or just random people in other lobbies. It's not only amusing but quite challenging due of different play styles which also goes through in story mode as each historical figure has different tactics and items they use more of. Time trials are a good way to get familiar with maps to get the fastest time around each track finally we come to skeeball, just when you thought this game couldn't get any better, they add in carnival games to the mix. What more needs to be said.
Rock of Ages is definitely one of the most unusual games I have played but one of the best. Sadly a bit short and lacking in the levels department in my opinion as I could have gone on for at least another 10 or so levels, but with solely that whinge aside, it is a perfect balance of amusing and challenging but not punishing and tedious.. I have not come across a game like that for quite some time. Honestly, this game is glorious and I would recommend it to anyone.

Note: This review is entirely written for an SMNC audience. If you are not familiar with SMNC, you should probably ignore this review :)
This game will not scratch your SMNC itch. There are no classes, just loadouts. You can switch loadouts during a match. There are currently two game modes, and it switches back and forth between them: team deathmatch and Titan. It is the Titan mode that is most like SMNC. In Titan mode there are two giant robots that head from home to enemy base. When they meet, they fight each other. There are also barriers that come up and in the base there are some feeble defenses against titans. Once the Titan defeats the defenses in the base the game is over. So, it is sorta like SMNC... but with a single (albiet giant) 'bot.
Teams are 5v5 and you can leave/join whenever.
Death comes quickly, sort of like MNC or Turbo. You can build yourself and weapons up during the game with pickups, when you respawn you start that process over.
Verdict: it may be a good game, but it is not an SMNC replacement. Perhaps 10-20% of SMNC gameplay elements.
Outside of SMNC: I was not pulled in by the game on its own merits. There are plenty of other similar games out there, not sure how this is all that different.
